headline: 26.7% of Pakistan’s population affected by diabetes
description: Diabetes is rapidly spreading in Pakistan, with 26.7 percent of the population, or around 33 million people, affected by the disease, including 11 percent
author: NNI
article_text:
Diabetes is rapidly spreading in Pakistan, with 26.7 percent of the population, or around 33 million people, affected by the disease, including 11 percent young people, according to the International Diabetes Federation.

Pakistan is currently ranked as the world's third-largest country in terms of diabetes prevalence, raising concerns among health experts about the growing burden of the disease.

Medical experts warn that uncontrolled diabetes can lead to serious health complications, including heart attacks, kidney failure, loss of eyesight and, in severe cases, amputation of body parts.

They said obesity, smoking, lack of physical activity and unhealthy eating habits were among the major risk factors contributing to the disease.

Experts stressed that diabetes could be managed through regular exercise, a balanced diet, avoiding excessive fatty foods and sweets, taking prescribed medication and adopting healthier lifestyle habits.

They added that timely diagnosis and proper management could help patients prevent complications and maintain a healthy life.

World Diabetes Day will be observed on November 14 in Pakistan and across the world to raise awareness about diabetes, its symptoms, complications and preventive measures.

Health departments and social organisations are expected to organise awareness seminars, walks and other activities across the country to educate people about the disease and encourage preventive healthcare.

headline: Maryam vows strict action against ministers involved in corruption
description: Punjab CM Maryam Nawaz vows strict action against ministers involved in corruption or bribery during a scholarship and laptop distribution ceremony in Jhelum.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif on Tuesday warned that strict action would be taken against any provincial minister found involved in corruption or bribery, declaring that such practices would not be tolerated in her government.

Addressing a scholarship and laptop distribution ceremony in Jhelum, the chief minister said she would take action against any minister if credible information emerged regarding their involvement in corrupt practices.

"Let me know if any minister has committed corruption or taken a bribe; I will not spare them," she said.

Maryam challenged her critics to identify even a single rupee of corruption in development projects worth thousands of billions of rupees undertaken by the provincial government.

She claimed that Punjab was the only province where the chief minister regularly exposed cases of corruption.

Questioning allegations levelled against her administration, Maryam asked whether corruption-related issues did not exist in Sindh, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Referring to the political situation ahead of the next elections, the chief minister said criticism of her government had intensified as the polls approached.

She alleged that certain political figures were attempting to secure their positions for the future by targeting the provincial administration.

Highlighting the Punjab government's initiatives for young people, Maryam said the province's youth were now holding laptops instead of petrol bombs and stones.

She described talented students as her heroes and emphasised that investing in education was essential to securing the country's future.

headline: Ahsan Iqbal urges doctors to prioritise humanity and professional ethics
description: Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Professor Ahsan Iqbal on Tuesday urged newly graduated doctors to prioritise humanity,
author: APP
article_text:
Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Professor Ahsan Iqbal on Tuesday urged newly graduated doctors to prioritise humanity, compassion and professional ethics while adopting modern medical technologies to improve healthcare services in Pakistan.

Addressing the 59th convocation ceremony of the College of Physicians and Surgeons Pakistan (CPSP) in Lahore, he congratulated the graduating doctors, their families and teachers, acknowledging their dedication, sacrifices and hard work.

He said a medical degree was not merely an academic qualification but a significant responsibility to serve humanity with honesty, empathy and professional commitment.

The minister emphasised that doctors must treat patients with dignity, respect and compassion, particularly those facing financial difficulties. He said professional integrity, fair judgment and a caring attitude were essential to building patients' trust.

Referring to Islamic teachings, Ahsan Iqbal said saving one human life was equivalent to saving all humanity, stressing the importance of honesty, compassion and trustworthiness in public service.

Highlighting developments in the healthcare sector, he said artificial intelligence, genomics, robotic surgery, digital pathology and telemedicine were transforming medical practices worldwide.

He encouraged young doctors to pursue lifelong learning, regularly study medical research and collaborate with engineers and computer scientists to keep pace with technological advancements.

Recalling the importance of medical ethics, he cited the example of two Persian doctors who diagnosed Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah with a fatal lung disease in 1946 but maintained confidentiality to protect his historic mission.

The minister also urged professionals to counter fake news, avoid social polarisation and contribute positively to national development.

He said the generation of doctors graduating today had an important role in shaping Pakistan's future as the country moves towards its centenary in 2047, calling on them to combine professional excellence with a strong commitment to public service.

The ceremony was attended by CPSP President Professor Muhammad Shoaib Shafi, President of the Royal College of Physicians of Edinburgh Professor Mark Strachan and President of the Bangladesh College of Physicians and Surgeons Council Professor Moudud Hossain Alamgir, among other distinguished guests.

headline: Pakistan launches training programme for 35 Bangladeshi civil servants
description: Pakistan has launched a two-week Executive Development Programme for 35 senior Bangladeshi civil servants under the Pakistan-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor to
author: NNI
article_text:
Pakistan has launched a two-week Executive Development Programme for 35 senior Bangladeshi civil servants under the Pakistan-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor to strengthen professional capacity and promote institutional cooperation between the two countries.

The programme commenced on November 9 at the Executive Development Institute (EDI) of the National School of Public Policy (NSPP) in Lahore and will conclude on November 23. It is sponsored by the Higher Education Commission (HEC).

The Bangladeshi delegation, headed by High Commissioner Md. Iqbal Hussain Khan, will participate in institutional study tours across Lahore, Islamabad and Karachi.

The visits include the Prime Minister's Office, National Assembly, HEC, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Commerce, Ministry of Information Technology, NADRA, State Bank of Pakistan, Karachi Port Trust and other key public-sector institutions.

Addressing the inaugural session, EDI Dean Dr. Naveed Elahi welcomed the delegation and said the programme had been designed to enhance professional skills through engagement with major national institutions.

NSPP Rector Muhammad Sualeh Ahmad Faruqui expressed confidence that the initiative would provide valuable learning opportunities, promote professional development and strengthen friendship and cooperation between Pakistan and Bangladesh.

Bangladesh High Commissioner Md. Iqbal Hussain Khan said bilateral relations were improving and highlighted opportunities for cooperation in defence, leadership and public policy.

Chief Guest Malik M. Ahmed Khan, Acting Governor Punjab and Speaker of the Punjab Assembly, highlighted the importance of effective governance, legislative practices and public service focused on public welfare.

A question-and-answer session also provided participants an opportunity to discuss and compare governance and legislative practices in both countries.

The opening day coincided with Iqbal Day celebrations, with Justice (retd) Nasira Iqbal joining the cake-cutting ceremony and welcoming the visiting delegation.

The programme also included visits to Sadqain Gallery and an introduction to NSPP, the National Institute of Public Policy (NIPP) and EDI.

headline: UN Women says over 1.5B women, girls live in climate hotspots worldwide
description: More than 1.5 billion women and girls worldwide, over one-third of the total, live in areas where climate hazards intersect with economic insecurity and gender
author: Anadolu
article_text:
More than 1.5 billion women and girls worldwide, over one-third of the total, live in areas where climate hazards intersect with economic insecurity and gender inequality, UN Women warned Tuesday.

In a new fact sheet, the agency said 73% of countries acknowledge gender-specific climate risks in their national climate plans, but only slightly more than one-third address them comprehensively.

Under the worst-case scenario, climate change could push an additional 141 million women and girls into extreme poverty.

Data from 24 countries also showed that a 1C temperature increase was associated with women losing 34% more of their total income than men did.

Across 14 countries, prolonged extreme drought was linked to 21% higher odds of sexual violence against adolescent girls and young women.

"Across the world, women are already leading the fight for a better future," UN Women Executive Director Sima Bahous said, calling for equal rights, resources and decision-making power.

At COP31, the agency urged governments to expand gender-responsive climate financing and protect women's rights.

headline: Barrister Salman Safdar warns of serious health risks to Imran Khan
description: Barrister Salman Safdar, lawyer for Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan, on Tuesday warned that the former prime minister could face a brain
author: NNI
article_text:
Barrister Salman Safdar, lawyer for Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan, on Tuesday warned that the former prime minister could face a brain haemorrhage or heart attack without timely medical treatment.

Speaking to journalists outside the court, Safdar said he had recently met Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, at the jail and briefed the court on their health conditions.

He said the court had been requested to immediately shift both prisoners to hospital and constitute an independent medical board to examine them.

According to Safdar, Imran Khan's blood pressure had reached 192 on November 1, raising concerns about the risk of serious medical complications if proper treatment was not provided.

He also expressed concern over Bushra Bibi's deteriorating eyesight, saying her next surgery was scheduled for November 15. However, she had refused to undergo another procedure at the same hospital or under the supervision of her previous doctors.

The lawyer questioned the decision to send her back to jail immediately after her first surgery while her eyes were still bandaged and called for detailed reports of her previous procedures.

On legal matters, Safdar said Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi had directed their legal team to cooperate fully with the court proceedings in the Al-Qadir Trust case.

He said the judge had agreed to hear the main appeals together, while the court would decide whether to take up the National Accountability Bureau appeals or the Al-Qadir Trust case first.

Safdar said Imran Khan wanted all legal matters to be resolved through the courts and expressed hope of meeting the PTI founder again along with Barrister Latif Khosa.

headline: World Science Day 2026 celebrated in Islamabad with focus on science diplomacy
description: World Science Day for Peace and Development 2026 was celebrated in Islamabad on Tuesday under the theme “Common Ground Through Science Diplomacy”, highlighting
author: Web Desk
article_text:
World Science Day for Peace and Development 2026 was celebrated in Islamabad on Tuesday under the theme “Common Ground Through Science Diplomacy”, highlighting the role of scientific cooperation in promoting peace, international dialogue and sustainable development.

The national event was organised by the Pakistan Science Foundation (PSF) in collaboration with UNESCO, the Ministry of Science and Technology, Economic Cooperation Organization Science Foundation (ECOSF), COMSATS and Pakistan Academy of Sciences (PAS) at the Ministry of Science and Technology auditorium.

The event was held under the International Decade of Sciences for Sustainable Development (2024–2033), focusing on scientific collaboration and evidence-based policymaking to address global challenges.

The inaugural session featured welcome remarks by PSF Chairman Dr. Muhammad Akmal, while Additional Secretary Ministry of Science and Technology Ali Bahadur Qazi also addressed the gathering. Federal Minister for Science and Technology Khalid Hussain Magsi distributed cash prizes among students who won medals in international competitions.

A high-level round-table discussion titled “Navigating Shared Challenges Through Science Diplomacy” brought together diplomats, scientists, policymakers and international representatives to discuss the role of science in strengthening trust and cooperation among nations.

The discussion, moderated by Pakistan Academy of Sciences Secretary General Dr. Aslam Baig, covered climate change, water security, public health, emerging technologies and disaster risk reduction.

Another panel discussion, titled “Inclusive Science for Cooperation and Sustainable Development”, highlighted women's participation and leadership in scientific research and innovation.

The panelists stressed the need to expand opportunities for women scientists, strengthen mentorship programmes, promote gender equality in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education, and increase women's representation in scientific leadership.

The event also featured a prize distribution ceremony recognising Pakistani students for their achievements in international scientific activities.

In his concluding remarks, PSF Member Science Dr. Mirza Habib Ali emphasised strengthening national and international scientific partnerships, promoting science diplomacy and encouraging youth participation in scientific activities.

The celebration reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to promoting scientific knowledge, international cooperation and science-based solutions for a peaceful and sustainable future.

headline: Gold prices fall by Rs1,500 per tola
description: Gold prices witnessed a decline in the domestic market on Tuesday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola falling by Rs1,500 to Rs430,836, according to rates
author: APP
article_text: Gold prices witnessed a decline in the domestic market on Tuesday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola falling by Rs1,500 to Rs430,836, according to rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association. Similarly, the price of 10 grams of 24-karat gold decreased by Rs1,286 to Rs369,372, while the price of 10 grams of 22-karat gold declined by Rs1,179 to Rs338,603. In the international market, the price of gold decreased by $15 to $4,083 per ounce, the association reported. Meanwhile, the price of silver per tola remained unchanged at Rs5,723, while the price of 10 grams of silver also stayed stable at Rs4,906. The price of silver in the international market remained unchanged at $52.45 per ounce, the association added.

headline: Cricket Australia rules out reopening 2018 ball-tampering investigation
description: Cricket Australia has rejected calls to revisit the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying it sees no compelling reason to reopen the investigation into the
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Cricket Australia has rejected calls to revisit the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, saying it sees no compelling reason to reopen the investigation into the controversy.

Chief Executive Todd Greenberg said the board believed there was little value in revisiting past events and wanted to move forward rather than reopen the matter.

He reiterated that Cricket Australia's position remained unchanged and added that national team captain Pat Cummins would address the issue soon.

The decision follows fresh comments by former Australian cricketer Usman Khawaja, who recently made further revelations about the scandal while defending his own position.

In response to Khawaja's remarks, Cricket Australia issued a statement reaffirming its confidence in the investigation previously conducted into the incident.

headline: WHO trains doctors to treat children with acute malnutrition
description: The World Health Organization (WHO), in collaboration with the Sindh Health Department and with support from the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) has
author: APP
article_text:
The World Health Organization (WHO), in collaboration with the Sindh Health Department and with support from the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) has trained doctors on recommended protocols for providing life-saving treatment to children suffering from severe acute malnutrition with medical complications.

The training aims to strengthen the capacity of healthcare professionals to manage complicated cases of severe acute malnutrition at WHO-supported Nutrition Stabilization Centres.

The initiative focuses on improving the quality of care and ensuring timely, appropriate treatment for vulnerable children facing life-threatening nutritional complications.

Through this collaboration, WHO, the Sindh Health Department, and BISP are working to strengthen nutrition services and improve access to essential healthcare for children in need.

headline: Sri Lanka reach 114-3 after Pakistan set 434-run target in Rawalpindi Test
description: Sri Lanka lost three wickets while reaching 114 runs in their second innings on the second day of the opening Test against Pakistan in Rawalpindi, leaving them
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Sri Lanka lost three wickets while reaching 114 runs in their second innings on the second day of the opening Test against Pakistan in Rawalpindi, leaving them with a challenging target of 434 runs.

Bad light brought an early end to the day's proceedings, with Kamindu Mendis unbeaten on 40 and Dhananjaya de Silva batting on 22. Dinesh Chandimal managed just one run before being dismissed, while Pasindu Sooriyabandara departed without opening his account.

Earlier, Pakistan declared their first innings at 434-9, building a substantial lead after resuming the day at 281-5.

Saud Shakeel led the batting effort with 93 runs before falling shortly after lunch. Arafat Minhas added 52, while Ghazi Ghori contributed 48. Razaullah scored 10 before captain Babar Azam called an end to the innings.

Among the other contributors, debutant Tayyab Arif scored 57, Muhammad Taha made 51, and Babar Azam added 50. Azaan Awais and Salman Ali Agha chipped in with 30 and 16 runs, respectively.

For Sri Lanka, Fernando and Madushanka claimed three wickets each, while Lahiru Kumara, Milan Rathnayake and Sonal took one wicket apiece.

First day recap

Pakistan ended the opening day at 281-5, with Saud Shakeel on 57 and Ghazi Ghori on seven when play was halted due to poor light after 67.2 overs.

Tayyab Arif and Muhammad Taha had both scored half-centuries, making 57 and 51 runs, respectively. Babar Azam contributed 50, while Azaan Awais and Salman Ali Agha scored 30 and 16.

Sri Lanka won the toss and elected to field in the Rawalpindi Test.

headline: DPM Dar for closer coordination to advance national economic priorities
description: Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, on Tuesday, emphasised closer coordination with relevant ministries to advance national
author: APP
article_text:
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, on Tuesday, emphasised closer coordination with relevant ministries to advance national economic priorities.

The DPM/FM chaired a meeting to review Pakistan’s economic diplomacy and efforts to support export promotion, the Foreign Office Spokesperson said in a press release.

The meeting was attended by senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Discussions focused on the role of Pakistan’s missions abroad in strengthening engagement with partner countries, showcasing Pakistan’s export potential and facilitating business linkages.

Dar also directed all concerned to ensure sustained follow-up to translate diplomatic outreach into tangible economic gains.

headline: Pakistan complete unbeaten group-stage campaign with 101-run win over Nepal in U-19 Asia Cup
description: Pakistan maintained their winning streak in the Under-19 Asia Cup, registering a 101-run victory over Nepal to finish the group stage with three wins from as
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan maintained their winning streak in the Under-19 Asia Cup, registering a 101-run victory over Nepal to finish the group stage with three wins from as many matches.

After being put in to bat in Oman, Pakistan posted 275-7 in their allotted 50 overs, setting Nepal a target of 276 runs.

Ahmed Hussain anchored the innings with 89 runs, while captain Farhan Yousaf provided strong support with a contribution of 74. Hasnain Abbas added 25, and Jahangir Bilal scored 22 to help Pakistan reach a competitive total.

Nepal failed to build a sustained response against Pakistan's bowling attack and were dismissed for 174 runs, falling 101 runs short of the target.

Ahmed Hussain continued his impressive display with the ball, taking four wickets to cap a memorable all-round performance. Muhammad Siaam and Muhammad Huzaifa claimed two wickets apiece.

The result gave Pakistan a clean sweep of their three group-stage fixtures, keeping them unbeaten and boosting their position heading into the next phase of the tournament.

headline: NA panel seeks plan to ensure payment of media workers’ salaries within 15 days
description: The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday expressed serious concern over delays in payment of salaries to media
author: APP
article_text:
The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday expressed serious concern over delays in payment of salaries to media workers and increasing layoffs by media organisations, directing the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to submit a comprehensive plan to address the issue within 15 days. The committee, chaired by MNA Pullain Baloch at Parliament House, observed that withholding salaries and terminating employees without prior notice or fulfilment of contractual obligations were serious issues affecting the livelihoods and welfare of media professionals.

The committee asked the ministry to develop a clear strategy to ensure payment of outstanding salaries and protect the rights of media workers. The secretary of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting informed the committee that the government was regularly releasing payments against outstanding dues to media organisations, but expressed concern that these organisations were not fulfilling their obligations towards employees. He said the ministry had sought details of unpaid salaries from the representative organisation of media workers in compliance with the committee’s earlier directions, but the required information had not yet been provided. The committee directed the ministry to engage with media organisations and representative bodies of journalists and other media workers, obtain details of pending salaries and present a concrete plan of action within the stipulated 15-day period. The committee also discussed the reported assault on the chairman of the Press Council of Pakistan but deferred consideration of the matter pending the outcome of judicial proceedings and an inquiry ordered by the ministry. The committee was informed that the matter was currently before the court and that the ministry had taken notice of the allegations and constituted an inquiry committee, which had been directed to submit its report within 60 days. It was observed that further deliberations at this stage could overlap with ongoing judicial and inquiry proceedings or potentially prejudice the matter. The committee was also briefed on the functioning and performance of the Central Board of Film Censors. Officials informed the meeting that recent amendments to the Motion Picture Ordinance, 1979, would bring changes to the board’s nomenclature and composition, aimed at improving its functioning. The committee expressed concern over the absence of a unified central mechanism for film certification, noting that separate certification arrangements in the provinces could result in inconsistencies in standards and regulatory practices. It stressed the need for greater coordination between federal and provincial authorities to develop a harmonised film certification framework while respecting their respective constitutional jurisdictions. The committee emphasised that the issue should be examined in consultation with all relevant stakeholders to ensure consistency in film certification across the country. MNAs Kiran Imran Dar, Kiran Haider, Shaheen, Salahuddin Junejo, Mehtab Akbar Rashdi and Rana Ansar attended the meeting, along with the secretary of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the chairperson of PEMRA and other senior officials.

headline: Ambassador Tirmizi partakes round table on people-to-people diplomacy in Kaza
description: Ambassador to the Russian Federation, Faisal Niaz Tirmizi, on Tuesday took part in the roundtable “The Eastern Fair as a Model of People-to-People Diplomacy”
author: APP
article_text: Ambassador to the Russian Federation, Faisal Niaz Tirmizi, on Tuesday took part in the roundtable “The Eastern Fair as a Model of People-to-People Diplomacy” here, which brought together representatives of cultural institutions, universities, the creative industries and organisations working on international cooperation. On the occasion, the ambassador said the “Russia–East” Festival shows how crafts, food, music and shared traditions can bring people together, a Ministry of Foreign Affairs news release said. He drew a parallel between Tatarstan and Pakistan: both are home to many faiths, languages and traditions, both have a rich Islamic heritage, and both serve as meeting points between regions. Pakistan lies at the crossroads of South, Central and West Asia, while Tatarstan links Europe and Asia. Kazan, with its mosque and cathedral standing side by side in the Kremlin, reflects the same spirit of coexistence that Pakistanis value. He said Pakistan is ready to work more closely with Russia in culture, education, youth exchanges and museums. The Ambassador also announced that at the next Festival, the Embassy of Pakistan will ensure a strong presence of Pakistani culture and arts. The participants agreed that culture, education, cinema and scientific exchange are among the best ways to build understanding between Russia and the Islamic world. The roundtable participants included Director of the Rashit Vagapov Tatar Cultural Foundation, Rifat Fattakhov; Director General of the Centre for the Development of Creative Industries of Tatarstan, Ranko Tepavchevich; Chairperson of the Academy of Youth Diplomacy and Creative Communications, Dilbar Sadykova; Leonid Isaev of HSE University; Executive Director of the “Altyn Minbar” Film Festival, Milyausha Aituganova; Director General of the National Museum of Tatarstan, Airat Faizrakhmanov; and Elmira Sadykova of the Foundation for Promoting Strategic Dialogue and Partnership.

Two Lahore-based companies, Marksol and ZAPTA Technologies, have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to collaborate on software development, artificial intelligence tools, and digital marketing projects for businesses in Pakistan.

The agreement was signed in Lahore by Marksol Founder and CEO Hasan Farid Joyia and ZAPTA Technologies representative Ateeq Ur Rehman. Nasir Ali Joyia of ZAPTA Technologies was also present at the ceremony.

The partnership will cover joint projects requiring both technical and marketing services. The companies also plan to exchange client referrals, use AI-powered tools to review e-commerce websites and organise training sessions on online business operations and digital skills.

Speaking at the signing ceremony, Hasan Farid Joyia said businesses could lose potential online sales when website management, advertising and performance data were dealt with separately. He said cooperation between technology firms and marketing agencies could help local businesses coordinate these functions and assess the commercial outcomes of their advertising campaigns.

He added that the agreement would be particularly relevant to small and medium-sized businesses transitioning to online sales through platforms such as Shopify and Instagram.

ZAPTA Technologies, established in 2020, develops web and mobile applications and software products and has a workforce of around 100 people. Marksol began operations in 2024 and works in e-commerce website development, digital advertising, content creation, search engine optimisation and public relations.

headline: PM Shehbaz calls for building economically dominant, energy-independent, environmentally resilient Pakistan
description: Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called for building an economically dominant, energy-independent and environmentally resilient Pakistan,
author: APP
article_text:
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called for building an economically dominant, energy-independent and environmentally resilient Pakistan, declaring that the country will harness its resources, technology and human capital to secure a prosperous future.

Addressing the dome placement ceremony of the Chashma-5 Nuclear Power Plant (C-5) here, the prime minister described the milestone as a reflection of Pakistan’s determination to shape its own future through hard work, technological advancement and strategic partnerships.

Prime Minister Shehbaz, while emphasising the importance of energy security, said Chashma-5 represented much more than steel and concrete—rather, it was a promise of clean, reliable, and affordable electricity that would strengthen the national economy and improve people’s lives.

He said that nuclear power would reduce Pakistan’s dependence on imported fuels and international price fluctuations while ensuring a stable electricity supply for industries, hospitals, educational institutions and households.

“Pakistan will not wait for anyone, but will build its own future through its hard work and untiring efforts,” the prime minister recalled, referring to his commitment at the project’s groundbreaking ceremony in July 2023.

He noted with satisfaction that the dome had been installed less than three and a half years after the groundbreaking, ahead of schedule, and expressed confidence that the project would also be commissioned earlier than planned.

The prime minister stressed that Pakistan, as a climate-vulnerable country, had a particular responsibility to pursue energy solutions that simultaneously advance economic development and protect the environment.

Highlighting the strategic importance of national security for economic progress, he said no country could build a prosperous future without first safeguarding its present.

He acknowledged the role of the armed forces under the leadership of Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir in ensuring security and stability.

Referring to the country’s experience during Marka-e-Haq, the prime minister praised the professionalism, courage and resolve of the armed forces, saying a secure environment was essential for attracting investment, reviving the economy and accelerating socioeconomic development.

He also appreciated Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir’s support for the government’s economic revival and development initiatives.

Underscoring Pakistan-China strategic cooperation, Prime Minister Shehbaz described Chashma-5 as another enduring symbol of the two countries’ all-weather friendship and their shared commitment to economic progress.

He said the project marked the seventh nuclear power unit China had helped Pakistan construct, reflecting the consistency and strength of bilateral cooperation across challenging times.

The prime minister conveyed his gratitude to Chinese President Xi Jinping, the Chinese government and the China National Nuclear Corporation for their continued support, acknowledging the contributions of Chinese engineers and their Pakistani counterparts.

He further stated that the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) would open new economic opportunities, strengthen strategic ties and contribute to a brighter future for both countries.

The prime minister, while congratulating the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC), China Atomic Energy Authority, China National Nuclear Corporation, contractors, engineers, financial institutions and other stakeholders, also acknowledged the people of Mianwali for hosting the landmark project.

Concluding his address, Prime Minister Shehbaz reaffirmed his government’s commitment to building a Pakistan that is economically stronger, energy-secure and environmentally responsible, expressing hope that Chashma-5 would remain a lasting symbol of Pakistan-China friendship and shared aspirations for peace, stability and prosperity.

Earlier, PAEC Chairman highlighted nuclear energy’s growing contribution to Pakistan’s electricity mix and national energy security. He said the country’s nuclear power plants were safely and efficiently generating 3,530 megawatts of electricity, helping avoid approximately 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually.

Nuclear energy currently accounts for around 16.6 per cent of Pakistan’s electricity generation despite representing only 8.6 per cent of installed power capacity. Its contribution rises to approximately 26 per cent during winter.

The Chashma-5 project will have a generation capacity of 1,200 megawatts and is expected to begin electricity production in September 2030.

The ceremony was attended by Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, senior Pakistani officials, Chinese representatives, and officials from relevant organisations.

headline: Rain, thunderstorms expected in upper parts of country from Nov 11-14: PMD
description: The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast rain accompanied by wind and thunderstorms, with snowfall over the hills, in upper parts of the
author: APP
article_text:
The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast rain accompanied by wind and thunderstorms, with snowfall over the hills, in upper parts of the country during the next two to three days under the influence of a westerly weather system.

According to the PMD, a shallow westerly wave approached the western and northern parts of the country on the evening of November 10. The system is likely to intensify on November 12 and may persist over upper parts of the country until the morning of November 14.

Under the influence of this weather system, rain accompanied by wind and thunderstorms, with isolated heavy falls and hailstorms, is expected in various districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa from November 11 to the morning of November 14, with occasional gaps.

The areas likely to receive rain include Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Shangla, Battagram, Mansehra, Abbottabad, Haripur, Buner, Malakand, Bajaur, Mohmand, Kohat, Peshawar, Charsadda, Nowshera, Mardan, Swabi, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, Hangu, Lakki Marwat, Karak, Bannu, Dera Ismail Khan and Waziristan. Snowfall over the mountains is also likely during the period.

In Punjab and Islamabad, light rain accompanied by wind and thunderstorms is expected in Islamabad, the Potohar region, Mianwali, Khushab, Bhakkar, Sargodha, Murree and adjoining areas tonight.

More rain and thunderstorms are forecast for Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Murree, Galiyat, Attock, Chakwal, Jhelum, Mandi Bahauddin, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad, Lahore, Kasur, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Narowal, Mianwali, Khushab and Sargodha on November 12 and 13, with occasional gaps.

Rain and thunderstorms are also expected in Dera Ghazi Khan, Layyah, Bhakkar and Multan on November 12. Isolated hailstorms may also occur during the forecast period.

In Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, rain accompanied by wind and thunderstorms, with snowfall over the hills, is expected until the afternoon of November 14, with occasional gaps.

The areas where rain is likely in Kashmir include Neelum Valley, Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot, Poonch, Hattian, Bagh, Haveli, Sudhanoti, Kotli, Bhimber and Mirpur, while in Gilgit-Baltistan, Diamir, Astore, Ghizer, Skardu, Hunza, Gilgit, Ghanche and Shigar are likely to receive precipitation.

Meanwhile, mainly dry weather is expected to prevail over most districts of Balochistan and Sindh. However, isolated rain accompanied by wind and thunderstorms, with possible hailstorms, is forecast in Zhob, Barkhan, Musakhel, Quetta, Ziarat, Chaman, Qila Abdullah, Qila Saifullah, Kalat and Khuzdar on the night of November 11 and November 12.

The PMD has advised farmers to plan their agricultural activities in accordance with the expected weather conditions.

It further stated that light snowfall is likely over high mountains and glaciers during the wet spell, while foggy conditions may develop in patches over plain areas after the rainy period. Daytime temperatures are also expected to drop by 2-4 degrees Celsius during the forecast period.

The department has advised all concerned authorities to remain vigilant and take necessary precautionary measures to avoid any untoward situation.

The public can access daily weather updates through the PMD website at weather.gov.pk and the Pak Weather mobile application.

headline: DPM Dar holds follow-up with JI delegation to continue petroleum prices, public relief consultations
description: Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister (DPM/FM), Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar on Tuesday held a follow-up meeting with a delegation of Jamaat-e-Islami (JI), led
author: APP
article_text: Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister (DPM/FM), Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar on Tuesday held a follow-up meeting with a delegation of Jamaat-e-Islami (JI), led by Liaquat Baloch, to continue consultations on petroleum prices and public relief. The two sides held constructive discussions on measures to provide relief to consumers, particularly low-income households. There was broad agreement on the need to address public concerns through continued consultation and cooperation, a DPM’s Office news release said. The DPM/FM welcomed the positive spirit of the engagement. He reiterated that the Government remained focused on supporting ordinary households amid prevailing economic challenges. The meeting was attended by Adviser to the Prime Minister on Inter-Provincial Coordination Rana Sanaullah, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Tariq Bajwa, Special Secretary, Petroleum Division, Additional Secretary, Finance Division, as well as members of the JI delegation, Syed Firasat Shah, Nasrullah Randhawa and Inayatullah Khan.

headline: PM Shehbaz arrives in Antalya to participate in COP31 Leaders’ Summit
description: Prime Minister Muhammad Shahbaz Sharif arrived in Antalya, Republic of Türkiye, on Tuesday on an official visit to attend the Leaders’ Summit of the 31st
author: APP
article_text:
Prime Minister Muhammad Shahbaz Sharif arrived in Antalya, Republic of Türkiye, on Tuesday on an official visit to attend the Leaders’ Summit of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Upon arrival, the prime minister was received by the Deputy Minister of Culture and Tourism of the Republic of Türkiye, Gökhan Yazgi, Pakistan’s Ambassador-designate to Türkiye, Amna Baloch, and senior Turkish officials, a Prime Minister’s Office news release said.

The prime minister will address the COP31 Antalya Leaders’ Summit, highlighting Pakistan’s climate priorities and emphasizing the urgent need for enhanced global climate action and strengthened international cooperation to mitigate the adverse impacts of climate change, in accordance with established principles.

The prime minister will also address the High-Level Dialogue on Clean Energy Transition and Electrification, titled “35 by 35: Powering the Future.”

On the sidelines of the Summit, the prime minister is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Erdogan and other world leaders attending COP31 to discuss matters of mutual interest and strengthen bilateral cooperation.

“Pakistan Pavilion” has been established at the COP31 venue, where 54 events will be hosted on various themes.

Pakistan’s contributions in previous COP outcomes include, among others, active climate diplomacy that led to the establishment of the Loss and Damage Fund during COP27.

headline: First winter storm floods thousands of Gaza tents, killing children and leaving thousands stranded
description: At least five Palestinians, including three children and an infant, died when a rain-soaked sand dune collapsed onto their displacement tents in Gaza, the UN
author: APP
article_text:
At least five Palestinians, including three children and an infant, died when a rain-soaked sand dune collapsed onto their displacement tents in Gaza, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) reported.

Thousands of families lost their shelters and belongings as rain and strong winds began lashing Gaza on Friday night, flooding displacement sites, collapsing damaged buildings and disrupting services across all five governorates, OCHA said in its latest update.

The dune collapsed onto tents at Al Berka Reservoir, west of Deir Al Balah, killing three children and two women and injuring one other person, according to local authorities.

Speaking from Ramallah, UN Deputy Special Coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov said that while rain could not be prevented, more must be done to protect the vulnerable, noting that most Gazans are living in worn-out tents that cannot withstand what would be considered a moderate storm elsewhere.

Some 65 per cent of Gaza’s population, about 1.4 million people, live in tents or makeshift shelters.

By 8 November, humanitarian partners had received appeals for aid from more than 26,000 households whose shelters or belongings were damaged. More than 6,000 family shelters were reportedly destroyed and 17,400 damaged, and more than 3,900 households currently have no shelter at all.

Partners have so far assessed the needs of 1,877 households and supported 422 households at 29 displacement sites.

Water levels rose to 1.5 metres in some locations, and civil defence units received 2,166 distress calls but could respond to only 218.

At least 55 learning spaces serving some 55,000 children were also flooded. Health facilities were also damaged forcing some medical teams to suspend services. Mine action partners warned that floodwaters could expose or displace explosive ordnance.

The UN and its partners are pumping out water, improving drainage, reinforcing sites with sandbags, repairing shelters and delivering emergency supplies. But humanitarian stocks of tents, tarpaulins, blankets and clothes inside Gaza are virtually exhausted.

Residents of one tent camp in Deir Al Balah said overflowing sewage had surged in with the floodwater, soaking mattresses, clothing and other belongings.

More than 150,000 tents purchased by humanitarian partners and Member States are outside Gaza ready to be dispatched, including about 117,000 from the Egyptian Relief Committee in Al-Arish.

Alakbarov called for the urgent lifting of all unnecessary restrictions and delays, including those preventing aid organizations from bringing in enough vacuum trucks, dewatering pumps, heavy machinery, engine oil, spare parts, tents, tarpaulins, plastic sheeting, blankets and winter clothing.

In response to a reporter’s question, UN Deputy Spokesperson Farhan Haq told the daily news briefing that Israeli efforts to facilitate rebuilding in Gaza had been insufficient.

“We certainly can be getting more in. We just need the permissions from the Israeli authorities to get them in through the various checkpoints.”

Meanwhile, Israeli strikes continue to hit populated areas. On Saturday, UN personnel visiting a displacement site in Gaza City had to take cover when gunfire erupted nearby.

headline: Petrol price reduced to Rs338 per litre, diesel set at Rs371
description: The federal government has announced a fresh reduction in fuel prices, lowering petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) rates to provide some relief to consumers.
author: Web Desk
article_text:
The federal government has announced a fresh reduction in fuel prices, lowering petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) rates to provide some relief to consumers.

Under a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, petrol has become cheaper by Rs8 per litre, while the price of high-speed diesel has been cut by Rs7.

With the latest adjustment, petrol will now cost Rs338 per litre, compared with the previous rate of Rs346. Diesel prices have also declined from Rs378 to Rs371 per litre.

The reduction is expected to ease fuel expenses for motorists and transport operators, while the lower diesel rate may help reduce freight and transportation costs.

According to the notification, the revised prices will take effect from midnight on November 10 (Wednesday) and remain in force until November 11.

headline: PESSI Commissioner directs accelerated registration of industrial workers
description: LAHORE - Commissioner Punjab Social Security Zulfiqar Ali Kharal has directed all directorates to accelerate the registration of unregistered industrial and
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Commissioner Punjab Social Security Zulfiqar Ali Kharal has directed all directorates to accelerate the registration of unregistered industrial and commercial establishments to bring maximum workers under the Social Security system. Chairing a meeting at the Punjab Employees Social Security Institution (PESSI) Head Office here on Tuesday, he reviewed the performance of Social Security Directorates across Punjab, recovery targets and workers’ registration. During the meeting, he was briefed on progress in the recovery of Social Security contributions and Workers Welfare Funds, along with measures being taken to extend Social Security coverage to more workers. The commissioner said registration with Punjab Social Security was mandatory for all industrial and commercial establishments employing two or more workers. He stressed the need to make the registration process more effective and expedite the inclusion of unregistered establishments so that maximum workers could benefit from Social Security facilities. He also directed all directorates concerned to improve their performance and ensure timely achievement of assigned recovery and registration targets. Zulfiqar Ali Kharal said industrial and commercial establishments must fulfil their legal and moral responsibility by registering their workers with Social Security.

headline: Eight matches decided as Allama Iqbal Elnox Basketball begins
description: LAHORE - The inaugural Allama Iqbal Elnox Trophy Inter-School Boys and Girls Basketball Tournament got off to an exciting start at the International Abdul
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The inaugural Allama Iqbal Elnox Trophy Inter-School Boys and Girls Basketball Tournament got off to an exciting start at the International Abdul Nasir Basketball Court, Burns Road, with eight matches decided on the opening day. Additional Commissioner Karachi Dr Aatif Jalib formally inaugurated the event, organised by Usman Club and Firdous Ittehad Basketball Club under the permission of the Karachi Basketball Association (KBBA). The opening ceremony was attended by Babar Hanif, M Yousuf, Ghulam Muhammad Khan, Asad Ibad Ali, Imran Katia, Ghulam Din, Abdul Hameed Baloch, Younis Qureshi, Haider Khan and a large number of sports enthusiasts. On the court, Army Public School Saddar defeated Beaconhouse School Gulshan 20-15, with Furqan Haider scoring 12 points. Bahria Roots recorded a convincing 29-0 victory over K.N. Academy, while Indus Academy overcame St Patrick’s School 16-4. NJV School beat FG Public School Saddar 22-2, and Wheels School and College edged Beaconhouse PECHS 23-19 in a competitive encounter. Bahria College School defeated BCP Gulshan 20-8, while Karachi Grammar School registered an emphatic 44-10 win over Army Public School Faisal. In the eighth fixture, FG Fazaia School were awarded a walkover against Fazaia School Malir. The matches were supervised by Muhammad Ashraf, Zahid Malik, Aamir Sharif, Naeem Ahmed, Zaeema Khatoon, Izhar Hussain and Nusrat Afzal. Congratulating the organisers on the launch of the tournament, renowned journalist and Pakistan Sports Writers Association (PSWA) Secretary General Asghar Azeem appreciated the efforts of the organising committee, particularly patron Ghulam Muhammad Khan, Organising Secretary Asad Ibad Ali, Coordinator Haji Muhammad Ashraf Yahya, Aamir Sharif and Ghulam Abbas Jamal Chaudhry. He also assured the organisers of his full cooperation in promoting the event.

headline: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
description: PARIS - French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: PARIS - French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed’s abuse. The Paris prosecutor’s office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released. In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities. It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner. Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor’s office said. It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into “allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape”. The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed. The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family. The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson. The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims: “At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities. “In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators. “Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations. “The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor’s Office.” A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation. Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024. One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence. Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers. A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed’s brother, Salah Fayed, who died in 2010. Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations. Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate. In a statement, a force spokesperson said: “Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims. “Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further.” The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the “significant developments” and cooperation between the Met and French authorities. “We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked,” the group said. “We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated.” The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: “France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like. “Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over.” The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it “does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour” and that it was ready “to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities”.

In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities. It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner. Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor’s office said.

It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into “allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape”. The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed.

The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family.

headline: Police officer dies and another injured after backpack explosion in northern Spain
description: MADRID - A police officer has died and another has been injured in the northern Spanish city of Oviedo after an explosive device went off at the scene of a
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: MADRID - A police officer has died and another has been injured in the northern Spanish city of Oviedo after an explosive device went off at the scene of a shooting. The blast happened when officers from Spain’s canine unit and explosives disposal unit arrived and examined a suspicious backpack following reports of a dispute between neighbours on Tuesday morning. A woman who had been shot and the injured officer have been taken to hospital for treatment. The suspect fled the scene and is still at large, police said. Spanish police paid tribute to the dead officer, who has been named as Juan José, in a statement on X and said: “Our hearts are with his family, friends, colleagues and loved ones.” Officers attended the scene early after receiving reports of an argument between neighbours and upon arriving found a woman who had sustained gunshot wounds, police spokesman Pedro Aguado said. While searching for the suspected attacker, officers found a suspicious backpack with a flashing light and contacted both the bomb disposal unit and canine unit. “While the package was being moved outside to ensure the safety of the residents, an explosion occurred,” Aguado added. The explosion left a member of the canine unit dead and an officer from the bomb disposal unit seriously injured, he said. A three-year-old police dog named Deny was also killed in the explosion. A widespread police operation is ongoing near the scene of the explosion and officers are continuing to hunt for the suspect. Taking to social media, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he was “deeply shocked” by the fatal incident and paid tribute to the officer injured in the explosion. “Your dedication and courage deserve the gratitude of an entire country,” he said. Spanish opposition leader and President of the People’s Party Alberto Núñez Feijóo said: “What happened in Oviedo is heartbreaking. “My condolences to the family of the officer who died and my best wishes for the recovery of the one who was seriously injured.

headline: Pakistan set to make strong impression in Tent Pegging World Cup: ECP President
description: LAHORE - Equestrian Federation of Pakistan (EFP) President Raja Zarrar Sajjad has expressed confidence in the national team’s prospects at the 2026 Tent
author: Azhar Khan
article_text:
LAHORE - Equestrian Federation of Pakistan (EFP) President Raja Zarrar Sajjad has expressed confidence in the national team’s prospects at the 2026 Tent Pegging World Cup in Aqaba, Jordan, following Pakistan’s historic first-place finish in the qualifying competition in Oman, where the riders secured 455 points, six gold, five silver and two bronze medals, besides sweeping all three positions on the overall individual podium. In an interview with The Nation, Raja Zarrar Sajjad described the Oman performance as a major milestone for Pakistan’s tent pegging and said it reflected the country’s strength, depth of talent and growing competitiveness at the international level. “Pakistan’s runners-up finish at the 2023 World Cup in South Africa has already established its ability to challenge the best teams, while the latest qualifying triumph has further strengthened confidence in the national squad,” he said. He credited the success to the commitment and hard work of the riders, coaches and support staff, emphasising that the federation’s long-term ambition was to develop a sustainable system capable of producing international champions consistently. “Pakistan wants to earn recognition as a leading equestrian nation through professional sporting standards alongside its rich horse-riding traditions.” Regarding preparations for the 2026 World Cup in Aqaba, Sajjad said the national team had completed a dedicated training camp in Mianwali under the supervision of head coach Haroon Bandial. The programme focused on physical conditioning, advanced horsemanship, lance and sword techniques, target accuracy, consistency and coordination.

He said the Oman qualifying triumph had provided the riders with considerable confidence, but stressed that competing at World Cup level demanded exceptional preparation, discipline and precision, as even minor technical mistakes could influence the final outcome. He expressed confidence that the team’s preparation and international experience would help Pakistan make a strong impression at the prestigious championship.Discussing the development of tent pegging, Sajjad described it as one of the oldest and most exciting equestrian disciplines, combining horsemanship, speed, courage, precision and technical ability. “The sport requires riders to gallop along a designated track and strike and retrieve ground targets, traditionally wooden pegs, using a lance or sword. “Other competitions include picking up rings and striking suspended targets such as lemons. Its principal events comprise individual lance, individual sword, rings and peg, lemons and peg, and team competitions,” he asserted. He explained that successful target retrieval and accuracy determine the scoring, while the biggest challenge is maintaining balance, control and coordination with the horse at high speed. According to him, Pakistan enjoys a natural advantage because of its established horse-riding culture and longstanding association with tent pegging.

However, the EFP president said the federation was determined to develop the sport beyond its traditional foundations through structured coaching, youth development, national competitions and technical education. “The greater participation from schools, colleges and universities has also been among the federation’s priorities, with the objective of preserving the sport’s heritage while bringing training and competition standards in line with international requirements.”

headline: Top Iranian security official says no talks underway with US
description: Tehran - Iran’s top security official Mohsen Rezaei said Tuesday there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran and Washington, in an
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:

headline: France blames Iran for ‘unprecedented’ supermarket fridge cyberattack
description: PARIS - France is blaming Iran for last month’s supermarket refrigerator cyberattack that spoiled produce at around 700 retailers, and is vowing to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: PARIS - France is blaming Iran for last month’s supermarket refrigerator cyberattack that spoiled produce at around 700 retailers, and is vowing to impose sanctions in response, with Tehran on Tuesday rejecting the claim as “baseless and hostile.” “This was an attack of unprecedented scale and unprecedented aggressiveness,” Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot told reporters Monday. He described it as the first large-scale cyberattack carried out for sabotage purposes on French national territory. “It represents a major assault on the nation’s interests and on the security of the French people,” Barrot said. France has summoned Iran’s ambassador and intends to impose retaliatory sanctions “at a European level,” he added. Iran’s Foreign Ministry on Tuesday strongly dismissed the French government’s accusation, claiming it “is intended to divert public opinion from France’s destructive policies toward Iran.” Tehran “will not hesitate to take necessary and appropriate measures to protect its national interests and security against unlawful foreign actions,” it added. Asked Tuesday about Iran’s response and how France could be certain the attack was Iranian, Barrot said France had established “with certainty” that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was behind it, but said he would not disclose how that determination was made. Barrot said the Revolutionary Guards would “obviously” deny responsibility because “they fear the response that we could make, and that we will make.” The cyberattack in October occurred when hackers remotely connected to supermarket refrigerators and freezers, then raised their temperature by switching on defrost cycles, according to CNN affiliate BFMTV. That led to the loss of large quantities of fresh and frozen produce and even caused some of the refrigeration equipment to catch fire. The Paris prosecutor’s office took up the case and on Monday accused Iran of being behind the attack, citing “the use of Farsi and IP addresses pointing to devices located in Iran.”

headline: First day of Ukraine peace talks ‘very productive’, US says
description: ABU DHABI - The first day of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi. While senior
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ABU DHABI - The first day of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi. While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions - due to resume on Wednesday - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who did not attend the talks, said they had been “very productive”. Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia’s full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing “a little bit of flexibility” on the issue of who would control Ukraine’s eastern regions in a postwar scenario. At the start of Tuesday’s talks President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had “narrowed the gaps” between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a “solution that hopefully ends the war”. Kushner said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the “postwar security concerns” of both Russia and Ukraine. He and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting.

headline: Oman triumph boosts Pakistan’s World Cup hopes: EFP President
description: LAHORE - Equestrian Federation of Pakistan (EFP) President Raja Zarrar Sajjad has expressed confidence in the national team’s prospects at the 2026 Tent
author: Azhar Khan
article_text:
LAHORE - Equestrian Federation of Pakistan (EFP) President Raja Zarrar Sajjad has expressed confidence in the national team’s prospects at the 2026 Tent Pegging World Cup in Aqaba, Jordan, following Pakistan’s historic first-place finish in the qualifying competition in Oman, where the riders secured 455 points, six gold, five silver and two bronze medals, besides sweeping all three positions on the overall individual podium.

In an interview with The Nation, Raja Zarrar Sajjad described the Oman performance as a major milestone for Pakistan’s tent pegging and said it reflected the country’s strength, depth of talent and growing competitive-ness at the international level. “Pakistan’s runners-up finish at the 2023 World Cup in South Af-rica has already established its ability to challenge the best teams, while the latest qualifying triumph has further strengthened confidence in the national squad,” he said. He credited the success to the commitment and hard work of the riders, coaches and support staff, emphasising that the federation’s long-term ambition was to develop a sustainable system capable of producing international champions consistently. “Pakistan wants to earn recognition as a leading equestrian nation through professional sporting standards alongside its rich horse-riding traditions.”

Discussing the development of tent pegging, Sajjad described it as one of the oldest and most exciting equestrian disciplines, combining horsemanship, speed, courage, precision and tech-nical ability. “The sport requires riders to gallop along a designated track and strike and retrieve ground targets, traditionally wooden pegs, using a lance or sword.

“Other competitions include picking up rings and striking suspended targets such as lemons. Its principal events comprise individual lance, individual sword, rings and peg, lemons and peg, and team competitions,” he asserted.

He explained that successful target retrieval and accuracy determine the scoring, while the big-gest challenge is maintaining balance, control and coordination with the horse at high speed. According to him, Pakistan enjoys a natural advantage because of its established horse-riding culture and longstanding association with tent pegging.

However, the EFP president said the federation was determined to develop the sport beyond its traditional foundations through structured coaching, youth development, national competitions and technical education. “The greater participation from schools, colleges and universities has also been among the federation’s priorities, with the objective of preserving the sport’s heritage while bringing training and competition standards in line with international requirements.”

Regarding preparations for the 2026 World Cup in Aqaba, Sajjad said the national team had completed a dedicated training camp in Mianwali under the supervision of head coach Haroon Bandial. The programme focused on physical conditioning, advanced horsemanship, lance and sword techniques, target accuracy, consistency and coordination.

He said the Oman qualifying triumph had provided the riders with considerable confidence, but stressed that competing at World Cup level demanded exceptional preparation, discipline and precision, as even minor technical mistakes could influence the final outcome. He expressed confidence that the team’s preparation and international experience would help Pakistan make a strong impression at the prestigious championship.

headline: Twelve dead after motorway pile-ups in Bulgaria fog
description: SOFIA - Twelve people have been killed after dozens of cars and lorries were involved in two pile-ups on the Trakia motorway in south-eastern Bulgaria,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
SOFIA - Twelve people have been killed after dozens of cars and lorries were involved in two pile-ups on the Trakia motorway in south-eastern Bulgaria, President Rumen Radev has said. Health Minister Katya Ivkova said 11 people died at the scene on Tuesday, near the town of Zimnitsa, while another person later died in hospital. About 50 others were taken to hospital with injuries. Sliven regional governor Mihail Kasherov told journalists that more than 70 vehicles were involved in the incident, Bulgarian state news agency BTA reported. Officials have said dense fog reduced visibility and was the likely cause of the first crash, which occurred on the eastbound carriageway. Radev declared Wednesday a day of national mourning following the incident. The second crash, on the Sofia-bound carriageway, was likely also caused by the fog, with drivers also distracted by the first crash, BTA reported an official as saying. The Trakia motorway runs from west-to-east of Bulgaria, and connects the capital Sofia to the Black Sea coast. Road administration director Galin Kostov added that speeds were unsuitable for the conditions, which included wet road surfaces, and the motorway would remain closed until it had been cleared, BTA reported. Yambol regional governor Georgi Chalakov said reports first came in at 07:10 local time (05:10 GMT), with the injured taken by ambulance to hospitals in the Yambol, Sliven and Burgas regions. Chalakov told BTA rescue teams had to remove sections of the crash barrier to reach people. He added that the fog meant that helicopters could not be used in the evacuation efforts.

One witness who helped rescue a man from a burning vehicle blamed “very thick fog” for the pile-up. “I got out of the car, I ran forward and pulled that man out,” the witness told Reuters news agency. Another told Reuters that “many, many people died”. “As for me, there were four cars behind me - trucks - and I don’t know how I got out or what happened, but in the end, thank God I’m still alive,” that witness said.

headline: More than 12 US military aircraft leave second UK base
description: LONDON - More than 12 US Air Force aircraft have left a second airbase in Britain weeks after the US withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford over a suspected
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LONDON - More than 12 US Air Force aircraft have left a second airbase in Britain weeks after the US withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford over a suspected Iran-linked security incident. The latest plane to leave, a Boeing Stratotanker KC-135 refuelling aircraft, flew from RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk on Tuesday afternoon and headed towards Germany. The Wall Street Journal reported that the departures have been in response to a further threat from Iran but the BBC has not independently verified that claim. Downing Street has insisted British air bases are safe and that their security is a “top priority”. Using public flight-tracking site Flightradar24 BBC Verify was able to see 10 USAF KC-135 tankers leaving RAF Mildenhall throughout Monday. Two aircraft which left the base on Monday morning initially flew to US bases in Germany and Italy. The first of these KC-135s flew to Spangdahlem air base in south-west Germany where it completed a series of circuits before returning to Mildenhall. It then flew east and landed at Spangdahlem. The other aircraft was seen flying circuits over Aviano air base in north-east Italy before going on to land at Spangdahlem. Neither aircraft was tracked returning to Mildenhall. Later in the day more KC-135s flew from Mildenhall - two flew to Spangdahlem, one to the US base at Ramstein in Germany and four to Morón air base in southern Spain. Three Osprey aircraft have have also left that RAF base.

One aircraft, belonging to the Nebraska Air National Guard in the US, went to Prestwick Airport in Ayrshire. It is not clear if this was a planned stopover before the jet returned to its home base. Asked about Monday’s flights, a Ministry of Defence (MoD) spokesperson told the BBC: “We do not routinely comment on the activity of other nations. Aircraft and other assets move regularly according to operational requirements.” Downing Street, meanwhile, has insisted that UK airbases are safe, with the prime minister’s official spokesperson saying “the protection of our bases, both in the UK and across the world, is a top priority”. About 3,000 military personnel are stationed at RAF Mildenhall, which is around 80 miles (130km) north of London.

There was no apparent additional security at the base on Tuesday, and the spaces from which the public could photograph aircraft remained open. The base is mostly used for refuelling and maintenance operations. Flights carrying US presidents, including Donald Trump, have often used it, and Trump came through RAF Mildenhall on his way back to the US from a Nato summit in Ankara in July.

It has also been used as a staging area for aircraft and material bound for the Middle East, with air refuelling tankers “forward deployed” to the region during operations against Iran. Asked about the US evacuating aircraft from RAF Mildenhall, Education Secretary Lucy Powell told BBC Breakfast she could not comment on ongoing operational matters. She added that “we take the security and safety of our bases incredibly seriously” and “we will always act on security intelligence when we need to”. A US Air Force spokesperson said its aircraft “rotate between installations and operating locations for a variety of reasons including training and real world requirements”.

headline: Embassy of Pakistan commemorates 149th birth anniversary of Allama Iqbal with special event
description: WASHINGTON, D.C - To commemorate the 149th birth anniversary of Dr Allama Muhammad Iqbal, the Embassy of Pakistan in Washington, D.C., hosted a commemorative
author: The Nation
article_text: WASHINGTON, D.C - To commemorate the 149th birth anniversary of Dr Allama Muhammad Iqbal, the Embassy of Pakistan in Washington, D.C., hosted a commemorative event featuring an Iqbal Day Mehfil-e-Mushaira (poetry symposium) alongside an exhibition of Sadequain’s paintings depicting Iqbal’s poetry. The event was marked by rich tributes to the National Poet of Pakistan, who spelled out the idea of an independent homeland for the Muslims of the subcontinent. The event was organized in collaboration with the International Academy of Letters USA and Bazm-e-Harf-o-Sukhan, a prominent literary organization dedicated to promoting Urdu literature and poetry. The gathering drew a distinguished audience, including members of civil society, academicians, students, and representatives from the media. During the ceremony, official messages from the Prime Minister of Pakistan and the Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister were read out. In his keynote address, Ambassador Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, highlighted the profound intellectual significance of Allama Iqbal’s message that continued to inspire generations. “The intellectual foundation of our national life is rooted in the thought of Iqbal, just as the leadership of the Quaid constitutes the political foundation of our national life,” Ambassador Sheikh stated. Elaborating on the central focus of Iqbal’s poetry in relation to the conceptualization of Pakistan, the Ambassador noted: “The way Iqbal sought to awaken the youth and the nation during his time effectively yielded the intellectual foundation of the Pakistan Movement.” Ambassador Sheikh further underscored the concept of Khudi (Selfhood) and human nobility—one of the cardinal themes in Iqbal’s philosophy and poetic works. “Within Iqbal’s vision of Khudi lies a self- realization and confidence. It is taking cognizance of rightful place as the crown of all creation,” the Ambassador remarked. Calling for sustained engagement with Iqbal’s intellectual heritage, Ambassador Sheikh urged attendees to convey his timeless message to future generations for academic self-reliance, guidance, and new ideas. “It marks a glowing chapter of our national history that we must celebrate and need to do a far batter job at transfer of this lavish legacy to the future generations. Our intellectual tradition is undoubtedly rich and worthy of carriage forward”, he added. The program also featured an engaging panel discussion titled “The Poetry of Iqbal and the Demands of the Contemporary Era,” where speakers emphasized how Iqbal’s philosophy resonates across eras to provide continuous guidance for contemporary challenges. Following the panel, a musical performance based on the poetry of Iqbal captivated the audience. In his closing remarks, Ambassador Rizwan Saeed Sheikh expressed his gratitude to all participants for joining the Embassy in honoring Iqbal’s legacy and reiterated the importance of integrating his philosophy into practical life.
