headline: Trump says more US attacks on Iran highly unlikely
description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump has said he believes the US war on Iran is “effectively over” but Washington was ready to resume military
author: News Desk
article_text:
WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump has said he believes the US war on Iran is “effectively over” but Washington was ready to resume military strikes if necessary.

In a briefing on Monday after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House, Trump reiterated his position that the United States had destroyed Iran’s military. But his remarks suggested he faces pressure from allies in the Middle East to bring hostilities to a close.

Qatar and Saudi Arabia were eager for a peaceful solution to the Iran conflict, Trump said. “Qatar would rather see a peaceful solution and Saudi Arabia would rather see a peaceful solution” but “we’re ready ⁠to go anytime we want” with strikes, he told Reuters.

Trump added in a post on Truth Social that a resumption of US military strikes on Iran was “quite unlikely,” saying that Gulf powers wanted to keep the status quo.

“Iran militarily is effectively over,” he said. “We’re just keeping it the status quo, and we’re doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbors.”

He added that Iran has been “decapitated” but said he is still looking to make sure there’s a long-term solution to ensuring that Iran’s nuclear program is defanged.

“I had an excellent conversation with Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani,” Trump said on Truth Social, adding that “much was discussed with respect to the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

“We are seeing positive momentum toward an end to this conflict, and will ensure that America’s interests are at all times protected,” Trump said. Trump’s comments echoed early statements to CNN over the weekend when he said it was “highly unlikely” fighting would resume.

Sheikh Mohammed said he had positive discussions with Trump ⁠and Vice President JD Vance ⁠on Monday. “We discussed the situation in the region and ways to progress the US-Iran talks. Grateful for the positive discussions on reaching a deal and bringing peace to the ⁠region,” he ⁠said on X.

Trump said the “status quo” would involve continuing the US naval blockade against Iranian ports, as well as the newly announced Task Force Iron Gate, which seeks to cut off trade by land and through the Caspian Sea.

“In other words, a continuation of the greatest naval blockade in the history of our country. Probably in the history of the world,” he said.

Trump also indicated in his briefing that the US was willing to resume fighting, should the need arise.

“Taking military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing, but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes,” he said.

“Israel and the entire Middle East are protected from Iranian danger and threats, and we’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon.”

Iranian officials, meanwhile, dismissed Trump’s latest remarks as a distraction.

headline: IHC orders lawyers meeting with jailed Imran, Bushra
description: ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) Tuesday directed authorities to arrange meetings between imprisoned PTI founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The Islamabad High Court (IHC) Tuesday directed authorities to arrange meetings between imprisoned PTI founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi and their lawyers. A division bench of IHC comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif conducted hearing of their appeals against convictions in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case and issued the directives after lawyers Latif Khosa and Barrister Salman Safdar complained of prolonged denial of access to their clients. The court ordered that the counsel be allowed one-hour meetings with both Khan and Bushra at Adiala Jail before the next hearing and urged the defence to begin arguments when proceedings resume. During the hearing, Safdar told the court he had met Imran Khan after seven months and Bushra Bibi after eleven months, and raised serious concerns about their health. He said that Khan’s blood pressure remained uncontrolled and that the former prime minister feared a risk of brain haemorrhage, while Bushra’s eyesight had deteriorated and she was scheduled for another operation on November 15. The lawyer requested a medical board to examine Bushra Bibi, but the court noted that health-related matters were already pending before the Federal Constitutional Court. At the outset, Khosa told the court that an earlier order allowing him to meet Imran had not been implemented. IHC Chief Justice said that the previous order had been for Barrister Salman Safdar to meet the PTI founder, not Khosa. “You are not the one whose meeting was ordered; the order was for Salman Safdar’s meeting,” Justice Dogar told Khosa. Khosa responded that an order for a meeting already existed but that no meeting had taken place. He said his undertaking to argue the appeals was conditional on being allowed to meet Imran. The IHC Chief Justice, however, said that it had already been settled that Khosa would argue the appeals and urged him to begin. He asked Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Malik whether arrangements could be made for the meeting within one or two days. “I want to remove this obstacle and proceed with the matter,” Chief Justice Dogar said, adding that he wanted Khosa to begin his arguments even if he had only two sentences to make. He also said that the lawyer could argue for two or four hours. Khosa subsequently requested a one-hour meeting with Imran, prompting the chief justice to direct the advocate general to arrange it within two days. Safdar also asked the court to fix appeals against sentences in the other cases for hearing and take up a miscellaneous application. He said that his first protest in the matter concerned the failure to arrange a meeting with Bushra Bibi for 11 months. He added that he had filed an affidavit in the case, something he had never done before. The lawyer said he could file a fresh bail application on new grounds but had not done so yet. He then drew the court’s attention to Bushra Bibi’s health, saying that she had been wearing dark glasses and that her eyesight had deteriorated. According to Safdar, jail authorities had informed him that her next operation was scheduled for November 15. He said that he did not know who was treating her or where she was receiving treatment. “I am not asking for bail; a medical board should be formed,” he told the court, seeking an independent assessment of her condition. He added that even if Bushra Bibi was not entitled to bail, she could be granted temporary bail for four to six weeks to receive treatment. Safdar said that women were entitled to concessions in such matters and asked the court to obtain complete medical reports from Adiala jail. He maintained that proper treatment was not possible in prison and questioned why Bushra Bibi had been returned to her cell on the same day after an operation. He also conveyed Imran’s concerns about his own health, saying the PTI founder had told him that his blood pressure was not under control and had risen above 190, putting him at risk of a brain haemorrhage. Safdar added that Imran had said that his eyesight had improved. The advocate general told the court that medical treatment was a fundamental right and that the government was not neglecting its responsibilities. “All medical facilities are being provided,” he said, presenting a record of the treatment provided to Bushra Bibi. He said the matter concerned not just one prisoner but around 10,000 inmates. He also referred to records summoned by the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) from the Supreme Court in cases involving three prisoners. At the conclusion of the hearing, the court directed that the paper books be provided to the lawyers and prepared before the next hearing. It also instructed counsel to begin their arguments at the next hearing, following the arrangement of Khosa’s meeting with Imran. Later, the court deferred the proceedings for ten days.

The advocate general told the court that medical treatment was a fundamental right and that the government was not neglecting its responsibilities. “All medical facilities are being provided,” he said, presenting a record of the treatment provided to Bushra Bibi.

He said the matter concerned not just one prisoner but around 10,000 inmates. He also referred to records summoned by the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) from the Supreme Court in cases involving three prisoners.

At the conclusion of the hearing, the court directed that the paper books be provided to the lawyers and prepared before the next hearing. It also instructed counsel to begin their arguments at the next hearing, following the arrangement of Khosa’s meeting with Imran.

Later, the court deferred the proceedings for ten days.

headline: PM arrives in Türkiye to attend COP31 Leaders’ Summit
description: ANTALYA - Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif arrived in Antalya Republic of Türkiye, on Tuesday on official visit to attend the Leaders’ Summit of the
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ANTALYA - Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif arrived in Antalya Republic of Türkiye, on Tuesday on official visit to attend the Leaders’ Summit of the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

Upon arrival, the prime minister was received by Deputy Minister of Culture and Tourism of the Republic of Türkiye, Gökhan Yazgi, Pakistan’s Ambassador-designate to Türkiye, Amna Baloch, and senior Turkish officials, a Prime Minister’s Office news release said.

The prime minister will address the COP31 Antalya Leaders’ Summit, highlighting Pakistan’s climate priorities and emphasizing the urgent need for enhanced global climate action and strengthened international cooperation to mitigate the adverse impacts of climate change, in accordance with established principles.

The prime minister will also address the High-Level Dialogue on Clean Energy Transition and Electrification, titled “35 by 35: Powering the Future.”

On the sidelines of the Summit, the prime minister is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Turkish President Recep Erdogan and other world leaders attending COP31 to discuss matters of mutual interest and strengthen bilateral cooperation.

“Pakistan Pavilion” has been established at the COP31 venue where 54 events will be hosted on various themes. Pakistan’s contributions in previous COP outcomes include among others active climate diplomacy that led to the establishment of Loss and Damage Fund during COP27.

headline: Seven Pakistani juniors shine in J-30 World Junior Tennis
description: LAHORE -Seven Pakistani boys made impressive progress in the round-robin stage of the J-30 PPL Pakistan World Junior Tennis Championships, securing victories
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE -Seven Pakistani boys made impressive progress in the round-robin stage of the J-30 PPL Pakistan World Junior Tennis Championships, securing victories in their second-round matches at the PTF Tennis Complex on Tuesday. Hamza Roman, Ahtesham Hu-mayun, Rayyan Khan, M Yahya, Amir Mazari, Abdul Basit and M Hassan Usmani all recorded wins to remain in contention for quarter-final places. Hamza defeated Singapore’s Brennon Ng 6-4, 7-5, while Abdul Basit overcame Thailand’s Tachatam Srisen 7-5, 6-3. Rayyan edged Serbia’s Vukasin Pavlovic 6-4, 1-6, 10-7, and Ahtesham beat Sri Lanka’s Jayin De Saram 6-3, 6-4. Hassan defeated Kazakhstan’s Alshinhan Mukhamedkali 6-2, 6-0, while Amir and Yahya also registered victories.

headline: Trump nominates Natalie Baker as US Ambassador to Pakistan
description: ISLAMABAD - US President Donald Trump has nominated Natalie Baker, currently serving as the American chargé d’affaires in Islamabad, as the next
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text: ISLAMABAD - US President Donald Trump has nominated Natalie Baker, currently serving as the American chargé d’affaires in Islamabad, as the next United States ambassador to Pakistan. The nomination signals Washington’s intent to sustain and deepen diplomatic engagement with Islamabad amid growing cooperation in trade, investment and regional security. The nomination, announced by the White House yesterday, comes at a time when Pakistan-US relations have gained renewed momentum, with both countries exploring avenues for expanded economic cooperation and closer coordination on regional and international issues. Pakistan has also emerged as an important diplomatic interlocutor in efforts to facilitate a resolution of the US-Iran conflict, adding to the significance of sustained engagement between Islamabad and Washington. In announcing the nomination, the White House said: “Natalie Baker, of Texas, a Career Member of the Senior Foreign Service, Class of Minister-Counselor, to be Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the United States of America to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.” Baker’s nomination has been forwarded to the US Senate for consideration and confirmation. She will formally assume the ambassadorial position following the completion of the confirmation process. A seasoned American diplomat, Baker has been heading the US diplomatic mission in Pakistan as chargé d’affaires since January 2025. She previously served as deputy chief of mission at the US Embassy in Islamabad, joining the mission in August 2024. She assumed leadership of the embassy following the departure of Donald Blome, the last US ambassador to Pakistan to have been confirmed by the Senate. Her nomination is expected to provide continuity in Washington’s diplomatic representation and engagement with Islamabad, particularly as the two countries seek to build on recent progress in bilateral relations. Baker has been closely involved in diplomatic engagement with Pakistani officials on a range of issues, including trade negotiations, investment opportunities and regional developments. Her elevation to the ambassadorial position is expected to strengthen the institutional framework for bilateral dialogue and provide greater diplomatic momentum to ongoing initiatives. The renewed engagement between Pakistan and the United States has increasingly focused on expanding economic ties, encouraging investment and exploring opportunities for cooperation in areas of mutual interest. Regional security and diplomatic efforts to promote stability have also remained important elements of the bilateral relationship. Baker brings extensive diplomatic experience and academic credentials to the proposed assignment. She holds a bachelor’s degree from Princeton University and a master’s degree in public policy from Harvard University. She is also a graduate of the US National War College. Her nomination comes against the backdrop of efforts by Islamabad and Washington to move beyond past differences and pursue a more constructive and mutually beneficial relationship, with economic cooperation and regional diplomacy emerging as key areas of engagement.

headline: Why don’t you resign, CM Maryam hits back at federal ministers after corruption allegations
description: LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday challenged ministers levelling corruption allegations against the provincial government to resign from
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Tuesday challenged ministers levelling corruption allegations against the provincial government to resign from their cabinet positions, saying those who had reservations about the administration should not continue to be part of it.

Without naming anyone, she referred to Federal Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain, who recently accused the Maryam Nawaz-led government of widespread corruption and questioned its development priorities.

“If some people have objections and are levelling allegations of corruption against the Punjab government, why don’t they resign from the cabinet?” she asked while addressing a Honhaar Scholarship and laptop distribution ceremony at Government Comprehensive High School in Jhelum.

Her remarks followed her assertion that Punjab’s governance and accountability practices were different from those in other provinces. While saying she would not comment on the affairs of other provinces, as their respective governments were answerable to their people, she claimed that Punjab was the only province where the chief minister pursued a new corruption case every day.

Maryam, however, clarified that she had never claimed corruption had been completely eliminated from Punjab. She maintained that there had been no corruption in the development projects worth trillions of rupees launched by her government over the past three years.

She said she is answerable to the people for the expenditure of public money and would not spare any minister or government official if evidence of corruption or bribery was brought forward.

The chief minister said political narratives, allegations and criticism had a limited shelf life, arguing that public service and development work ultimately determined electoral success.

Referring to recent local elections in Sahiwal and Gujranwala, she said the PML-N had secured victories despite opposition parties joining hands against her government. “No matter how much you talk or how many claims you make, if you have not served the people, there comes a day when you are deprived of public support,” she said.

Maryam believed attempts were being made to distract her as the next general elections approached, but she remained focused on delivering public services. She maintained that her government had broken the tradition of concentrating development spending in major cities, citing the expansion of the Green Bus service to Jhelum, Khushab, Layyah, Bhakkar, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur and Multan.

The chief minister also highlighted the establishment of Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence, saying the institutions would offer facilities comparable to expensive private schools, including air-conditioned classrooms, computer and artificial intelligence laboratories, science laboratories and qualified faculty.

Praising Education Minister Rana Sikandar Hayat, she announced that 300 such schools would be established across the province, with work on the initiative in Jhelum scheduled to begin on December 15.

She further said cardiac treatment facilities were being established in 25 cities where such services had previously been unavailable. Patients visiting catheterisation laboratories (cath labs) at public hospitals would receive procedures, including angiograms, angioplasty, stenting and pacemaker implantation, free of charge.

Cancer hospitals were also being established at every divisional headquarters, she said, adding that the country’s first government-run cancer hospital was being built in Lahore.

The chief minister said her government believed in performance rather than rhetoric. The PML-N repeatedly returned to power because of its public service, she added. “Popularity is reflected in public support. People vote for service, not political narratives.”

Referring to the Lillah-Jhelum Road project, she said some people would now claim ownership of the initiative. “If it was your project, why did you not complete it during your four-year government? They are good at talking but fail to deliver.”

She said her government faced criticism whenever it undertook development work, but remained committed to fulfilling the aspirations of young people. “Let children dream; Maryam Nawaz will work day and night to turn their dreams into reality.”

Addressing female students, she urged them to move forward confidently and not allow anyone to tell them that certain professions or achievements were beyond their reach.

The chief minister said she felt grateful to Allah when she watched videos of students opening their laptops. “I thank Allah that our children’s hands are holding laptops, not sticks, stones and bombs.”

Congratulating the parents of talented students, she said deserving students were being rewarded for their hard work. Parents sent their children to educational institutions with countless dreams, and those who fulfilled their aspirations deserved recognition.

She said more than 100,000 scooters were being provided to students across Punjab, adding that recipients would also receive proper training. Students were being provided free travel facilities on Green Buses across the province.

Maryam Nawaz said 300 Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence were being established throughout Punjab. Referring to the school in Attock, she said a private grammar school and a government-run Nawaz Sharif School of Eminence were located side by side, but the government school offered much better facilities.

She challenged critics to identify a public-sector school outside Punjab that matched the standard of the Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence. The schools featured air-conditioned classrooms, modern laboratories and highly qualified faculty, facilities that were not even available at some private schools charging Rs100,000 in fees.

She said 50,000 schools across Punjab were providing education to millions of children. “Education is the best investment because every child is an ambassador of Pakistan.” The success of children would not only bring happiness to their parents but also benefit the country and nation, she added.

The chief minister said her government had broken the longstanding tradition of restricting development projects to major cities. She had spent entire days in Sahiwal, Attock and Mandi Bahauddin and would do the same in Jhelum. Young people were previously misled through narratives, but today they could see development taking place for themselves, she added.

“The Green Buses operating in Lahore and Rawalpindi are the same as those running in Khushab, Layyah and Bhakkar. There is no discrimination.” She said thousands of kilometres of roads had been constructed, with more development work carried out in smaller cities than in Lahore.

She said patients were receiving free stents, pacemakers and other cardiac treatment at the Jhelum Cath Lab. “Could anyone have imagined receiving such treatment in Jhelum in the past?”

Cath labs had been launched in 25 smaller districts, while Punjab’s largest public-sector cancer hospital was being established in Lahore, she added.

Recalling an example, she said a driver working in Dubai had travelled from Faisalabad to Jhelum on the advice of his sister to receive a heart stent. In the past, patients from Jhelum had to travel to Rawalpindi or Lahore for cardiac treatment. “Did people from major cities ever travel to smaller cities for medical treatment before?”

The chief minister said loans had been provided for 250,000 houses under the Apni Chhat, Apna Ghar programme over the past one-and-a-half to two years. She had recently met a woman in Jhelum who previously paid Rs15,000 in rent but was now paying an instalment of Rs14,000 for her own house.

She said hundreds of families who lacked financial resources had managed to construct their homes within months through the loan scheme. “Why were laptops, scholarships, cath labs and housing loans not provided in the past? Earlier, news from smaller cities highlighted problems; today, it highlights development.”

She also praised the newly developed market in Jhelum, saying its beauty and facilities could rival those of markets in major cities.

Maryam Nawaz said her government had established a system in which no personal reference, recommendation or influence was required, and all services were provided purely on merit. “My promise is that if you deserve promotion on merit, no power in the world can stop your progress.”

She said government jobs in Punjab were being given to deserving poor candidates on merit rather than to wealthy individuals through personal recommendations.

Referring to an incident in which a salesgirl was allegedly assaulted at a garment shop, she said the person responsible would remember the strong response from the police. She added that, for the first time, the Punjab government was standing with ordinary citizens and would continue to do so.

“No influential person can dare to assault a poor citizen now. Arrogance of power will not be tolerated under the Maryam Nawaz government,” she said.

She said some self-proclaimed intellectuals were uncomfortable with the government’s policies because the administration was standing with poor people and ensuring justice. There were so many development projects in every city of Punjab that even after spending an entire day there, she could inspect only 30 percent of them.

Referring to the recent by-elections in Gujranwala and Sahiwal, the chief minister said all political opponents had joined forces, while proscribed organisations had also made every effort to influence the outcome. However, the PML-N had emerged victorious.

“People have grown tired of rhetoric and empty promises. No political narrative can compete with public service,” she said.

She added that people were increasingly preferring government hospitals and schools over private institutions because of improvements in public-sector facilities.

Expressing her commitment to expanding quality education, she said she wanted every child in Punjab to benefit from the Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence model.

The chief minister said opposition parties were intensifying their activities as the next elections approached, but had failed to deliver any meaningful development during their tenure. “In just three years, we have initiated projects worth billions and trillions of rupees.”

While saying she would not comment on the affairs of other provinces, as their respective governments were answerable to their people, she claimed that Punjab was the only province where the chief minister pursued a new corruption case every day.

Maryam, however, clarified that she had never claimed corruption had been completely eliminated from Punjab. She maintained that there had been no corruption in the development projects worth trillions of rupees launched by her government over the past three years.

She said she is answerable to the people for the expenditure of public money and would not spare any minister or government official if evidence of corruption or bribery was brought forward.

The chief minister said political narratives, allegations and criticism had a limited shelf life, arguing that public service and development work ultimately determined electoral success.

Referring to recent local elections in Sahiwal and Gujranwala, she said the PML-N had secured victories despite opposition parties joining hands against her government. “No matter how much you talk or how many claims you make, if you have not served the people, there comes a day when you are deprived of public support,” she said.

Maryam believed attempts were being made to distract her as the next general elections approached, but she remained focused on delivering public services. She maintained that her government had broken the tradition of concentrating development spending in major cities, citing the expansion of the Green Bus service to Jhelum, Khushab, Layyah, Bhakkar, Rahim Yar Khan, Bahawalpur and Multan.

The chief minister also highlighted the establishment of Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence, saying the institutions would offer facilities comparable to expensive private schools, including air-conditioned classrooms, computer and artificial intelligence laboratories, science laboratories and qualified faculty.

Praising Education Minister Rana Sikandar Hayat, she announced that 300 such schools would be established across the province, with work on the initiative in Jhelum scheduled to begin on December 15.

She further said cardiac treatment facilities were being established in 25 cities where such services had previously been unavailable. Patients visiting catheterisation laboratories (cath labs) at public hospitals would receive procedures, including angiograms, angioplasty, stenting and pacemaker implantation, free of charge.

Cancer hospitals were also being established at every divisional headquarters, she said, adding that the country’s first government-run cancer hospital was being built in Lahore.

Referring to the Lillah-Jhelum Road project, she said some people would now claim ownership of the initiative. “If it was your project, why did you not complete it during your four-year government? They are good at talking but fail to deliver.”

She said her government faced criticism whenever it undertook development work, but remained committed to fulfilling the aspirations of young people. “Let children dream; Maryam Nawaz will work day and night to turn their dreams into reality.”

Addressing female students, she urged them to move forward confidently and not allow anyone to tell them that certain professions or achievements were beyond their reach.

The chief minister said she felt grateful to Allah when she watched videos of students opening their laptops. “I thank Allah that our children’s hands are holding laptops, not sticks, stones and bombs.”

Congratulating the parents of talented students, she said deserving students were being rewarded for their hard work. Parents sent their children to educational institutions with countless dreams, and those who fulfilled their aspirations deserved recognition.

She said more than 100,000 scooters were being provided to students across Punjab, adding that recipients would also receive proper training. Students were being provided free travel facilities on Green Buses across the province.

Referring to the school in Attock, she said a private grammar school and a government-run Nawaz Sharif School of Eminence were located side by side, but the government school offered much better facilities.

She challenged critics to identify a public-sector school outside Punjab that matched the standard of the Nawaz Sharif Schools of Eminence. The schools featured air-conditioned classrooms, modern laboratories and highly qualified faculty, facilities that were not even available at some private schools charging Rs100,000 in fees.

She said 50,000 schools across Punjab were providing education to millions of children. “Education is the best investment because every child is an ambassador of Pakistan.” The success of children would not only bring happiness to their parents but also benefit the country and nation, she added.

Young people were previously misled through narratives, but today they could see development taking place for themselves, she added.

“The Green Buses operating in Lahore and Rawalpindi are the same as those running in Khushab, Layyah and Bhakkar. There is no discrimination.” She said thousands of kilometres of roads had been constructed, with more development work carried out in smaller cities than in Lahore.

Cath labs had been launched in 25 smaller districts, while Punjab’s largest public-sector cancer hospital was being established in Lahore, she added.

She said hundreds of families who lacked financial resources had managed to construct their homes within months through the loan scheme. “Why were laptops, scholarships, cath labs and housing loans not provided in the past? headline: Saudi Air defenses intercept Houthi cruise, ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh
description: RIYADH - Air defenses intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Houthi militia toward Riyadh, the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen
author: News Desk
article_text: RIYADH - Air defenses intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Houthi militia toward Riyadh, the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen announced Tuesday. The coalition also reported that Saudi air defenses had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis toward the capital. Saudi Civil Defense activated an early warning alert in Riyadh, warning residents of a potential threat and urging them to follow official safety instructions. In a separate incident, Saudi air defenses thwarted another ballistic missile launched by the Houthi militia toward the Kingdom’s southern region, according to the coalition. The interceptions came shortly after the coalition announced the destruction of a Houthi facility used to assemble and produce ballistic missile components.

headline: Imam’s 137, Abdullah’s 112 lead day two action in QAT Gold
description: LAHORE - Centuries by Imam-ul-Haq, Abdullah Shafique and Azeem Bari high-lighted the second day of the second-round matches in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Centuries by Imam-ul-Haq, Abdullah Shafique and Azeem Bari high-lighted the second day of the second-round matches in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Gold, while Rawalpindi and Abbottabad registered emphatic innings victories in the Silver competition on Tuesday. At Diamond Cricket Ground, Imam remained unbeaten on 137 as Multan were dis-missed for 216. Asad Umar claimed 6-45. Karachi Blues reached 72-1 in their second innings. Abdullah struck 112 to guide Sialkot Blues to 316-9 against Faisalabad’s 222. Azeem scored 105 as Islamabad reached 403-6 against Lahore Whites. FATA were bowled out for 230, while Pesh-awar Blues reached 150-4, with Shaheen Shah Afridi taking three.

headline: Netanyahu repeats call for unity government
description: JERUSALEM - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu once again called for the establishment of a national unity government in an address to the newly
author: News Desk
article_text: JERUSALEM - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu once again called for the establishment of a national unity government in an address to the newly sworn-in Knesset, while launching a fierce attack on the Arab parties Ra’am and the Joint List, accusing both of seeking Israel’s destruction and warning his political rivals against relying on their support to form a government. Having lost his parliamentary majority in last month’s elections, and after President Isaac Herzog handed Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, Netanyahu has continued a campaign he pursued throughout the election season to delegitimize the Arab parties and portray them as supporters of terrorism, in an apparent effort to undermine the ability of Eisenkot and his allies to form a government with their backing. “Iran is working to revive the nuclear threat. The only way to permanently eliminate this existential threat is to overthrow the ayatollahs’ regime,” Netanyahu declares in a speech following the swearing-in of the new Knesset.

headline: We’re preparing future leaders and champions for Pakistan: Moazzam Klair
description: LAHORE - Celebrating young talent, sporting excellence and the importance of physical education, The Educators Elite Campus Annual Sports Gala 2026 was held in
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Celebrating young talent, sporting excellence and the importance of physical education, The Educators Elite Campus Annual Sports Gala 2026 was held in great style at LDA Hockey Stadium, Johar Town, Lahore, in collaboration with ACTIVIT. The colourful sporting extravaganza was graced by Rd. Rizwan Aftab Ahmed, CEO ACTIVIT and Director, National Hospital DHA Lahore, as the chief guest. He was warmly welcomed by Moazzam Khan Klair, CEO The Educators Elite Campus and PCF General Secretary, Wahhab Ali Klair, Executive Director, and members of the school’s management. The opening ceremony featured the release of colourful balloons and pigeons, symbolising peace, unity and sportsmanship. Students showcased their sporting abilities through various competitions, energetic aerobic performances, a commando display, welcome songs and entertaining presentations, while enthusiastic parents added to the festive atmosphere. Addressing the gathering, chief guest Rd. Rizwan Aftab Ahmed appreciated the institution’s commitment to promoting sports alongside academic education. Emphasising the importance of grassroots sports development, he observed that educational institutions could play a significant role in identifying and nurturing future sporting talent. He expressed hope that platforms such as The Educators Elite Campus would help produce future champions like Arshad Nadeem and Nooh Dastgir Butt through professional training, proper guidance and institutional support. During the prize distribution ceremony, Rd. Rizwan Aftab Ahmed, accompanied by Moazzam Khan Klair and Wahhab Ali Klair, presented medals and certificates to outstanding performers and position holders in recognition of their achievements, dedication and sporting spirit.

In his remarks, Moazzam Khan Klair reaffirmed the institution’s commitment to developing well-rounded students through a balanced focus on academics, sports, character building, leadership and physical fitness. He thanked the chief guest for his encouragement and valuable support. A commemorative souvenir was also presented to Rd. Rizwan Aftab Ahmed as a token of appreciation. The gala concluded with a renewed commitment to promoting sporting culture, discovering young talent and preparing the next generation of national and international athletes.

headline: US delivers summonses for India’s NSA, ex-RAW chief in Pannun assassination lawsuit
description: ISLAMABAD - The United States has formally transmitted court summons and legal documents to the Indian government through diplomatic channels in connection
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The United States has formally transmitted court summons and legal documents to the Indian government through diplomatic channels in connection with a civil lawsuit alleging an Indian government-backed conspiracy to assassinate Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York, bringing India’s National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and former intelligence officials under renewed legal scrutiny. The US State Department confirmed that the summons, complaint and notice of suit were delivered to the Indian Embassy in Washington through a diplomatic note on October 9, 2026, following a request from the US District Court for the Southern District of New York. The lawsuit, filed by Pannun in September 2024, names the Government of India, National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, former Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief Samant Goel, former RAW officer Vikram Yadav, Indian national Nikhil Gupta and other individuals as defendants. The case alleges their involvement in a conspiracy to orchestrate Pannun’s assassination on American soil. The allegations against the named officials remain to be adjudicated by the court. The diplomatic transmission marks a significant procedural development in the case, although the US State Department has clarified that its role in delivering the legal documents does not constitute an endorsement of the allegations or a position on their merits. The development comes against the backdrop of a separate US criminal prosecution in which Indian national Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty in February 2026 to three charges, including murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering.The US prosecutors alleged that Gupta had worked with an Indian government employee, identified as Vikash Yadav, who recruited him in May 2023 to arrange Pannun’s assassination in New York. Gupta’s guilty plea has added a significant dimension to the US investigation into the alleged assassination conspiracy. India has previously distanced itself from the alleged plot, maintaining that such actions are contrary to government policy. The allegations of Indian involvement in transnational operations targeting Sikh activists have remained a source of diplomatic tensions between India and Western countries. The latest US legal development has brought renewed attention to allegations concerning the activities of Indian intelligence operatives beyond India’s borders. The October 9 diplomatic transmission concerned the lawsuit against the Government of India. The individual defendants, including Ajit Doval and Samant Goel, are separately named in the civil case. The transmission of legal papers does not establish their liability or prove the allegations.

headline: Bilawal urges PM to restore confidence of allies, opposition parties
description: KARACHI - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari on Tuesday said that the country’s politics must be reset in order to confront the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari on Tuesday said that the country’s politics must be reset in order to confront the ‘economic disaster’ and provide relief to the people.

Instead of stirring up fresh disputes, he said, the federal government should restore the confidence of its allies and the opposition.

While addressing a ceremony in connection with completion of one million houses in the first phase of the Sindh government’s flagship project to build 2.1 million homes for victims of the 2022 floods, Bilawal Bhutto went on to say that political parties, through this reset, will have to work together rather than fight one another.

The people of Pakistan do not want to hear today about how we should fight each other, he said. “They do not want to see how, at Islamabad’s behest or at the wish of Lahore’s business class, our system is manipulated. This is not the time for such things,” he said. “We need a political reset, and I invite the Prime Minister first to restore the confidence of his allies, and then to restore the confidence of the political parties sitting in opposition, instead of starting new quarrels with them.”

Until we face the economic crisis together, he said, we will not be able to save our people from this hardship. Until such conditions emerge at the national level, he said, the people’s government of Sindh will keep taking steps, within its limited resources, such as building homes for the homeless and making landless women the owners of land.

The ceremony was attended by Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, provincial ministers, members of the assembly, and diplomatic, social and business figures.

According to a press release issued by Media Cell Bilawal House, the PPP chairman said that critics should learn from the PPP how to serve the people rather than criticise without cause. Citing a briefing by the SPHF, he said the people’s government of Sindh had set a world record by building one million of the planned 2.1 million homes, surpassing the previous record held by the government of Nepal, which built 700,000. “So the Sindh government has built one million homes so far, and God willing, once this project is complete, we will build two million more,” he said.

Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari pointed out that when the two-million-home project was launched, the country was dealing with the devastation of a massive natural disaster, and that today, as the project passes an important milestone, the whole world, Pakistan included, is caught in an “economic disaster”. He said the project is also giving the poor of Sindh “a measure of economic security” amid the present economic crisis, record inflation, poverty and unemployment.

He said that during this economic crisis, people across the country are looking to political parties and governments. They are not looking to see how they will be set against one another or how the politics of hatred and division will be spread, he said; they are looking to see who stands with them in this crisis. He said that, at the very least, he could tell the people of Sindh that every step the provincial government takes is aimed at delivering relief to the public and lightening the economic burden on their shoulders.

He said some politicians believe the country will progress by making the rich and business classes richer, running the country as they dictate, and resetting the system. “I believe the reset that is needed is this: if this country is run on the word of the poor and the homeless rather than the rich and business classes, not only will the country progress, our economy will progress too,” he said.

Bilawal lauded Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah for his outstanding performance on the project to build homes for two million flood-affected families. He said that when the work began, many people did not believe it could be done. Recalling the start of the floods in 2022, he said he was in Larkana at the time, and the rain turned into a severe flood before his eyes. “It felt as though I was passing over the sea,” he said.

Bilawal said that as foreign minister he had arranged financing for rebuilding victims’ homes in flood-affected areas of all four provinces, including Sindh. He added that in Balochistan the federal government took on the responsibility for building such homes, where only 30,000 have been built so far, while the PPP government in Sindh has already built one million. “We are criticised, our character is attacked, and Sindh is attacked the most. That is because everyone knows that Sindh does more than any other province to defend not only its own rights but the rights of all provinces, and that is why you are attacked the most,” he said. He declared that those who criticise without cause link every issue to the NFC, devolution and the 18th Constitutional Amendment, which is contrary to the facts.

He said that Sindh has faced great hardship because of repeated floods and torrential rains, including in the education sector. He pointed out that 50 percent of Sindh’s schools were badly affected in the last flood. The other provinces have not faced such difficulties, he said. He said that in the recent past there was even a prime minister who, instead of helping flood-hit Sindh, said, “Sindh is not ours anyway.” “But Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, at least, did not let us feel that,” he said.

KARACHI - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari on Tuesday said that the country’s politics must be reset in order to confront the ‘economic disaster’ and provide relief to the people. 

Instead of stirring up fresh disputes, he said, the federal government should restore the confidence of its allies and the opposition.

While addressing a ceremony in connection with completion of one million houses in the first phase of the Sindh government’s flagship project to build 2.1 million homes for victims of the 2022 floods, Bilawal Bhutto went on to say that political parties, through this reset, will have to work together rather than fight one another.

The people of Pakistan do not want to hear today about how we should fight each other, he said. “They do not want to see how, at Islamabad’s behest or at the wish of Lahore’s business class, our system is manipulated. This is not the time for such things,” he said. “We need a political reset, and I invite the Prime Minister first to restore the confidence of his allies, and then to restore the confidence of the political parties sitting in opposition, instead of starting new quarrels with them.”

Until we face the economic crisis together, he said, we will not be able to save our people from this hardship. Until such conditions emerge at the national level, he said, the people’s government of Sindh will keep taking steps, within its limited resources, such as building homes for the homeless and making landless women the owners of land.

Court rejects plea to drop terrorism charge in Group Captain’s murder case

The ceremony was attended by Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah, provincial ministers, members of the assembly, and diplomatic, social and business figures.

According to a press release issued by Media Cell Bilawal House, the PPP chairman said that critics should learn from the PPP how to serve the people rather than criticise without cause. Citing a briefing by the SPHF, he said the people’s government of Sindh had set a world record by building one million of the planned 2.1 million homes, surpassing the previous record held by the government of Nepal, which built 700,000. “So the Sindh government has built one million homes so far, and God willing, once this project is complete, we will build two million more,” he said.

He said the project is also giving the poor of Sindh “a measure of economic security” amid the present economic crisis, record inflation, poverty and unemployment.

He said that during this economic crisis, people across the country are looking to political parties and governments. They are not looking to see how they will be set against one another or how the politics of hatred and division will be spread, he said; they are looking to see who stands with them in this crisis. He said that, at the very least, he could tell the people of Sindh that every step the provincial government takes is aimed at delivering relief to the public and lightening the economic burden on their shoulders.

He said some politicians believe the country will progress by making the rich and business classes richer, running the country as they dictate, and resetting the system. “I believe the reset that is needed is this: if this country is run on the word of the poor and the homeless rather than the rich and business classes, not only will the country progress, our economy will progress too,” he said.

Bilawal lauded Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah for his outstanding performance on the project to build homes for two million flood-affected families. He said that when the work began, many people did not believe it could be done. Recalling the start of the floods in 2022, he said he was in Larkana at the time, and the rain turned into a severe flood before his eyes. “It felt as though I was passing over the sea,” he said.

Bilawal said that as foreign minister he had arranged financing for rebuilding victims’ homes in flood-affected areas of all four provinces, including Sindh. He added that in Balochistan the federal government took on the responsibility for building such homes, where only 30,000 have been built so far, while the PPP government in Sindh has already built one million. “We are criticised, our character is attacked, and Sindh is attacked the most. That is because everyone knows that Sindh does more than any other province to defend not only its own rights but the rights of all provinces, and that is why you are attacked the most,” he said. He declared that those who criticise without cause link every issue to the NFC, devolution and the 18th Constitutional Amendment, which is contrary to the facts.

He said that Sindh has faced great hardship because of repeated floods and torrential rains, including in the education sector. He pointed out that 50 percent of Sindh’s schools were badly affected in the last flood. The other provinces have not faced such difficulties, he said. He said that in the recent past there was even a prime minister who, instead of helping flood-hit Sindh, said, “Sindh is not ours anyway.” “But Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, at least, did not let us feel that,” he said.

headline: Lahore Qalandars appoint Aminul Islam as high-performance advisor
description: LAHORE - Lahore Qalandars have appointed former Bangladesh captain Aminul Islam as an advisor to the franchise’s High-Performance Centres, bringing his
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Lahore Qalandars have appointed former Bangladesh captain Aminul Islam as an advisor to the franchise’s High-Performance Centres, bringing his extensive international cricket and development experience into the organisation’s player development programme. In his new role, Islam will provide strategic guidance on strengthening the Qalandars’ High-Performance Centres, with particular focus on improving player development structures, enhancing coaching practices and creating more opportunities for emerging cricketers to progress towards higher levels of the game. The appointment reflects Lahore Qalandars’ continued emphasis on nurturing young talent and building a sustainable pathway for aspiring players. The franchise also aims to benefit from Islam’s experience and understanding of cricket development across the region, particularly through his work in Bangladesh and at the international level. Islam brings considerable administrative, developmental and playing experience to the position. He served as Cricket Development Manager, Asia, at the International Cricket Council (ICC) from 2015 to 2025 and previously worked as a Cricket Development Officer at the Asian Cricket Council (ACC). He also served as President of the Bangladesh Cricket Board, gaining valuable experience in cricket administration and the development of the game.

During his playing career, Islam represented Bangladesh in international cricket from 1988 to 2002 and captained the national side at the 1999 ICC Cricket World Cup. His experience as an international player, team leader and cricket administrator is expected to add valuable insight to the Qalandars’ high-performance and talent-development initiatives.

headline: Bangladesh HC visits PFF, discusses bilateral football cooperation
description: LAHORE - Pakistan and Bangladesh have explored fresh avenues for strengthening bilateral football relations, with a focus on player and coaching exchanges,
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Pakistan and Bangladesh have explored fresh avenues for strengthening bilateral football relations, with a focus on player and coaching exchanges, technical cooperation and joint development initiatives, during a meeting between Bangladesh High Commissioner to Pakistan Muhammad Iqbal Hussain Khan and Pakistan Football Federation (PFF) officials. The High Commissioner visited the PFF headquarters, where he was warmly received by Chief Operating Officer Muhammad Shahid Niaz Khokhar. The meeting provided an opportunity to discuss ways of developing closer sporting links between the two countries, which share longstanding bonds of friendship and cooperation. During the discussions, Khokhar outlined PFF President Syed Mohsen Gilani’s vision for the advancement of football in Pakistan. He highlighted the federation’s commitment to strengthening football governance, improving infrastructure and expanding the game’s reach through a sustainable development strategy. He also emphasised the importance of promoting grassroots football, identifying and nurturing young talent, and creating greater opportunities for women and youth to participate in the sport. The vision, he explained, aims to establish a stronger foundation for the game and create a clear development pathway for aspiring footballers across the country. The two sides also discussed practical measures to enhance football cooperation between Pakistan and Bangladesh. Proposed areas of collaboration included exchange programmes for players, coaches and technical officials, sharing technical knowledge and expertise, and arranging joint initiatives to support the development of football in both countries. Such exchanges could provide players and coaching personnel with valuable exposure, encourage the sharing of best practices and help strengthen professional links between the football communities of the two nations. The meeting highlighted the potential of sport, particularly football, to bring the two friendly countries closer and translate their longstanding diplomatic relations into meaningful sporting partnerships.

The PFF expressed its commitment to developing stronger institutional ties with Bangladesh and pursuing mutually beneficial initiatives aimed at promoting the game, improving technical standards and creating new opportunities for football development in both countries.

headline: Pakistan to face Bangladesh in U19 Asia Cup semifinals
description: AL AMERAT - Defending champions Pakistan will face Bangladesh in the first semifinal of the ACC Men’s U19 Asia Cup 2026 after completing their
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: AL AMERAT - Defending champions Pakistan will face Bangladesh in the first semifinal of the ACC Men’s U19 Asia Cup 2026 after completing their group-stage campaign at the top of Group A with a 101-run victory over Nepal on Tuesday. The Green Shirts collected six points from three matches, finishing with a net run rate of 1.186 to book a place in Thursday’s last-four contest at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground (Ministry Turf 2). Pakistan made an impressive start to their title defence, opening with a nine-wicket win over the United Arab Emirates (UAE). They then defeated arch-rivals India by three wickets in a closely fought encounter on Sunday, before sealing their group campaign with another convincing result against Nepal. Their first-place finish means they will take on Bangladesh, who ended the Group B league stage in second position with four points from three matches. The contest will offer Pakistan an opportunity to move closer to retaining the continental crown. The second semifinal will feature India and Afghanistan at Turf 1 of the same venue, also on Thursday. India secured the final place in the knockout stage after beating the UAE by 70 runs in their concluding group fixture on Tuesday. The previous edition’s runners-up began their campaign with a 10-wicket victory over Nepal but were subsequently beaten by Pakistan. Their win over the UAE ensured qualification and set up a meeting with Group B leaders Afghanistan. Afghanistan topped Group B with six points from three matches and a net run rate of 3.176. They confirmed their semi-final berth on Monday with a 106-run triumph over Sri Lanka, underlining their credentials as title contenders. With the group stage complete, attention turns to Thursday’s knockout matches, where Pakistan and Bangladesh will meet in the opening semifinal, followed by India’s clash with Afghanistan. The two winning teams will advance to the final, scheduled to be played at Turf 2 of the Al Amerat Cricket Ground on November 14.

headline: Saqib’s double strike puts Pakistan in command as Sri Lanka reach 114-3
description: RAWALPINDI - Pakistan strengthened their grip on the opening Test against Sri Lanka after declaring their first innings at 434-9, before debutant pacer Saqib
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: RAWALPINDI - Pakistan strengthened their grip on the opening Test against Sri Lanka after declaring their first innings at 434-9, before debutant pacer Saqib Khan struck twice to leave the visitors struggling at 114-3 at stumps on the second day at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday. Sri Lanka, who still trail by 320 runs, made a disastrous start to their reply as Mohammad Abbas dismissed opener Pasindu Sooriyabandara for a duck in the third over. Saqib then claimed his maiden Test wicket, removing Dinesh Chandimal for one to reduce the visitors to 12-2. Lahiru Udara and Kamindu Mendis steadied the innings with a 53-run stand. Udara looked positive during his 42 off 52 balls, striking seven boundaries, while Mendis held firm at the other end. Saqib, however, ended the partnership by dismissing Udara at 65-3, completing an impressive two-wicket haul. Dhananjaya de Silva joined Mendis and the pair prevented further damage, adding an unbeaten 49 runs to take Sri Lanka beyond the 100-run mark. Mendis was 40 not out, while De Silva had made 22 when bad light forced an early close to proceedings, with 27.1 overs bowled. The two will resume on the third day with Sri Lanka seeking to narrow the substantial deficit. Earlier, Pakistan resumed at 281-5 and extended their total through a valuable sixth-wicket partnership between Saud Shakeel and Ghazi Ghori. The pair added 96 runs, taking the hosts past 300 before Dilshan Madushanka dismissed Ghori for a useful 48 off 72 deliveries, including two boundaries. Shakeel continued to anchor the innings, sharing a 44-run stand with debutant Arafat Minhas. He fell seven runs short of a century, scoring 93 from 199 balls with nine fours, when Asitha Fernando had him caught by wicketkeeper Kusal Mendis. Minhas then took charge, reaching his maiden Test half-century in an impressive debut. He scored 52 off 72 balls, hitting nine boundaries and a six, before Madushanka ended his innings. Razaullah contributed 10, and Pakistan captain Babar Azam declared at 434-9 after 106.3 overs. Fernando and Madushanka led Sri Lanka’s attack with three wickets each, while Lahiru Kumara, Milan Rathnayake and Sonal Dinusha claimed one apiece.

headline: PM Shehbaz performs dome placement of Chashma-5 Nuclear Power Plant
description: MIANWALI - Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called for building an economically dominant, energy-independent and environmentally resilient Pakistan,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
MIANWALI - Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday called for building an economically dominant, energy-independent and environmentally resilient Pakistan, declaring that the country will harness its resources, technology and human capital to secure a prosperous future.

Addressing the dome placement ceremony of the Chashma-5 Nuclear Power Plant (C-5) here, the prime minister described the milestone as a reflection of Pakistan’s determination to shape its own future through hard work, technological advancement and strategic partnerships.

Prime Minister Shehbaz, while emphasising the importance of energy security, said Chashma-5 represented much more than steel and concrete—rather, it was a promise of clean, reliable, and affordable electricity that would strengthen the national economy and improve people’s lives.

He said that nuclear power would reduce Pakistan’s dependence on imported fuels and international price fluctuations while ensuring a stable electricity supply for industries, hospitals, educational institutions and households.

“Pakistan will not wait for anyone, but will build its own future through its hard work and untiring efforts,” the prime minister recalled, referring to his commitment at the project’s groundbreaking ceremony in July 2023.

He noted with satisfaction that the dome had been installed less than three and a half years after the groundbreaking, ahead of schedule, and expressed confidence that the project would also be commissioned earlier than planned.

The prime minister stressed that Pakistan, as a climate-vulnerable country, had a particular responsibility to pursue energy solutions that simultaneously advance economic development and protect the environment.

Highlighting the strategic importance of national security for economic progress, he said no country could build a prosperous future without first safeguarding its present.

He acknowledged the role of the armed forces under the leadership of Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir in ensuring security and stability.

Referring to the country’s experience during Marka-e-Haq, the prime minister praised the professionalism, courage and resolve of the armed forces, saying a secure environment was essential for attracting investment, reviving the economy and accelerating socioeconomic development.

He also appreciated Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir’s support for the government’s economic revival and development initiatives.Underscoring Pakistan-China strategic cooperation, Prime Minister Shehbaz described Chashma-5 as another enduring symbol of the two countries’ all-weather friendship and their shared commitment to economic progress.

He said the project marked the seventh nuclear power unit China had helped Pakistan construct, reflecting the consistency and strength of bilateral cooperation across challenging times.

The prime minister conveyed his gratitude to Chinese President Xi Jinping, the Chinese government and the China National Nuclear Corporation for their continued support, acknowledging the contributions of Chinese engineers and their Pakistani counterparts.

He further stated that the second phase of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) would open new economic opportunities, strengthen strategic ties and contribute to a brighter future for both countries.

The prime minister while congratulating the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC), China Atomic Energy Authority, China National Nuclear Corporation, contractors, engineers, financial institutions and other stakeholders, also acknowledged the people of Mianwali for hosting the landmark project.

Concluding his address, Prime Minister Shehbaz reaffirmed his government’s commitment to building a Pakistan that is economically stronger, energy-secure and environmentally responsible, expressing hope that Chashma-5 would remain a lasting symbol of Pakistan-China friendship and shared aspirations for peace, stability and prosperity.

Earlier, PAEC Chairman highlighted nuclear energy’s growing contribution to Pakistan’s electricity mix and national energy security. He said the country’s nuclear power plants were safely and efficiently generating 3,530 megawatts of electricity, helping avoid approximately 15 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually.

Nuclear energy currently accounts for around 16.6 per cent of Pakistan’s electricity generation despite representing only 8.6 per cent of installed power capacity. Its contribution rises to approximately 26 per cent during winter.

The Chashma-5 project will have a generation capacity of 1,200 megawatts and is expected to begin electricity production in September 2030. The ceremony was attended by Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, senior Pakistani officials, Chinese representatives and officials from relevant organisations.

headline: Pakistan Railways reported 89 accidents in 10 months
description: ISLAMABAD - The National Assembly Standing Committee on Railways was Tuesday informed that Pakistan Railways suffered 89 accidents from 1st January to 2nd
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The National Assembly Standing Committee on Railways was Tuesday informed that Pakistan Railways suffered 89 accidents from 1st January to 2nd November 2026. The Railways had reported almost the same number of accidents (92) during the corresponding period of 2025. The Committee which met under the acting chairmanship of Ramesh Lal, MNA, at the Parliament House, was briefed on recent railway accidents across the country. The major causes of accidents included track-related issues, rolling stock defects, human errors, violations by road users, sabotage, natural calamities and other operational failures. The Ministry highlighted that ageing railway infrastructure, inadequate development funding, trespassing, violations at level crossings and foggy weather were among the contributing factors adding that Pakistan Railways is striving to reduce the accident ratio to below 0.19% under its strategic roadmap. The Committee also reviewed matters relating to Pakistan Railways, including the Railway Board Bill, 2026, encroachments on railway land in Karachi Division, and recent railway accidents across the country. The Committee considered the Bill titled “The Railway Board Bill, 2026, (Government Bill) and decided to defer its consideration until the next meeting of the Committee. The Committee was also briefed by the Ministry of Railways on the status of encroachments on railway land in Karachi Division. It was informed that, out of 19,594 acres of railway land, approximately 951.28 acres were under private encroachment, while 307 acres were under government encroachment. The Department reported that 363.907 acres of land had been retrieved during the last four years. Furthermore, during July to October 2026, encroachments covering approximately 8.992 acres were removed, with an estimated value of Rs. 305.67 million. The Ministry also shared a comprehensive schedule for the removal of further encroachments during November 2026. The Committee emphasized the importance of protecting valuable railway land from encroachments, ensuring effective coordination with provincial and local administrations, expediting land retrieval operations and taking concrete measures to improve railway safety. It also stressed the need for timely implementation of the Committee’s previous recommendations and further strengthening the overall operational efficiency of Pakistan Railways.

The Railways had reported almost the same number of accidents (92) during the corresponding period of 2025. The Committee which met under the acting chairmanship of Ramesh Lal, MNA, at the Parliament House, was briefed on recent railway accidents across the country. The major causes of accidents included track-related issues, rolling stock defects, human errors, violations by road users, sabotage, natural calamities and other operational failures.  The Ministry highlighted that ageing railway infrastructure, inadequate development funding, trespassing, violations at level crossings and foggy weather were among the contributing factors adding that Pakistan Railways is striving to reduce the accident ratio to below 0.19% under its strategic roadmap.          
The Committee also reviewed matters relating to Pakistan Railways, including the Railway Board Bill, 2026, encroachments on railway land in Karachi Division, and recent railway accidents across the country. The Committee considered the Bill titled “The Railway Board Bill, 2026, (Government Bill) and decided to defer its consideration until the next meeting of the Committee.  
The Committee was also briefed by the Ministry of Railways on the status of encroachments on railway land in Karachi Division. It was informed that, out of 19,594 acres of railway land, approximately 951.28 acres were under private encroachment, while 307 acres were under government encroachment. 
The Department reported that 363.907 acres of land had been retrieved during the last four years. Furthermore, during July to October 2026, encroachments covering approximately 8.992 acres were removed, with an estimated value of Rs. 305.67 million. The Ministry also shared a comprehensive schedule for the removal of further encroachments during November 2026. The Committee emphasized the importance of protecting valuable railway land from encroachments, ensuring effective coordination with provincial and local administrations, expediting land retrieval operations and taking concrete measures to improve railway safety. It also stressed the need for timely implementation of the Committee’s previous recommendations and further strengthening the overall operational efficiency of Pakistan Railways.

headline: Families spend at least 13% household income to keep daughters in public schools: Report
description: ISLAMABAD - The National Girls Education Financing Conference 2026, under the theme “Hazir: She’s Here. Is the Budget?” organized by the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The National Girls Education Financing Conference 2026, under the theme “Hazir: She’s Here. Is the Budget?” organized by the Pakistan Coalition for Education (PCE) in collaboration with Malala Fund was held in Islamabad. The conference highlighted the gap between public education financing and the costs families bear to keep girls in school. Discussions focused on recognising these costs in education planning and budgets, strengthening domestic resource mobilisation, and ensuring that a girl’s access to education should not depend on her family’s ability to pay. Dr Nishat Riaz, Chief Executive Officer, Malala Fund, while speaking on the occasion said that every budget must account for the real costs of keeping girls in school and address the intersecting barriers that limit their access, participation and transition. “While resource scarcity remains a constant challenge, governments must mobilise innovative financing, prioritise equitable allocations and ensure that every investment translates into meaningful opportunities for girls.” Zehra Arshad, Executive Director, Pakistan Coalition for Education stated that the decline in public education financing has shifted the cost onto families, who now spend an average of 13% of their household income to keep a daughter in a public secondary school. “When families bear the cost, the right to education stops being a right and becomes a compromise. Yet these out-of-pocket expenses remain invisible in public education budgets, which must account for the actual cost of keeping girls in school.” A girl-led panel discussion was also part of the proceedings. During this session, secondary-school-going Girl Champions provided first-hand accounts of financial and other barriers that affect girls’ ability to access and remain in school. The session was chaired by MNA Asia Naz Tanoli, who demanded a reduction in the education-related financial burden on households, improving school facilities and enhancing public investment in education During the policy session, Domestic Resource Mobilization for Girls’ Education: What Does “Free Education” Actually Mean? representatives from federal and provincial school education departments shared how each region had made efforts in FY2026-27 to enhance public investment in education but agreed that budgetary constraints remained the leading hurdle in realizing key education outcomes. MPA Ms. Nausheen Adnan, Parliamentary Secretary for Education, Punjab said, “Key education stakeholders including legislators and high level decisionmakers do not fully understand the economics of education. The education system needs to be fully decentralized to ensure that grassroots level actors are independent to make decisions in line with the unique realities of their specific area.” The conference also witnessed the launch of the report, “The Real Cost of Educating a Daughter: Out-of-pocket Costs of Girls’ Secondary Education in Pakistan’s Public Schools.” The study found that despite being constitutionally free, families must spend a minimum of Rs. 5,899 each month to keep their daughter in school. The conference called for education financing that goes beyond enrolment commitments to address the real costs of attendance, participation and completion. Its message was clear: when a girl is ready to learn, public financing must be ready to support her.

headline: Khelo Karachi inter school, collegiate girls games begin
description: KARACHI - The 2-day Khelo Karachi Inter-School and Collegiate Girls Games 2026 began on Tuesday, with participation of over 500 female students from more than
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - The 2-day Khelo Karachi Inter-School and Collegiate Girls Games 2026 began on Tuesday, with participation of over 500 female students from more than 35 government and private schools and colleges. The Khelo Karachi Girls Games 2026, consisted of tape ball cricket, badminton, futsal and table tennis competitions, being organized at Khatun-e-Pakistan Government Degree Girls College under the auspices of the Sindh Sports and Youth Affairs Department. In the opening ceremony, Secretary Sports Munawar Ali Mahesar, along with Director Sports Dr. Asad Ishaq and District Sports Officer East Karachi Syed Ismail Shah, formally inaugurated the games by releasing the game’s banner with colorful balloons in the air. The Sindh government initiative is aimed at promoting sports activities in schools, colleges and universities across the province and providing equal sports opportunities to male and female students to showcase their sporting talents. Secretary Sports Sindh Munawar Ali Mahesar, speaking on the occasion, said that organizing ‘Khelo Karachi: Inter-School and Collegiate Girls Games 2026’ is a practical manifestation of the Sindh government’s commitment to provide equal opportunities for female students and promote women’s sports. The Sindh government is expanding the scope of sports activities to schools, colleges and universities, so that the sporting talent of the youth in educational institutions, especially female students, can be brought to the fore and they are provided better opportunities to express their talents, he stated.

headline: Digital magazine ‘FUUAST Political Review’ launched
description: KARACHI -The Department of International Relations, Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences and Technology (FUUAST), Karachi, organized the launching
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI -The Department of International Relations, Federal Urdu University of Arts, Sciences and Technology (FUUAST), Karachi, organized the launching ceremony of its newly introduced digital magazine, “FUUAST Political Review”. The ceremony was attended by Member of the Provincial Assembly (MPA) Sindh and Jamaat-e-Islami leader Muhammad Farhan Farooq as the chief guest. Addressing the ceremony, MPA Muhammad Farhan Farooq said that students possess immense potential, knowledge and capabilities to change the direction of the country and transform Pakistan into a rapidly developing nation. He urged young people to utilize their abilities positively, contribute to society and play an active role in national development. The chief guest formally inaugurated the digital magazine by cutting the ribbon and distributed shields among students in recognition of their outstanding contributions to the magazine and the Department’s Students’ Council. In his welcome address, Dr. Syed Shahab Uddin, Head of the Department of International Relations, highlighted the department’s commitment to academic excellence, intellectual growth and promoting awareness of contemporary international political developments. Dr. Muhammad Azeem introduced FUUAST Political Review and explained its objectives and academic significance.
