headline: Four Pakistani students to participate in international Chemistry Olympiad 2027
description: KARACHI - The first week-long selection and training programme for the 59th International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO) 2027 has successfully concluded at the
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - The first week-long selection and training programme for the 59th International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO) 2027 has successfully concluded at the International Centre for Chemical and Biological Sciences (ICCBS), University of Karachi. As many as 44 students from across the country participated in the first training camp, organized under the National Science Talent Contest (NSTC), from October 31 to November 7, 2026, at the ICCBS. Following the completion of all training and selection phases, only four students will be selected to represent Pakistan at the International Chemistry Olympiad 2027. The primary objective of the programme is to assess students’ knowledge of chemistry, analytical abilities, problem-solving skills, and laboratory competencies to identify candidates for the subsequent selection stages. Prof. Dr. Muhammad Raza Shah, Director of ICCBS, congratulated the ICCBS experts, including Prof Dr Khalid M. Khan, Programme Coordinator, and Prof Dr M. Imran Malik, Deputy Programme Coordinator, on successfully conducting and completing the first phase of the training programme. He expressed confidence that the second and third (final) phases of the selection process would also be conducted successfully. As per established practice, ICCBS scientists are preparing Pakistani students for participation in the International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO), scheduled to be held in Taipei, Taiwan, from July 19 to 28, 2027. It is pertinent to mention that the National Science Talent Contest (NSTC), operating under the STEM Careers Programme, serves as the main official pathway for selecting and preparing Pakistani students for international science Olympiads in various disciplines. The intensive training programme included extensive theoretical and practical chemistry instruction, laboratory training, problem-solving sessions, and other academic activities. The camp followed a rigorous 24-hour training schedule throughout the week.

headline: Rangers arrest two suspected robbers in Metroville
description: KARACHI - Pakistan Rangers Sindh have arrested two alleged robbers red-handed during snap checking in Metroville, SITE Town, and recovered an unlicensed 9mm
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Pakistan Rangers Sindh have arrested two alleged robbers red-handed during snap checking in Metroville, SITE Town, and recovered an unlicensed 9mm pistol, ammunition, two snatched mobile phones and cash from their possession. According to a Rangers spokesperson on Tuesday, the arrested suspects were identified as Sher Malik, son of Habibullah, and Amjad Ali, son of Muhammad Anwar. They were allegedly involved in several incidents of robbery and street crime. The spokesperson said the suspects used to follow citizens withdrawing money from banks and ATMs in areas adjoining SITE Town and rob them at gunpoint, taking away cash, mobile phones, motorcycles and other valuables. The suspects, along with an accomplice, had recently robbed a citizen of Rs300,000 in the Shershah area. They would subsequently divide the stolen money among themselves, he added. The spokesperson said both suspects had previous criminal records and were allegedly involved in robbery, attempted murder and illegal possession of arms. Sher Malik, described as the alleged gang leader, had recently been released from prison after serving a three-year sentence in a robbery case. He was reportedly responsible for running and supervising the group’s criminal activities. Several cases had been registered against the suspects at different police stations, the spokesperson said, adding that raids were under way to arrest their remaining accomplices. The arrested suspects, along with the recovered weapon, ammunition and other items, have been handed over to police for further legal proceedings.

headline: SSP takes notice of murder incident in Shikarpur, orders transparent investigation
description: SUKKUR - Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Shikarpur Muhammad Kaleem has taken notice of a tragic murder incident within the jurisdiction of Lakhi Ghulam
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: SUKKUR - Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Shikarpur Muhammad Kaleem has taken notice of a tragic murder incident within the jurisdiction of Lakhi Ghulam Shah, Shikarpur’s police station. According to the police spokesperson, SSP appointed DSP Lakhi Ghulam Shah Muhammad Ali Soomro as the inquiry officer to ensure a transparent investigation. According to preliminary investigations, the murder was not the result of resistance during a robbery. However, investigations are underway to determine the actual motive behind the incident. Police are examining all aspects of the case in detail, while further facts are expected to emerge after the receipt of the post-mortem report. SSP Muhammad Kaleem directed the concerned police officials to utilise all available resources to ensure the prompt arrest of those involved in the murder and bring them to justice. He stated that those responsible for the tragic killing would not be shown any leniency and that every possible measure would be taken to ensure they receive strict punishment in accordance with the law. He further emphasised that providing justice to the victim’s family remains the top priority of Shikarpur Police.

headline: Governor attends grand final, closing ceremony of 2nd Ultimate Padel League
description: KARACHI - Governor of Sindh Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi said that nations progress when they provide their youth with healthy recreational activities and
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: KARACHI - Governor of Sindh Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi said that nations progress when they provide their youth with healthy recreational activities and opportunities to participate in sports. He appreciated the management of Johar Sports Arena for providing excellent sporting facilities to young people through its dedicated efforts. He expressed these views while addressing the grand final and closing ceremony of the Second Ultimate Padel League at Johar Sports Arena. The Governor Sindh further observed that sporting arenas had become important platforms for marketing and promoting various products. He noted that branding in sports was playing a significant role in promoting business activities. He emphasised that organising sporting competitions was essential to encourage young people to participate in positive and constructive activities. Hashmi distributed prizes among the players who excelled in various competitions of the Second Ultimate Padel League.

headline: Karachi police review security, traffic arrangements for FoodAg 2026
description: KARACHI - Additional Inspector General of Police, Karachi Azad Khan chaired a meeting at the Karachi Police Office (KPO) on Monday to review security and
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: KARACHI - Additional Inspector General of Police, Karachi Azad Khan chaired a meeting at the Karachi Police Office (KPO) on Monday to review security and traffic arrangements for the fourth International Food and Agriculture Exhibition (FoodAg 2026). The meeting discussed in detail the security and traffic plans for the exhibition, with senior police officials attending, including Director Security (Retd.) Brigadier Amjad, Assistant Director Sarang Gul, DIGP Administration, DIGP East, DIGP Traffic, DIGP Special Branch, DIGP Special Protection Unit (SPU), Commandant Special Security Unit (SSU), and SSPs East and South. The Additional IGP was given a detailed briefing on the proposed security and traffic arrangements for the event. Azad Khan directed all concerned officers to ensure coordinated and comprehensive measures for effective security and smooth traffic flow throughout the exhibition. He called for foolproof security, effective patrolling and random checking, while directing officers to maintain uninterrupted traffic movement. He further ordered strict surveillance around and inside the Karachi Expo Centre, particularly at all main entrances, and directed that plainclothes personnel be deployed at appropriate locations. The Additional IGP also stressed the need for adequate security for foreign guests and their places of accommodation, alongside all necessary measures to protect the lives and property of citizens.

headline: CM Murad approves major Public-Private Partnership development projects
description: KARACHI - In a major push to improve public services, attract private investment and accelerate development across Sindh, Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: KARACHI - In a major push to improve public services, attract private investment and accelerate development across Sindh, Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Tuesday approved a series of landmark initiatives through the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) framework, including the outsourcing of 750 schools, development of Keti Bandar as a maritime and economic hub, restructuring of Sukkur’s water supply and sewerage system, and major road connectivity projects. Presiding over the 53rd meeting of the PPP Policy Board at the CM House, the chief minister also approved a revised joint venture model for Dhabeji Special Economic Zone (SEZ), bridge financing of Rs2 billion for the Ghotki-Kandhkot Bridge and several initiatives to strengthen Karachi’s infrastructure, expand industrial investment and introduce modern digital facilities. The decisions, involving proposals from seven government departments, reflect the provincial government’s commitment to using private-sector expertise, investment and technology to improve essential services, create economic opportunities and deliver better facilities to citizens. The meeting was attended by Provincial Ministers Syed Nasir Hussain Shah, Syed Sardar Shah and Jam Khan Shoro; Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah; MPAs Ghulam Qadir Chandio and Qasim Siraj Soomro; Special Assistants Syed Qasim Naveed and Muhammad Ali Rashid; Principal Secretary to the CM Agha Wasif; Chairman Planning and Development Board Najam Shah; Senior Member Board of Revenue Khalid Hyder Shah and other senior officials. In a major education-sector decision, the Board approved Phase-II outsourcing of 750 schools under the Sindh Secondary Education Improvement Project (SSEIP), Sindh Early Learning Enhancement through Classroom Transformation (SELECT) programme and People’s Schools initiative. The programme covers 453 SSEIP schools, including 401 under additional financing and 52 under original financing, 295 SELECT schools and two English-medium People’s Schools. Education Management Organisations (EMOs) will manage the schools under 10-year service management contracts, following a three-month preparatory period. The private operators will be responsible for teachers’ salaries, non-teaching staff, operational expenses, uniforms, stationery and other essential services, with government funding. The 750 schools have a combined capacity of 345,940 students, against current enrolment of 188,852, offering considerable potential to expand access to quality education. The Board also approved the constitution of a Technical and Financial Evaluation Committee and the initiation of open national competitive bidding through the e-PADS platform, using Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS). To accelerate industrialisation and attract private investment, the Board approved a revised transaction structure for Dhabeji Special Economic Zone, replacing the earlier Build-Operate-Transfer model with a joint venture between the Sindh government, through Sindh Economic Zones Management Company (SEZMC), and private investors. Under the arrangement, the government will contribute land, existing development works and other agreed inputs, while private partners will bring equity, technical expertise and investment to finance, develop and operate the industrial zone. The project covers approximately 1,171 acres of saleable land, including 1,071 acres for industrial activities and 100 acres for commercial use. Development is planned in two phases over 36 months. The Board approved investor solicitation through a competitive two-stage, two-envelope bidding process, including prequalification, investor dialogue and requests for proposals. In another landmark decision, the Board approved the project concept for developing Keti Bandar into an integrated maritime, industrial, logistics and energy hub. The initiative aims to unlock the economic potential of Sindh’s coastline and the Indus Delta through modern maritime infrastructure and domestic and international private investment. The proposed development encompasses six major areas: energy and petroleum infrastructure, industrial and logistics facilities, port and marine infrastructure, shipbuilding and marine services, community and tourism facilities, and digital security systems. The envisaged facilities include oil terminals, storage tanks, pipelines, cargo yards, warehouses, industrial and export zones, deep-water berths, a modern fishing harbour, shipyard, dry docks and marine training facilities. The plan also includes tourism, hotels, a marina, housing, healthcare and education facilities, supported by modern vessel-monitoring, surveillance and emergency-response systems. The Board approved funding through the Project Development Facility (PDF) to engage transaction advisers for detailed feasibility studies and preparation of a bankable PPP structure, paving the way for private-sector participation.Karachi Financial Centre initiative approved The Board also approved the concept of the proposed Karachi Financial Centre, aimed at strengthening Karachi’s position as a regional financial and investment hub. The initiative seeks to attract domestic and international investment in financial services, infrastructure, energy, housing and technology. PDF funding was approved to engage transaction advisers for a comprehensive feasibility study and development of the transaction structure.Sindh Institute of Teacher Education under PPP The Board approved the proposed PPP structure for establishing and operating the Sindh Institute of Teacher Education (SITE), Karachi, through a proposal submitted by M/s Durbeen. The degree-awarding institution will focus on improving teacher education, educational leadership, research-based learning, modern teaching practices and professional development of faculty. The Board approved the project scope, transaction structure, private partner’s capital and operational commitments, government support and risk-sharing arrangements. It also approved the revised framework, including the proponent’s Right of First Refusal and initiation of the investor-solicitation process, subject to applicable legal and regulatory requirements.Karachi Port-Qayumabad Corridor and Shahrah-e-Bhutto The Board considered key matters relating to the 16.5-kilometre Karachi Port to Qayumabad Corridor, an access-controlled, four-lane expressway connecting Shahrah-e-Bhutto with Karachi Port’s East Wharf. Being developed under a Design, Finance, Build, Operate, Maintain and Transfer (DFBOT) arrangement, the project has a concession period of 27.5 years, including 2.5 years of construction and 25 years of operation and maintenance. The Board considered the concessionaire’s proposal to introduce an Infrastructure Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) structure in place of Class-A equity in the project company, along with matters relating to the Karachi Port Trust licence agreement and final No Objection Certificate. For Shahrah-e-Bhutto Expressway, the Board approved riverbank protection works, including submerged groynes, an additional loop and ramp at Interchange No. 5 at Memon Goth, and street lighting along designated sections.KDA Parking Plaza and 41 additional parking sites To address Karachi’s growing parking needs, the Board approved the concept of a multi-level KDA Parking Plaza near Ziauddin Hospital, Clifton Block-2. The proposed facility will be developed on a 1,352-square-yard KDA-owned plot and provide 96 car parking spaces and 160 motorcycle spaces, along with limited commercial facilities. With an estimated cost of Rs1.61 billion, the project will be developed under a Design-Build-Operate-Transfer arrangement with a proposed 35-year concession period. The Board also approved including an assessment of 41 additional KDA-owned parking sites across Clifton Blocks 1 to 7 and 9 in the transaction advisers’ scope, for possible development under the PPP framework. The Board approved proposals for improved police facilitation and installation of intelligent surveillance cameras with solar-powered solutions along Shahrah-e-Bhutto Expressway. The proposals include security and protective measures identified by the Senior Superintendents of Police of Korangi and Malir districts, as well as intelligent cameras to strengthen monitoring and law-enforcement arrangements. The proposed measures will be implemented through adjustments to the concession scope or budgetary allocations to the Police Department, in accordance with applicable financial and project arrangements.IFC’s $100 million guarantee facility approved To facilitate financing for major infrastructure projects, the Board approved a draft mandate agreement with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) for a Partial Credit Guarantee facility of up to $100 million, equivalent to approximately Rs28.5 billion. The proposed arrangement involving IFC, the Sindh Finance Department and Sindh Public-Private Partnership (Private) Limited will provide guarantees against the government’s termination-payment obligations to lenders financing selected PPP projects, subject to IFC’s due diligence and appraisal. The facility is expected to strengthen lenders’ confidence, broaden financing options and facilitate financial closure of major development projects. The Board approved recommending the agreement to the provincial cabinet for formal approval. Reviewing progress on the Ghotki-Kandhkot Bridge, the chief minister examined construction, financial closure, additional works and pending clearances from the National Highway Authority (NHA). The Board ratified the chairman’s approval of a Rs2 billion bridge financing facility to maintain construction activities until commercial debt financing becomes available. The project includes a 12.2-kilometre bridge across the Indus River, along with connecting approach roads, and is expected to improve connectivity between Ghotki and Kandhkot and facilitate regional trade and movement. In an important step towards improving essential municipal services, the Board approved the transaction structure for the Sukkur Water Supply Project, paving the way for investor solicitation under the PPP framework. Being developed through the Sukkur Water and Sewerage Corporation, the project aims to improve the city’s water supply, distribution network, sewerage and drainage infrastructure, while strengthening the corporation’s institutional capacity. Based on an estimated population of 608,095 in 2026, water demand is projected to rise from the current 30 million gallons per day to 32 MGD in 2029 and 41 MGD by 2048. The proposed interventions include water treatment and pumping facilities, distribution networks, billing meters, sewerage infrastructure, an eight-MGD sewage treatment plant, drainage improvements, digitisation and institutional capacity-building. The Board approved the transaction and risk-allocation frameworks, along with the Unsolicited Proposal for competitive bidding. It also approved the proponent’s Right of First Refusal and exemption from prequalification, subject to formal acceptance of the revised proposal and applicable legal requirements, allowing the investor-solicitation process to proceed. The chief minister emphasised the importance of moving approved initiatives towards implementation through transparent competitive processes, sound project preparation and effective coordination among the concerned departments. The government, he said, remained committed to mobilising private investment to improve public services and accelerate Sindh’s development.

Being developed through the Sukkur Water and Sewerage Corporation, the project aims to improve the city’s water supply, distribution network, sewerage and drainage infrastructure, while strengthening the corporation’s institutional capacity.

Based on an estimated population of 608,095 in 2026, water demand is projected to rise from the current 30 million gallons per day to 32 MGD in 2029 and 41 MGD by 2048.

The proposed interventions include water treatment and pumping facilities, distribution networks, billing meters, sewerage infrastructure, an eight-MGD sewage treatment plant, drainage improvements, digitisation and institutional capacity-building.

The Board approved the transaction and risk-allocation frameworks, along with the Unsolicited Proposal for competitive bidding. It also approved the proponent’s Right of First Refusal and exemption from prequalification, subject to formal acceptance of the revised proposal and applicable legal requirements, allowing the investor-solicitation process to proceed.

The chief minister emphasised the importance of moving approved initiatives towards implementation through transparent competitive processes, sound project preparation and effective coordination among the concerned departments. The government, he said, remained committed to mobilising private investment to improve public services and accelerate Sindh’s development.

headline: Rupee gains 01 paisa against dollar
description: ISLAMABAD - Rupee on Tuesday appreciated by 01 paisa against the US dollar in interbank trading and closed at Rs276.65, compared to the previous day’s
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Rupee on Tuesday appreciated by 01 paisa against the US dollar in interbank trading and closed at Rs276.65, compared to the previous day’s closing of Rs276.66. According the Forex Association of Pakistan (FAP), the dollar’s open-market buying and selling rates were Rs277.25 and Rs279.50, respectively. The Euro rose by Rs1.45 to close at Rs310.95, up from Rs309.50 the previous day, according to the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP). The Japanese Yen remained unchanged, closing at Rs1.75, while the British Pound surged by Rs1.53 to Rs372.15 from Rs370.62 the previous day. The exchange rates of the Emirate Dirham and Saudi Riyal stood stagnant to close at Rs75.32 and Rs73.70, respectively.

headline: Gold prices fall by Rs1,500 per tola
description: ISLAMABAD (NEWS WIRE): Gold prices witnessed a decline in the domestic market on Tuesday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola falling by Rs1,500 to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD (NEWS WIRE): Gold prices witnessed a decline in the domestic market on Tuesday, with the price of 24-karat gold per tola falling by Rs1,500 to Rs430,836, according to rates issued by the All Pakistan Sarafa Gems and Jewellers Association. Similarly, the price of 10 grams of 24-karat gold decreased by Rs1,286 to Rs369,372, while the price of 10 grams of 22-karat gold declined by Rs1,179 to Rs338,603. In the international market, the price of gold decreased by $15 to $4,083 per ounce, the association reported. Meanwhile, the price of silver per tola remained unchanged at Rs5,723, while the price of 10 grams of silver also stayed stable at Rs4,906. The price of silver in the international market remained unchanged at $52.45 per ounce, the association added.

headline: CCoSOEs approves proposals for NESPAK, Hesco, Sepco boards
description: ISLAMABAD - The Cabinet Committee on State-Owned Enterprises (CCoSOEs), chaired by Federal Finance and Revenue Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, on Tuesday
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The Cabinet Committee on State-Owned Enterprises (CCoSOEs), chaired by Federal Finance and Revenue Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, on Tuesday approved proposals regarding the appointment and reconstitution of Boards of Directors of NESPAK, HESCO and Sukkur Electric Power SEPCO. The meeting was also attended by Federal Science and Technology Minister Khalid Hussain Magsi, relevant federal secretaries and senior representatives of various ministries, divisions and regulatory bodies. The committee considered two agenda items, including the appointment of chairman/independent director of National Engineering Services Pakistan (NESPAK) and the reconstitution of the Board of Directors of Hyderabad Electric Supply Company (HESCO), alongwith the appointment of an independent director for the Board of Sukkur Electric Power Company (SEPCO). After detailed deliberations, the committee approved the proposals. The finance minister stressed that government representatives serving as ex-officio directors on the boards of state-owned enterprises should hold appropriate positions and possess the necessary competence, experience and institutional understanding to effectively represent their respective divisions.

headline: Stock market gains 5,448 points
description: ISLAMABAD - The benchmark KSE-100 Index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) witnessed a positive trend on Tuesday, gaining 5,448.56 points, a positive change
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The benchmark KSE-100 Index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) witnessed a positive trend on Tuesday, gaining 5,448.56 points, a positive change of 3.13 percent, to close at 179,335.24, points against 173,886.69 points recorded in the previous trading session. The ready market witnessed a trading volume of 972.432 million shares, compared to 1,479.999 million shares traded in the previous session. The traded value of the ready market reached Rs50.665 billion, up from Rs22.572 billion a day earlier.

Meanwhile, total market capitalisation also increased to Rs19.397 trillion from Rs18.909 trillion recorded in the previous session. Out of 501 companies that traded in the ready market, 363 posted gains, 107 suffered losses, while 31 remained unchanged, reflecting a mixed trend across the overall market. Cnergyico PK led the volume chart with 70.087 million shares, followed by Tasdeeq Information with 46.846 million shares, and K-Electric Ltd with 42.270 million shares.

Among the top gainers in the ready market, Rafhan Maize Products Company Limited surged by Rs134.90 to close at Rs8,534.89, while Sazgar Engineering Works Limited advanced by Rs96.94 to settle at Rs1,505.04. On the losing side, Attock Refinery Limited declined by Rs33.04 to close at Rs949.12, while National Refinery Limited fell by Rs31.53 to Rs442.92. In the futures (DFC) market, turnover stood at 203.687 million shares with a traded value of Rs10.667 billion, compared with 135.948 million shares worth Rs5.876 billion in the previous session. Of the 269 companies traded in the DFC market, 269 advanced, 35 declined, and 2 remained unchanged.

headline: Pakistan’s workers’ remittances rise 13.8pc to $3.9b in Oct 2026
description: ISLAMABAD - Overseas workers’ remittances to Pakistan recorded healthy growth of 13.8 percent, reaching $3.9 billion in October 2026. According to the
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Overseas workers’ remittances to Pakistan recorded healthy growth of 13.8 percent, reaching $3.9 billion in October 2026. According to the latest data released by the State Bank of Pakistan, remittances stood at $3.9 billion in October 2026, compared with $3.42 billion in the same month last year, reflecting an increase of 13.8 percent.

On a monthly basis, the remittances have shown an increase of 8.5 percent from $3.6 billion in September 2026. Meanwhile, during the first four months (July to October) of the current fiscal year, cumulatively, workers’ remittances increased by 14 percent to $14.8 billion compared to $13 billion received during the same period last year. “These sustained inflows are strengthening Pakistan’s foreign exchange position, supporting households and reinforcing external-account stability,” Khurram Schehzad, Advisor to the Finance Minister, commented on social media platform X.

The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) projects full-year workers’ remittances at $45 billion for fiscal year 2026–27 (FY27), having revised the target upward from an earlier estimate of $44 billion. SBP Governor Jameel Ahmed recently said that workers’ remittances have remained resilient in the first quarter of this fiscal year (FY27) and are projected to turn out higher than the earlier assessment. “Workers’ remittances are expected to increase further, with Pakistan’s inflows projected at $45 billion in the current fiscal year, up from the previous estimate of $44 billion,” he added.

The Ministry of Finance has also said that workers’ remittances increased by 14.0 percent to $10.9 billion (during July to September period), more than covering the combined goods and services trade deficit. These sustained inflows strengthened foreign exchange availability, helped meet the economy’s import and external payment requirements and cushioned the current account against higher energy costs as domestic activity continued to recover. “Rising services exports and remittances provide a further source of foreign exchange and household income. The stronger reserve position and broader access to external financing is creating a more supportive environment,” the ministry noted in its monthly report.

According to SBP data, Saudi Arabia remained the largest source of workers’ remittances in October 2026, with overseas Pakistanis sending $982 million. This represented a 17 percent increase compared to $838 million received in October 2025. On a month-on-month basis, inflows also rose by 9 percent from $899 million recorded in September 2026. Remittances from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) increased by 16 percent year-on-year, reaching $816 million in October 2026, compared to $703 million in the corresponding month last year. On a monthly basis, inflows grew by 9 percent from $749 million in September 2026.

Meanwhile, remittances from the United Kingdom (UK) stood at $592 million in October 2026, marking a 19 percent increase from $499 million received in October 2025. Overseas Pakistanis in the United States (US) sent $329 million in October 2026, up 9 percent from $301 million in the same month last year. Compared with the $306 million recorded in August 2026, inflows increased by 8 percent. Remittances from European Union (EU) countries totalled $461 million in October 2026, registering a 3 month-on-month increase compared to $448 million received in September 2026.

headline: Govt authorises Rs412.294b in four months
description: ISLAMABAD - The federal government has authorised development funds amounting to Rs412.294 billion under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) during
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The federal government has authorised development funds amounting to Rs412.294 billion under the Public Sector Development Programme (PSDP) during the first four months (July-October) of fiscal year 2026-27, against a total allocation of Rs1 trillion. According to the latest Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Initiatives data released on Tuesday, the PSDP 2026-27 allocation comprises Rs682.485 billion for federal ministries, Rs312.515 billion for corporations, Rs4 billion for project liabilities and Rs1 billion for new initiatives under CPEC 2.0. Against the total allocation of Rs1 trillion, Rs412.294 billion was authorised while development expenditure stood at Rs103.876 billion during July-October 2026.

Among the federal ministries and divisions, the highest authorisation was made for the Water Resources Division, amounting to Rs90.804 billion, against its allocation of Rs103.086 billion, while expenditure stood at Rs18.726 billion. The Cabinet Division received an allocation of Rs64.080 billion, of which Rs60.378 billion was authorised and Rs59.99 million spent during the period. The provinces and special areas were allocated Rs233.386 billion, against which Rs59.796 billion was authorised and Rs23.808 billion spent. The Higher Education Commission (HEC) was allocated Rs46 billion, of which Rs13.800 billion was authorised and Rs4.715 billion spent, while the Federal Education and Professional Training Division was allocated Rs36.312 billion, with Rs12.709 billion authorized and Rs6.877 billion spent.

The Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Division was allocated Rs22.626 billion, against which Rs6.788 billion was authorised and Rs2.152 billion spent. The Railways Division received an allocation of Rs40.658 billion, with Rs14.230 billion authorised and Rs4.655 billion spent. The Information Technology and Telecommunication Division was allocated Rs19.580 billion, including Rs9.801 billion in foreign assistance, against which Rs5.874 billion was authorised and Rs1.450 billion spent. The Interior Division had an allocation of Rs21.825 billion, with Rs6.547 billion authorised and Rs714.21 million spent. The National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination Division was allocated Rs16.065 billion, of which Rs9.639 billion was authorised and Rs6.609 billion spent, while the Housing and Works Division had an allocation of Rs16.395 billion, with Rs1.918 billion authorized and Rs422.90 million spent.

headline: Govt plans smart metre installation on Disco transformers to curb power theft, overbilling
description: ISLAMABAD - The government has decided to install smart metres on transformers across all power distribution companies (DISCOs) to curb electricity theft,
author: Imran Ali Kundi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The government has decided to install smart metres on transformers across all power distribution companies (DISCOs) to curb electricity theft, improve billing accuracy.

Federal Economic Affairs and Establishment Division Minister Ahad Cheema on Tuesday chaired a meeting on Power Distribution Companies (DISCOs). The meeting reviewed development programmes for DISCOs and discussed the Economic Affairs Division’s (EAD) efforts to arrange funding for installing smart metres on transformers across all DISCOs. Participants noted that positive progress had been made so far in arranging funding for the smart metering system, which is intended to help curb electricity theft and overbilling.

The meeting discussed the continuation of the smart metering project after privatisation. Ahad Cheema said the government would put in place arrangements to ensure that private investors carry the project forward. Smart metres on transformers can help curb electricity theft, improve billing accuracy and protect consumers from overbilling, while safeguarding the interests of consumers, investors and the government.

Negotiations with multilateral partners for development programmes would continue until privatisation is completed. If a DISCO is privatised while negotiations or programme preparations are under way, the relevant financing and development programmes would be transferred to the private investor as part of the handover, subject to agreed arrangements.

Ahad Cheema further emphasised that any new project undertaken by a private investor within a DISCO must be processed through competitive bidding and receive approval from the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (NEPRA), as applicable. He stressed that the purpose of privatisation was not to shift costs or undue pressure onto consumers. The government would facilitate the process while safeguarding consumers’ interests and ensuring that investors meet their financial and contractual obligations. Federal Power Division Minister Sardar Awais Ahmad Khan Leghari, the Prime Minister’s Adviser on Privatisation, and senior officials from the relevant ministries also attended the meeting.

headline: Four arrested, 5.66-kg charas recovered in Nowshera Virkan
description: NOWSHERA VIRKAN - Police arrested four alleged drug peddlers and recovered 5.66-kg of charas during four separate operations in different areas of Nowshera
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: NOWSHERA VIRKAN - Police arrested four alleged drug peddlers and recovered 5.66-kg of charas during four separate operations in different areas of Nowshera Virkan. According to police, the crackdown was conducted here on Tuesday under the supervision of DSP Anser Farooq Mann and SHO Ziafat Bhath. Sub-Inspector Shafqat Abbas recovered 1,520 grams of charas from Muhammad Yaseen at Babar Chowk, while ASI Muhammad Nawaz seized 820 grams from Muhammad Imran at Chand Colony Chowk. Similarly, ASI Waheed Ahmad recovered 1,680 grams of charas from Muhammad Asghar at Khand Peer Chowk, while Sub-Inspector Waheed Abbas seized 1,640 grams from Rana Afzal Ali at Adda Jagowal.

headline: 19 challans issued against overcharging, overloading
description: SARGODHA - The district administration has issued 19 challans against public transport operators for overcharging and overloading during a district-wide
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: SARGODHA - The district administration has issued 19 challans against public transport operators for overcharging and overloading during a district-wide crackdown. Acting on the directions of the deputy commissioner, the District Regional Transport Authority (RTA) launched an extensive enforcement operation across the district, inspecting around 500 vehicles. During the campaign, 19 vehicles were impounded for violating transport regulations. In a move to provide immediate relief to commuters, authorities recovered Rs72,000 in excess fares from transport operators and returned the amount to passengers. Additionally, fines totalling Rs83,000 were imposed on vehicle owners found violating the rules.

headline: Saudi, Pakistani investors sign MoU to launch Saudi–Pak Private Equity Fund
description: KARACHI - The Saudi–Pakistan Joint Business Council (SPJBC) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish the Saudi–Pakistan Private
author: PR
article_text:
KARACHI - The Saudi–Pakistan Joint Business Council (SPJBC) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to establish the Saudi–Pakistan Private Equity Fund. The signing ceremony was attended by members of the Council from both countries.

Representing the Pakistani side, Mr Fawad Mukhtar, Co-Chair of the Council and Chairman of Fatima Group, joined virtually. Members attending in person included Mr Zafar Masud, President and CEO of The Bank of Punjab; Mr Nassir Saleem, President and CEO of Habib Bank Limited; Mr Yousaf Hussain, President and CEO of Faysal Bank Limited; and Mr Maqsood Ismail, Director of Ismail Industries Limited. Dr Gohar Ejaz, Chairman of Lake City Group; Lord Zameer Choudrey, Chairman of Bestway Group; and Mr Jawaid Iqbal, President and CEO of United Bank Limited, also joined virtually.

From the Saudi side, the signing ceremony was attended by HH Prince Mansour bin Mohammad Al Saud, Chairman of the SPJBC; the Council’s two Vice-Chairmen, Mr Mohammad bin Abdulaziz Al Ajlan, CEO of Al Ajlan Group, and Mr Abdulaziz Bin Ali Al Ashrafi of Tayba Group; and the following Council members: Dr Mohammed Khan of RAEM Group; Mr Zaid Al Sharif of Alsharif Group; Eng. Mohammed Al Mufarij, CEO of Saudi Meters Company; Dr Mohammed Al-Sowaidan, CEO of International Investment Gare; Mr Abdallah Al Muhnna, CEO of SAFA Investment; Mr Abdulrahman Ayedh Algahtani, CEO of Somuo Investment; Mr Hani Baothman, CEO of Bin Dawood Investment; Mr Ghassan Amoudi, CEO of ASYAD Group; Mr Feras Albakri of Albakri Group; Barrister Habil Ahmed Khan, CEO of Welt Konnect; and Mr Mansour Chaudhry, CEO of Barq Pakistan.

The council was formed by the governments of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, in coordination with both countries high committee to deepen bilateral private-sector trade and investment. This MoU is the outcome of a series of meetings of the Saudi–Pakistan Joint Business Council which concluded and proposed to have an initial size of multi-hundred million and is envisaged to grow into a bigger scale figure fund, based on the opportunities on all sectors. Saudi and Pakistani private investors will contribute equally to the Fund, while 75 percent of the fund shall be invested in Pakistan and 25 percent in Saudi Arabia projects.

The fund intends to invest in high-growth private businesses, including in agriculture, mining, and industries including construction. It will also explore commercial projects arising from the Government of Pakistan’s programme to monetise its land bank, including airports and motorways development, port and maritime development. This will help unlock the economic value of under-utilised public land through commercially structured, transparent investments. The fund will also seek commercial investments across KSA, including in the holy cities. The MoU allows for institutions on both sides to be invited to participate in the equity of the fund management company.

Speaking at the signing, His Highness Prince Mansour bin Mohammad Al Saud said, “The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and Pakistan are bound by a friendship and kinship that run deeper than any agreement. That bond has always been strong in spirit; this fund now will give it an equally strong commercial footing. Pakistan is a natural partner for the Kingdom, and Saudi investors are looking for partners and markets where they can grow with confidence. Having looked closely at Pakistan, what we see today is a more stable economy with real opportunities. By investing side by side with our Pakistani brothers, in both our countries, we are turning years of contemplation and studies into on ground investment that benefits both our peoples and building a partnership designed to last.”

Mr Arif Habib said that this fund is a vote of confidence in profitable investment opportunities in Pakistan. For too long, perceptions of Pakistan have clouded the reality, and this agreement shows that serious investors are ready to act on that reality. Pakistani investors are putting their contribution as the lead in the confidence in Pakistan’s economy, and our Saudi brothers are investing alongside us. Directing capital towards the monetisation of the govt’s land bank will turn idle assets into productive investment. I am grateful to His Highness Prince Mansour and to colleagues on both sides for the time, patience and goodwill they have devoted to bringing this fund to life. We see it as the first step towards restoring the confidence of Saudi and wider foreign investors in Pakistan.”

The signing marks a new chapter in Saudi–Pakistan economic cooperation, in which a long friendship between the two nations becomes a shared investment in their future. The establishment of the fund shall comply with the regulatory requirements of the Governments of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. Once approvals are in place, the two sides will move ahead with the fund’s structuring and first investments.

headline: Livestock farmers urged to take precautionary measures against smog
description: SARGODHA - Additional Director Livestock and Dairy Development Dr Naila Maqsood on Tuesday urged livestock farmers to adopt precautionary measures to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
SARGODHA - Additional Director Livestock and Dairy Development Dr Naila Maqsood on Tuesday urged livestock farmers to adopt precautionary measures to protect their animals from the harmful effects of smog, warning that prolonged exposure could adversely affect animal health and productivity.

According to a spokesperson, she emphasised that timely preventive measures were essential to protect valuable livestock from smog-related hazards and maintain their health, milk production and overall productivity.

Dr Naila Maqsood explained that exposure to smog could cause respiratory distress, coughing, irritation of the nose and throat, and redness of the eyes in animals. These health complications could also lead to reduced fodder intake, declining milk yields and physical weakness.

Advising farmers to take preventive steps, she recommended keeping animals indoors during peak smog hours to minimise their exposure to smoke and dust. She also stressed the importance of maintaining clean, properly ventilated animal sheds and avoiding unnecessary long-distance transportation during periods of severe smog.

She further advised farmers to seek immediate veterinary assistance if their animals showed signs of smog-related illness to ensure timely diagnosis and treatment.

Dr Maqsood added that livestock farmers could obtain professional guidance or register complaints through the Punjab Livestock Department’s 24-hour helpline at 08000-9211.

headline: Pakistan’s marketing services exports rise 19pc as agencies gear up for global growth at Payoneer
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan’s exports of advertising and market research services rose 19 percent year-on-year to $30.7 million in July–September 2026, up
author: PR
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan’s exports of advertising and market research services rose 19 percent year-on-year to $30.7 million in July–September 2026, up from $25.8 million in the same quarter last year, State Bank of Pakistan data shows. The figures set the backdrop for Payoneer Connect Lahore, where more than 40 marketing agencies met to explore how to win clients abroad and scale with them.

Hosted by Payoneer, the global financial technology company that helps businesses grow across borders, the event was themed ‘The Export Era of Global Marketing’. It brought agency leaders together with representatives of the Pakistan Software Houses Association (P@SHA), Google, along with AI practitioners.

This services export momentum extends across professional services. Other business services, from the wider State Bank category that also covers public relations, consulting and technical services, recorded exports of $620 million in the same quarter, up 27 percent year-on-year. Within it, exports of consulting and public relations services rose 22 percent to $81.2 million.

That emphasis on quality over volume also ran through a fireside chat on agentic AI with Ali Imran Memon, founder and CEO of Kitsune AI. The conversation examined whether Pakistan has reached the limits of freelancing and outsourcing, and how agencies can turn their expertise into AI agents and products rather than billable hours. It also weighed whether AI services should be priced by subscription, task or outcome.

AI is also lowering the cost of scaling in new markets. Google’s Customer Solutions team showed how localisation using AI tools can greatly expand cross-border business opportunities for Pakistani companies. Sustaining this growth will also depend on policy. P@SHA Vice Chairman Samad Saleem outlined the policy and advocacy work under way to enable and scale Pakistan’s digital services exports, as the government pursues its target of $15 billion in IT exports by 2030.

headline: Faisalabad commissioner forms committee to review remodeling of roads, U-turns, ramps
description: FAISALABAD - Divisional Commissioner Dr Imran Hamid Sheikh has constituted a committee to review the remodeling of roads, U-turns and ramps at various
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
FAISALABAD - Divisional Commissioner Dr Imran Hamid Sheikh has constituted a committee to review the remodeling of roads, U-turns and ramps at various locations along Canal Road to remove traffic bottlenecks and trouble spots and ensure smooth traffic flow.

Headed by the additional deputy commissioner (Enforcement), the committee comprises representatives of the Faisalabad Development Authority (FDA), Municipal Corporation, Traffic Police and Highways Department. The FDA has also been assigned the necessary responsibilities regarding road redesigning and technical planning.

In this regard, Commissioner Dr Imran Hamid Sheikh chaired a high-level meeting to conduct a detailed review of the traffic management situation along Canal Road.

Various construction-related and technical measures were discussed to ensure smooth traffic flow, safe commuting and convenience for citizens. During the meeting, Director General FDA Muhammad Asif Chaudhary briefed the participants on various aspects of the designs and proposed remodeling plan already prepared by the FDA’s Engineering Branch.

Director Development Asif Iqbal Chohan, Chief Traffic Officer (CTO) Rana Nasir Javed, Chief Engineer FDA Mehr Ayub, Chief Officer Municipal Corporation Muhammad Usman Ghani and other relevant officers also attended the meeting.

headline: PFA destroys 70-kg of banned chinese salt, fines Rs60,000
description: BUREWALA - The Punjab Food Authority (PFA) has seized and destroyed 70-kg of banned Chinese salt during an inspection of a grocery store here on Tuesday
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
BUREWALA - The Punjab Food Authority (PFA) has seized and destroyed 70-kg of banned Chinese salt during an inspection of a grocery store here on Tuesday on Siphon Road in Mailsi and imposed a fine of Rs60,000 on its owner. According to a PFA spokesperson, the food safety team found the prohibited salt being stored and sold at the shop.

Inspectors also identified several hygiene violations, including food items placed directly on the floor, improper segregation of food and non-food items, and the absence of purchase records.

PFA Director General Raja Mansoor Ahmad said the use of chinese salt could contribute to health problems, including high blood pressure. He said action against those involved in the sale of prohibited food items would continue.

headline: NTU celebrates World Accounting Day, pays tribute to Father of Accounting Luca Pacioli
description: FAISALABAD - The Society of Accounting and Finance Faisalabad Business School National Textile University (NTU) on Tuesday celebrated World Accounting Day
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: FAISALABAD - The Society of Accounting and Finance Faisalabad Business School National Textile University (NTU) on Tuesday celebrated World Accounting Day with a special tribute to Fra Luca Pacioli, widely known as the Father of Accounting. World Accounting Day is observed annually on November 10 to commemorate the publication of Pacioli’s book in 1494 which introduced the double entry bookkeeping system, a fundamental accounting method that continues to be used worldwide. The event was organised under the supervision of the society’s convener Dr Muhammad Zia ur Rehman and Dr Tanveer Bajwa. A large number of faculty members and students attended the celebration. The activities included a cake cutting ceremony, a quiz competition, and various food and other stalls arranged by students. Addressing the gathering, NTU Rector Dr Rashid Masood said that accounting is the language of business and that accuracy in financial reporting plays a vital role in building trust among companies, investors and society. He urged students to uphold professional ethics and stay abreast of emerging technologies and advancements in the field of accounting. Dean of Faisalabad Business School Dr Sajjad Ahmed Baig appreciated the efforts of the society’s organising team and remarked that such activities provide students with valuable opportunities to connect their classroom learning with professional practices. The event highlighted the importance of accounting, professional ethics and technological advancements while providing students with an opportunity to engage in academic and extracurricular activities.

headline: FPCCI urges govt to reconsider early market closure policy
description: LAHORE - Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCC) Regional Chairman and Vice President Zaki Aijaz Tuesday called upon the government to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LAHORE - Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCC) Regional Chairman and Vice President Zaki Aijaz Tuesday called upon the government to reconsider its decision to enforce early market closures and formulate business policies through meaningful consultation with all relevant stakeholders, ensuring that the concerns of the business community are adequately addressed.

He expressed these views in a media briefing here at FPCCI Regional Office. FPCCI General Body Member and Chairman of the Oil Marketing Association Tariq Mahmood, Patron-in-Chief of the Chain Stores Association Rana Tariq Mehboob, Chairman Wasif Sikandar Butt, Chairman of Pakistan Footwear Manufacturers Association Hassan Javed, and other prominent business leaders were also present.

The business leaders observed that government’s decision to close markets early was placing businesses under severe financial pressure, disrupting commercial activities and threatening the livelihoods of millions of people associated with the retail and allied sectors. They added, government should revisit the decision and develop a sustainable policy framework in consultation with representatives of business community and other relevant stakeholders.

They further highlighted that Pakistan has an electricity generation capacity of approximately 48,000 megawatts, whereas current consumption stands at around 14,000 megawatts. A growing number of electricity consumers are shifting towards solar energy and battery storage solutions. In view of this changing consumption pattern, they urged the government to charge electricity consumed during peak hours, from 6:00pm to 10:00pm, at the same tariff applicable to normal units.

According to a new study conducted by renowned research organisation IPSOS, Zaki Aijaz said, restrictions on the operating hours of shops and commercial centres across Pakistan are creating significant financial challenges for businesses and contributing to a substantial decline in sales. The restrictions are also making shopping increasingly inconvenient and difficult for consumers.

The IPSOS study highlights that shortened business hours have adversely affected shopkeepers’ revenues, profitability and overall commercial activities, while simultaneously creating considerable inconvenience for consumers. The comprehensive study covered all four provinces and Islamabad, incorporating interviews with 1,046 consumers and 300 shopkeepers from 53 shopping malls and commercial markets. It also included 25 in-depth interviews with representatives of trade associations, manufacturers, retail brands and government officials. Furthermore, the study examined and compared market operating-hour policies in 15 countries to assess international practices.

He said, the research also reveals that businesses have been compelled to restructure their operations to cope with restricted trading hours. According to the findings, 73 percent of shopkeepers have started opening their businesses earlier, 34 percent have either introduced or expanded online sales, while 12 percent have reported reducing their workforce.

These operational adjustments have further intensified financial pressures on businesses, making it increasingly difficult for them to cover operating expenses, sustain profitability and retain employees. Consumers, meanwhile, are also experiencing significant inconvenience as a result of early market closures. The IPSOS research found that 53 percent of consumers now find it difficult to allocate time for shopping, while 37 percent reported a deterioration in their overall shopping experience. In contrast, only 23 percent of consumers indicated that their shopping experience had improved.

The findings underscore the need for a comprehensive review of the existing market closure policy, taking into account its economic implications, the sustainability of businesses, employment opportunities and consumer convenience. Meaningful engagement with all relevant stakeholders is essential to developing a balanced policy that protects commercial interests while addressing the government’s broader objectives.

headline: Subsidised tractors distributed among farmers in Muzaffargarh
description: MUZAFFARGARH - A ceremony was held in Muzaffargarh to distribute subsidised tractors among farmers under the vision of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz
author: Khurram Malaizai
article_text:
MUZAFFARGARH - A ceremony was held in Muzaffargarh to distribute subsidised tractors among farmers under the vision of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, as part of the provincial government’s initiatives to promote agricultural development and improve farmers’ welfare. Parliamentary Secretary for Higher Education and MPA Ajmal Khan Chandia, MPA Aun Hameed Dogar and Assistant Commissioner Muzaffargarh Umme Habiba attended the ceremony as special guests.

Addressing the gathering, Aun Hameed Dogar said the Punjab government was taking revolutionary steps to modernise agriculture and improve the economic well-being of farmers. He said the provision of modern agricultural machinery and subsidised tractors, in line with Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif’s vision, would help increase agricultural productivity and significantly reduce cultivation costs.

He added that farmers were the backbone of the country’s economy and their prosperity remained among the government’s top priorities. During the ceremony, keys of subsidised tractors were handed over to successful farmers. The beneficiaries appreciated the initiative and thanked the Punjab government and Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, describing it as a positive step towards agricultural development and farmers’ prosperity. Deputy Director Agriculture Extension Tahir Mahmood Bhatti and a number of successful farmers also attended the event.

headline: Petrol subsidy scheme marred by alleged arbitrary practices at fuel stations in Muzaffargarh
description: Muzaffargarh - MUZAFFARGARH: Prime Minister’s Petrol Subsidy Programme has reportedly been undermined by alleged arbitrary practices at fuel
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Muzaffargarh - MUZAFFARGARH: Prime Minister’s Petrol Subsidy Programme has reportedly been undermined by alleged arbitrary practices at fuel stations in Muzaffargarh, leaving motorists struggling to receive the government relief. Citizens seeking subsidised fuel have complained that some petrol pump employees are turning them away instead of facilitating the disbursement of subsidies.

According to complaints, employees allegedly tell customers, “Come at a time of our choosing if you want to receive the subsidy; the staff is currently occupied.” The Police Petrol Pump has reportedly attracted the highest number of complaints, raising concerns about the implementation of the government relief initiative.

Meanwhile, acting on the directions of Deputy Commissioner Muzaffargarh Usman Tahir Jappa, Assistant Commissioner Umm Habiba sealed a Total petrol station in the Doaba area over alleged negligence in implementing the Prime Minister’s Petrol Subsidy Programme and failure to facilitate eligible citizens. According to official details, the assistant commissioner inspected the Total petrol station near Mahmood Mill on Multan Road to assess compliance with the PM Fuel Subsidy Programme. During the inspection, the administration found that citizens were not being provided the government subsidy, prompting the assistant commissioner to take immediate action and seal the facility.

Assistant Commissioner Umm Habiba said negligence, non-cooperation and any obstruction in providing facilities to citizens under government relief programmes would not be tolerated. She added that inspections and monitoring of petrol stations would continue to ensure effective implementation of the Prime Minister’s Petrol Subsidy Programme. Citizens have urged the district administration to extend its inspection drive to all petrol stations rather than limiting action to a single outlet. They have particularly called for an inquiry into complaints against the Police Petrol Pump, demanding strict action against those found responsible for denying or delaying the subsidy. They said the government relief programme could only achieve its intended purpose if petrol stations ensured transparent and uninterrupted access to subsidies for eligible citizens.

headline: Pakistan seeks more LNG from Qatar as Hormuz disruption pushes spot prices to $31 per MMBtu
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has stepped up efforts to secure cheaper LNG supplies from Qatar under two long-term contracts for the winter season amid the disruption
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has stepped up efforts to secure cheaper LNG supplies from Qatar under two long-term contracts for the winter season amid the disruption in the Strait of Hormuz. In a parallel development, Pakistan LNG Limited (PLL) received three bids on Tuesday for the procurement of two spot LNG cargoes, with offers reaching up to $31 per MMBtu.

Federal Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik is in Qatar, leading a high-level delegation to secure LNG supplies for the winter season, a source in the Petroleum Division said. Meanwhile, two international companies submitted a total of three bids in response to PLL’s tender for the procurement of two LNG cargoes from the spot market, scheduled for delivery in December 2026 and January 2027.

Pakistan LNG Limited has received two bids for the supply of LNG for the supply window of December. TotalEnergies Gas & Power Limited quoted a bid offer of Rs24,433,920,000 for a cargo or $27.30 per MMBtu, while QatarEnergy Trading LLC quoted a bid offer of Rs27,776,000,000 or $ 31 per MMBtu. TotalEnergies Gas & Power Limited was declared the lowest evaluated bidder for the window. Similarly, for the second cargo for the delivery window of January 2027, TotalEnergies Gas & Power Limited quoted a bid offer of Rs24,281,600,000 or $27.1 per MMBtu and was declared the lowest evaluated bidder.

Notably, to meet gas and electricity demand during the winter months, PLL had invited bids on November 4, for the supply of two LNG cargoes, with November 6 as the original deadline, but was later extended to November 10 on the request of supplier.

PLL had floated tender to procure two LNG spot cargo of 140,000 cubic metres each, with a tolerance of plus or minus 5 percent, for delivery at Port Qasim for the delivery windows of December 14-16, 2026 and January 9-11, 2027. Regarding Ali Pervaiz Malik visit to Qatar, the source said that secretary petroleum and other senior officials are accompanying the minister during the visit. The delegation will hold talks with Qatari authorities on the supply of LNG cargoes to Pakistan under long-term agreements.

Federal Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik met with Qatar’s Minister of Energy Saad bin Sherida Al Kaabi, on Tuesday, according to a post on the Petroleum Minister’s X account. Pakistan has two long-term LNG supply agreements with Qatar, and Islamabad is seeking to maximise the number of cargoes under these contracts to meet its winter demand, sources said.

The government is making all-out efforts to obtain cheaper LNG from Qatar instead of relying on expensive spot cargoes, which would put additional burden on the national exchequer and consumers, the sources added. However, sources said the procurement of LNG cargoes from Qatar under the existing agreements has become extremely limited due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The visit is aimed at finding a workable arrangement with Doha to ensure uninterrupted LNG supplies to Pakistan despite the logistical constraints arising from the Hormuz closure, the sources said.

The US-Israel-Iran conflict has disrupted Qatari LNG supplies, forcing the government to procure from the spot market to meet electricity demand. Pakistan meets a major portion of its winter gas demand through LNG imported from Qatar under long-term contracts, in addition to procurement from the spot market.

It is noteworthy that, under the winter gas supply strategy, a target has been set to procure 18 LNG cargoes for the four winter months, from November 2026 to February 2027. Under the plan, the government has decided to prioritise cheaper LNG imports from Qatar under two long-term contracts, the source said.

headline: Umar Rehman Malik welcomes completion of one million homes for flood-hit families
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan People’s Party (PPP) leader Umar Rehman Malik yesterday termed the completion of one million homes for families affected by the
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan People’s Party (PPP) leader Umar Rehman Malik yesterday termed the completion of one million homes for families affected by the devastating 2022 floods in Sindh a historic and commendable achievement. In a statement, Umar Rehman Malik said the initiative goes beyond the construction of houses, providing millions of flood-affected people with secure shelter, dignity and the opportunity to rebuild their lives. He said the sustained efforts to rehabilitate affected communities, reconstruct homes and restore normalcy deserved recognition. He particularly highlighted the programme’s focus on women’s empowerment, noting that ownership of the houses is being transferred to women, alongside the establishment of bank accounts in their names. This, he said, provides women with property rights, greater financial security and independence, while strengthening their role in family decision-making. Umar Rehman Malik said the initiative had also received international recognition. Representatives of the World Bank, Asian Development Bank and Islamic Development Bank have appreciated Sindh’s inclusive, climate-resilient housing model, reflecting its wider significance as an approach to post-disaster recovery and rehabilitation. He observed that the true success of any welfare initiative lies in ensuring that its benefits reach ordinary citizens, particularly vulnerable and disaster-affected communities. The completion of one million homes demonstrates how effective public policy and sustained efforts can address major humanitarian challenges. Umar Rehman Malik appreciated the efforts of Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and the Sindh Government, saying the initiative reflected a commitment to rehabilitation, social protection, women’s rights and public welfare. He expressed hope that the programme would continue to provide more affected families with permanent housing and opportunities for a better future. He further said that the Pakistan Peoples Party had consistently remained committed to public service and to empowering and strengthening the country’s most vulnerable sections of society.

headline: South Punjab ACS orders crackdown on stray dogs after girl’s death in Bahawalnagar
description: BAHAWALNGAR - Additional Chief Secretary South Punjab on Tuesday took notice on The Nation’s news, expressing grief over the death of a girl due to
author: Ali Raza
article_text: BAHAWALNGAR - Additional Chief Secretary South Punjab on Tuesday took notice on The Nation’s news, expressing grief over the death of a girl due to stray dogs’ attack in Bahawalnagar. The ACS held an emergency review meeting on the increase in dog bite incidents in South Punjab. Deputy commissioners of all districts of South Punjab attended the video link meeting. A detailed briefing was given by all deputy commissioners about the steps taken by them to destroy stray dogs and vaccinate pet dogs. Additional Chief Secretary Fawad Hasham Rabbani expressed his anger over the performance of the deputy commissioner Bahawalnagar and directed the deputy commissioners of Rajanpur and Vehari to take more concrete and effective steps after a significant increase in dog bite incidents. He also directed all the deputy commissioners to identify areas and take effective steps to eradicate stray dogs. Addressing the meeting, he said that stray dog bites are the red line of the Punjab chief minister and the Punjab government has a zero tolerance policy on the unfortunate incidents of dog bite deaths. He added that the presence of stray dogs and incidents of biting passersby will not be tolerated at all. He directed that all administrative officers of South Punjab should ensure continuous and effective monitoring of municipal services as per government policy. He clarified that verbal collection and data will no longer work for the eradication of stray dogs, all deputy commissioners should be present in the field. He further said that concrete and effective work should be done in the field regarding the red lines clarified by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and the campaign for eradication of stray dogs should be launched in a real sense and fake reporting should be strictly discouraged. He further instructed that an immediate legal action should be taken against the owners in case of incidents of pet dog bites.

headline: Changes in geographical boundaries
description: ISLAMABAD - The plan to redraw geographical boundaries in the country has once again initiated in the political arena. A consensus on new administrative
author: JAVAID UR RAHMAN
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The plan to redraw geographical boundaries in the country has once again initiated in the political arena. A consensus on new administrative division among the parliamentary political forces is a complicated problem.

Political parties in the opposition are not the only reason behind the delay in legislation, as the coalition partners within the ruling clique have started showing their reservations on it. Legislative proceedings on the proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment, which could ultimately pave the way for the creation of new administrative units in the country, appear difficult without evolving a consensus among the ruling coalition partners. PPP, the main allied partner of the government, is partially in the favour of redrawing geographical boundaries.

The required numerical strength could not be completed without the votes of PPP’s members. On the other hand, the opposition parties are also not fully against the creation of new administrative units. This complex situation is apparently compelling the government to adopt a way to pass a resolution from the parliament to conduct a ‘referendum’ in the country. The result of the referendum would ultimately decide the fate of making new provinces/units in the country, background discussions with parliamentarians and constitutional experts revealed.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, around two months ago, remarked with commitment that the creation of new provinces or administrative units could ultimately be decided through public opinion. This idea triggered a debate over whether a referendum can constitutionally be used to create new provinces.

Article 48(6) of the Constitution provides that if the prime minister considers it necessary to hold a referendum on any matter of national importance, he may refer the matter to a joint sitting of Parliament. If approved by a joint sitting, the prime minister may cause the matter to be referred to a referendum in the form of a question capable of being answered by either “Yes” or “No.”

Some senior parliamentarians , desiring not to be named, said that a proposed constitutional amendment is under serious consideration, with around two dozen constitutional articles likely to be amended as part of a broader restructuring of the system. Whereas, Minister for parliamentary affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhary shared with this scribe no proposal under consideration to pass a resolution immediately. “In such a case, we definitely build a consensus,” he remarked. Interior minister Mohsin Naqvi has still not changed his stance that any new administrative units in the country would only be formed if people voiced their support for such a move.

Background discussions with senior parliamentarians and political gurus revealed that there are proposals under consideration for carving out 12 new provinces in the country. From Balochistan to KyberPakhtunkhwa, a political move will be materialized to ensure legislation in all the provincial assemblies and the national assembly. The presence of political bigwigs in London was also stated to be the part of this giant plan, which is likely to be practically seen in the assemblies in the coming months. The political titans in the country have still not finalized a move, which may redraw maps in Punjab, KPK, Balochistan and Sindh.

PPP’s senior leader Qamar Zaman Kaira had shared with this newspaper that the legislation on 28th constitutional package would be possible with the vote of the Pakistan Peoples Party(PPP). About the referendum in the country over new provinces, Kaira said that the referendum’s result would not help creating new provinces in the country. Political and constitutional experts viewed that the govt will soon share this proposal with the political factions from both sides before moving a resolution in the parliament.

headline: PML-F grand workers convention held
description: SUKKUR - A grand workers convention of Pakistan Muslim League Functional was held at Rohri Taluka here in Tuesday. The convention was specially attended by
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: SUKKUR - A grand workers convention of Pakistan Muslim League Functional was held at Rohri Taluka here in Tuesday. The convention was specially attended by members of the Divisional Monitoring Committee of PML-Functional Sukkur, Syed Shafqat Ali Shah, Abdul Karim Shar, and Comrade Nisar Abro, District President Sukkur Faqir Inayatullah Barro, respected Faqir of Hurr Jamaat Kamaluddin Panhyar, District General Secretary Mir Ijaz Ali Talpur, Muhammad Bachal Mahar, Provincial Vice President of MSF Sindh Arbaz Ali Abbasi, and others. On the occasion, a cake was cut to celebrate the birthday of Provincial President of PML-Functional Sindh, Syed Sadruddin Shah Rashdi, and prayers were offered for the security of the country and for the recovery and long life of Pir Sahib Pagara. On this occasion, President Taluka Rohri Faqeer Islamuddin Kandhro, District Vice President Syed Jial Shah, Joint Secretary Muhammad Qasim Kandhro, General Secretary City Saleh Pat Khan Muhammad Channa, General Secretary Taluka Rohri Muhammad Arif Katpar, President MSF District Sukkur Zameer Mahar, General Secretary Abdul Waheed Kandhro, Senior Vice President Haider Mangrio, President Taluka Rohri Sajjad Narejo, Vice President Rab Nawaz Janjho, Noor Muhammad Mahar, Khanzada Mirani, Shahnawaz Narejo, Misri Kalhoro, Ghulam Hussain Kandhro, Ghulam Nabi Barro, Ajeebullah Katpar, Muhammad Qabil Kandhro, Abdul Razzaq Jogi, along with other office-bearers and workers, participated in large numbers.

headline: Section 144 imposed at examination centres across Shaheed Benazirabad Division
description: HYDERABAD - Commissioner Shaheed Benazirabad Division, Ghulam Qadir Khan Talpur, has imposed Section 144 within the premises of all examination centres across
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: HYDERABAD - Commissioner Shaheed Benazirabad Division, Ghulam Qadir Khan Talpur, has imposed Section 144 within the premises of all examination centres across the division to ensure the peaceful conduct of the SSC Part-I and Part-II (Class IX and X) B-I Annual Examinations 2026. According to an official notification, the restrictions will remain in force from November 10 to 19 during the examinations being conducted by the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Shaheed Benazirabad. The notification stated that the decision was taken on the recommendation of Board Chairman Prof Dr Asif Ali Memon to maintain discipline and prevent any untoward incidents during the examinations. Under the restrictions, entry of unauthorized persons into examination centres will be prohibited, while only students appearing in the examinations and on-duty staff will be allowed inside the premises. The use of photocopy machines near examination centres during paper timings will also remain prohibited. Legal action will be taken against those found violating the restrictions.

headline: Security forces recover explosives, missile in North Waziristan
description: ISLAMABAD - Security forces have recovered 700 kilograms of locally manufactured explosives, an Al-Farooq missile and other explosive-making materials during
author: MATEEN HAIDER
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Security forces have recovered 700 kilograms of locally manufactured explosives, an Al-Farooq missile and other explosive-making materials during an ongoing search and clearance operation in different areas of North Waziristan, as troops continue efforts to eliminate potential terrorist hideouts and clear the area of security threats.

According to security sources, security forces have so far completed searches of another 62 houses and several compounds in different areas as part of the ongoing clearance operation. Security sources said that troops also recovered approximately 700 kilograms of locally manufactured explosive material during an operation in Mosaki. In addition, an Al-Farooq missile, 200 kilograms of urea and other related equipment were recovered from Hassu Khel. The recoveries point to the presence of explosives and weapons-related material at locations being searched during clearance operation. Security sources said the search and clearance operation would continue until all suspected locations and areas potentially being used by terrorists had been thoroughly cleared.
