headline: Awais Shah attends Pakistan–Malaysia Friendship Association’s 5th awards ceremony
description: KARACHI - Speaker of Provincial Assembly (PA) of Sindh, Syed Awais Qadir Shah, attended the 5th awards ceremony of the Pakistan–Malaysia Friendship
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
KARACHI - Speaker of Provincial Assembly (PA) of Sindh, Syed Awais Qadir Shah, attended the 5th awards ceremony of the Pakistan–Malaysia Friendship Association (PMFA) as Chief Guest at a local hotel. The Speaker was warmly received and welcomed by H.E. Mohd Yunus Ibrahim, Consul General of Malaysia in Karachi, and Mr Shahid Jawed Qureshi, President of PMFA, a communique said on Tuesday.

The ceremony was attended by diplomatic representatives from Malaysia, Oman, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Qatar, along with business leaders, members of civil society and other distinguished guests. Addressing the gathering, Speaker Syed Awais Qadir Shah said that Pakistan and Malaysia enjoy longstanding relations founded on mutual respect, shared values and cultural harmony. He emphasised the importance of strengthening parliamentary diplomacy, trade relations and people-to-people exchanges to further consolidate the friendship between the two countries.

Referring to the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) Regional Conference hosted by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh earlier this year, which was attended by Malaysian parliamentary representatives, the Speaker said such engagements provide valuable opportunities for exchanging experiences between parliamentary institutions and promoting democratic values.

He said Sindh, with Karachi as its commercial centre, offers significant opportunities for Malaysian investors in trade, agriculture, infrastructure, technology, education and tourism. He stressed the need to translate the longstanding friendly relations between the two countries into meaningful economic cooperation and tangible initiatives for the benefit of their people.

The Speaker appreciated the Pakistan–Malaysia Friendship Association for its contributions towards promoting bilateral trade and cultural relations. He also acknowledged the Pakistan–ASEAN Economic Dialogue, held in May 2026 in collaboration with the Consulate General of Malaysia in Karachi, as an important step towards strengthening regional economic engagement.

On the occasion, Shah congratulated the award recipients and appreciated their contributions towards strengthening Pakistan–Malaysia relations.

He also presented traditional Sindhi Ajrak and Sindhi Topi as gifts to the Consul General of Malaysia and other distinguished guests, reflecting the cultural traditions and hospitality of Sindh.

headline: Two children injured after falling into open manhole in Hashim Nagar
description: MIRPURKHAS - Two minor children were injured after falling into an uncovered sewer manhole in Hashim Nagar on Tuesday, while their uncle also sustained
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
MIRPURKHAS - Two minor children were injured after falling into an uncovered sewer manhole in Hashim Nagar on Tuesday, while their uncle also sustained injuries in an attempt to rescue them.

According to Civil Hospital Mirpurkhas emergency ward staff, 10-year-old Junaid and another child accidentally fell into the open manhole and were injured. Their uncle rushed to save them but also fell into the sewer water, sustaining injuries. All three injured persons were shifted to Civil Hospital Mirpurkhas for medical treatment. Junaid’s condition subsequently deteriorated, prompting doctors to admit him for further treatment, while the other two injured persons were also provided medical assistance. One killed, four injured in two road accidents in Mirpurkhas.

headline: Suspect arrested in injured condition
description: HYDERABAD - A suspected criminal was arrested in an injured condition along with a pistol and a snatched 125cc motorcycle following an alleged police
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
HYDERABAD - A suspected criminal was arrested in an injured condition along with a pistol and a snatched 125cc motorcycle following an alleged police encounter in Hyderabad, while his two accomplices managed to escape. According to the district police spokesperson, B-Section police received a tip-off late at night that three members of a snatching gang were present in the area with the intention of committing a crime. Acting on the information, police conducted a raid to arrest the suspects. During the operation, an exchange of fire took place between police and the suspects, resulting in the arrest of one suspect in an injured condition along with a pistol and a 125cc motorcycle. His two accomplices fled the scene.

During preliminary interrogation, the arrested suspect was identified as Faizan Khaskheli. He reportedly confessed to being involved in several snatching incidents along with his absconding accomplices. He also admitted that the recovered 125cc motorcycle had been snatched from the jurisdiction of Husri police station, where a case had already been registered.

The spokesperson informed that police took the recovered motorcycle and pistol into custody and registered cases after completing the necessary legal formalities, while raids were also underway to arrest the two absconding suspects.

headline: DC Sanghar reviews arrangements for providing wheat subsidies to farmers
description: SANGHAR - Deputy Commissioner Sanghar, Dr. Imran-ul-Hassan Khowaja chaired a meeting to review arrangements for providing wheat-related subsidies to
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
SANGHAR - Deputy Commissioner Sanghar, Dr. Imran-ul-Hassan Khowaja chaired a meeting to review arrangements for providing wheat-related subsidies to farmers owning agricultural land ranging from one to 25 acres under the Sindh government’s announced initiative. The meeting was attended by Additional Director Agriculture, Manthar Ali Panhwar, all Assistant Commissioners, Mukhtiarkars and other relevant officials.

The participants discussed the mechanism for providing subsidies on wheat, seeds and agricultural fertilisers, identification of eligible farmers, verification of land ownership and measures to ensure transparency in the distribution process in accordance with the government’s policy.

Speaking on the occasion, Deputy Commissioner Dr. Imran-ul-Hassan Khowaja directed the concerned officials to ensure complete transparency throughout the subsidy process and perform their responsibilities through effective coordination and cooperation among all relevant departments.

He instructed the officials to thoroughly verify the credentials of eligible farmers and issue verification certificates only after completing the required scrutiny. The Deputy Commissioner further directed all concerned departments to take necessary measures to ensure that the benefits of the government’s subsidy initiative reach deserving farmers in a fair and transparent manner. He made it clear that any negligence or laxity in the implementation of the programme would not be tolerated.

headline: Mayor Wahab lays foundation stone for development projects worth Rs731m
description: KARACHI - Mayor Karachi Barrister Murtaza Wahab has laid the foundation stone for development projects worth Rs731 million being undertaken by the North
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
KARACHI - Mayor Karachi Barrister Murtaza Wahab has laid the foundation stone for development projects worth Rs731 million being undertaken by the North Karachi Association of Trade and Industry (NKATI) in North Karachi.

Members of the City Council, President of the North Karachi Association of Trade and Industry Faisal Moiz Khan, other office-bearers and representatives of the industrial community were also present on the occasion.

Addressing the ceremony, Mayor Murtaza Wahab said that improving basic infrastructure in industrial areas was essential for Karachi’s economic growth and the promotion of industrial activities. He said it was necessary to ensure that both the city and its industries continued to function smoothly, as the growth of industries would benefit ordinary citizens, generate tax revenue for Pakistan, support the government’s operations and enable the industrial sector to play its role in earning foreign exchange for the country.

He said that the North Karachi Industrial Area played an important role in the city’s economic activities and that improvements in roads, drainage systems and other basic facilities would provide much-needed relief to industrialists and the business community. Better infrastructure in industrial areas would create a favourable business environment, encourage investment and generate new employment opportunities.

He said that the government had stood with industrialists in the past, stood with them today and would continue to extend its cooperation in the future. “If you take one step forward, we will take two. If two steps are not possible, we will take one step, and if even one step is not possible, we will take half a step. What matters is that we must take practical measures to move forward,” he said.

Mayor Karachi Barrister Murtaza Wahab said Sindh had considerable potential for generating electricity through wind power, with an extensive wind corridor offering opportunities for electricity generation extending beyond Gwadar. Despite this potential, expensive power plants had been established. He said that a way forward had been provided regarding wind power and that the need of the hour was to utilise available resources to provide affordable energy to industries. The Mayor said that practical solutions to the problems faced by investors could only be found by sitting together with the business community. Joint efforts were also needed to reduce the cost of doing business.

He said that Karachi’s water requirements should not be addressed solely through reliance on dams, as the possibility of bringing canal water to the city could also be explored.

Addressing representatives of the industrial sector, Mayor Wahab said that work would also be undertaken on international compliance and chemical analysis projects, with a focus on promoting recycling. He said he wanted to initiate work in the industrial area during the first phase, while industrialists should identify a suitable location for the second phase.

The government was ready to extend its cooperation, and any project that benefited the public would receive full support. He said that practical, locally developed solutions also needed to be explored for biogas projects. Further progress could be made through collaboration with the industrial sector in areas where similar initiatives were already underway. Mayor Wahab said he also intended to recommend grants for sewage treatment and biogas projects.

He directed all relevant consultants and contractors to ensure the earliest possible completion of development works. He said approximately Rs 732 million would be spent on the project and that the amount would subsequently be sought from the government. He stressed that the construction of roads and drains should be completed at the earliest to provide relief to the public.

He said that in the past, complaints had frequently been raised regarding road construction and rehabilitation, but approximately 7,000 roads had now undergone pavement works in the city.

He said that it was also necessary to consider whether the city wanted to return to the governance system of the past and to examine the reasons behind the shortcomings that had emerged under previous arrangements. He said the government’s efforts were focused on providing improved infrastructure and modern municipal facilities across Karachi, particularly in industrial zones.

The Mayor said that the cooperation of industrialists and the business community was vital to Karachi’s development and that all stakeholders needed to work together to resolve the city’s problems.

He said the primary objective was to provide relief to citizens and expressed hope that the coming period would bring progress and prosperity for both Karachi and Pakistan.

Members of the City Council, President of the North Karachi Association of Trade and Industry Faisal Moiz Khan, other office-bearers and representatives of the industrial community were also present on the occasion.

Addressing the ceremony, Mayor Murtaza Wahab said that improving basic infrastructure in industrial areas was essential for Karachi’s economic growth and the promotion of industrial activities. He said it was necessary to ensure that both the city and its industries continued to function smoothly, as the growth of industries would benefit ordinary citizens, generate tax revenue for Pakistan, support the government’s operations and enable the industrial sector to play its role in earning foreign exchange for the country.

He said that the North Karachi Industrial Area played an important role in the city’s economic activities and that improvements in roads, drainage systems and other basic facilities would provide much-needed relief to industrialists and the business community. Better infrastructure in industrial areas would create a favourable business environment, encourage investment and generate new employment opportunities.

He said that the government had stood with industrialists in the past, stood with them today and would continue to extend its cooperation in the future. “If you take one step forward, we will take two. If two steps are not possible, we will take one step, and if even one step is not possible, we will take half a step. What matters is that we must take practical measures to move forward,” he said.

Mayor Karachi Barrister Murtaza Wahab said Sindh had considerable potential for generating electricity through wind power, with an extensive wind corridor offering opportunities for electricity generation extending beyond Gwadar. Despite this potential, expensive power plants had been established. He said that a way forward had been provided regarding wind power and that the need of the hour was to utilise available resources to provide affordable energy to industries. The Mayor said that practical solutions to the problems faced by investors could only be found by sitting together with the business community. Joint efforts were also needed to reduce the cost of doing business.
He said that Karachi’s water requirements should not be addressed solely through reliance on dams, as the possibility of bringing canal water to the city could also be explored.

Addressing representatives of the industrial sector, Mayor Wahab said that work would also be undertaken on international compliance and chemical analysis projects, with a focus on promoting recycling. He said he wanted to initiate work in the industrial area during the first phase, while industrialists should identify a suitable location for the second phase.

The government was ready to extend its cooperation, and any project that benefited the public would receive full support. He said that practical, locally developed solutions also needed to be explored for biogas projects. Further progress could be made through collaboration with the industrial sector in areas where similar initiatives were already underway. Mayor Wahab said he also intended to recommend grants for sewage treatment and biogas projects.

He directed all relevant consultants and contractors to ensure the earliest possible completion of development works. He said approximately Rs 732 million would be spent on the project and that the amount would subsequently be sought from the government. He stressed that the construction of roads and drains should be completed at the earliest to provide relief to the public.
He said that in the past, complaints had frequently been raised regarding road construction and rehabilitation, but approximately 7,000 roads had now undergone pavement works in the city.

He said that it was also necessary to consider whether the city wanted to return to the governance system of the past and to examine the reasons behind the shortcomings that had emerged under previous arrangements. He said the government’s efforts were focused on providing improved infrastructure and modern municipal facilities across Karachi, particularly in industrial zones.
The Mayor said that the cooperation of industrialists and the business community was vital to Karachi’s development and that all stakeholders needed to work together to resolve the city’s problems.
He said the primary objective was to provide relief to citizens and expressed hope that the coming period would bring progress and prosperity for both Karachi and Pakistan.

headline: Pakistan to host 30th ECO Foreign Ministers’ meeting without Afghanistan
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has decided not to invite the Afghan Taliban government to the upcoming 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan has decided not to invite the Afghan Taliban government to the upcoming 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) Council of Ministers in Islamabad, amid strained relations between the two neighbouring countries, diplomatic sources said.

The two-day ministerial conference will be held on November 15–16, bringing together foreign ministers and senior representatives of ECO member states to discuss regional trade, economic integration, transport connectivity and avenues for strengthening economic cooperation across the region. ECO Secretary General Ambassador Dr Asad Majeed Khan has confirmed that Pakistan will host the conference, with preparations underway for the important regional diplomatic gathering.

Pakistan is chairing the ECO Council of Ministers for the 2026–27 term under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO.” Diplomatic sources confirmed that the Afghan Taliban government has not been extended an invitation to participate in the meeting. Afghanistan, however, remains a formal member of the ten-nation regional organisation. The ECO comprises Pakistan, Iran, Türkiye, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

The organisation brings together countries spanning South Asia, Central Asia, the Middle East and the Caucasus, representing a strategically important regional economic bloc.

The Islamabad meeting is expected to focus on strengthening intra-regional trade, improving cross-border transportation networks, facilitating the movement of goods and people, expanding transit trade and developing connectivity corridors linking Central Asian countries with regional markets and seaports.

Pakistan is expected to use its chairmanship to advance regional economic integration and promote its geographical position as a trade and transit corridor connecting landlocked Central Asian republics with the Arabian Sea.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is among the significant participants expected in Islamabad. His presence is particularly important in view of regional developments and Pakistan’s diplomatic engagement with Tehran.

The 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting is expected to provide an opportunity for member countries to translate their shared commitment to regional cooperation into practical initiatives, particularly in trade facilitation, transport infrastructure, energy cooperation and economic connectivity. Pakistan’s decision not to invite the Afghan Taliban government adds a significant diplomatic dimension to the gathering, as Afghanistan is non cooperative to Pakistan in addressing Pakistan security concerns.

headline: Dar, former US diplomat Robin Raphel discuss strengthening Pak-US ties
description: ISLAMABAD - Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar yesterday held a meeting with former US Assistant Secretary of State for South Asian Affairs
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar yesterday held a meeting with former US Assistant Secretary of State for South Asian Affairs Ambassador Robin Raphel, discussing matters of mutual interest and ways to further strengthen Pakistan-US relations. During the meeting, Dar appreciated the positive trajectory of bilateral relations between Pakistan and the United States and underscored the importance of sustained engagement to expand cooperation across various fields, the Foreign Office said.

Both sides also agreed to promote closer exchanges between think tanks and academic institutions in Pakistan and the United States to deepen mutual understanding and encourage meaningful dialogue on regional and international developments. The meeting highlighted the importance of continued interaction and intellectual engagement in advancing bilateral ties and promoting greater understanding of issues of shared interest.

headline: Dar calls for diplomacy amid global turmoil
description: ISLAMABAD - Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday called for a stronger role for diplomacy, dialogue and multilateral cooperation in
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday called for a stronger role for diplomacy, dialogue and multilateral cooperation in addressing growing global tensions, saying Pakistan will safeguard its sovereignty and national interests while continuing to work for regional peace and economic prosperity.

Addressing the Margalla Dialogue 2026 on the theme “Global Order in Transition: Navigating Strategic Uncertainty”, Ishaq Dar said the changing international landscape was marked by intensifying great-power rivalries, prolonged conflicts, weakening arms control arrangements and growing links between geopolitics and economic competition.

He warned that instability in regions such as the Gulf and the Red Sea could disrupt global trade, energy supplies and economies, while rapid advances in artificial intelligence, cyber capabilities and other emerging technologies were creating new security challenges. Citing Palestine and the situation in Gaza as examples of the consequences of impunity, the deputy prime minister said Pakistan remained committed to the principles of the UN Charter and the need to keep diplomatic channels open. He added that Pakistan’s regional diplomacy followed the same conviction.

The DPM/FM highlighted Pakistan’s diplomatic initiatives at the United Nations, particularly its 2025–26 membership of the Security Council. As regards the Middle East, Ishaq Dar said Pakistan’s facilitation of the Islamabad Talks between the United States and Iran in April had reflected its commitment to resolving conflicts through dialogue. He described the subsequent Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding as an important foundation for further negotiations. He also acknowledged close coordination with China, particularly the joint Five-Point Initiative for Restoring Peace and Stability in Gulf and Middle East Region issued on March 31, 2026, in Beijing.

The deputy prime minister said Pakistan was maintaining diplomatic engagement with regional partners, including Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Egypt through the R-4 framework, as well as European partners, to sustain negotiations and prevent further escalation. On South Asia, Ishaq Dar warned that unresolved disputes, military asymmetries and unilateral actions continued to threaten regional stability. He said Pakistan’s response to India’s aggression in May 2025 through Operation Bunyan-un-Marsoos demonstrated its determination and capability to defend national sovereignty, while paying tribute to the armed forces for their professionalism.

He reiterated that Pakistan sought peace but would firmly defend its sovereignty, stressing that a just settlement of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions was essential for lasting peace in the region. He also warned against attempts to weaponise water, reaffirming Pakistan’s commitment to safeguarding its rights under the Indus Waters Treaty. On Afghanistan, the DPM/FM described terrorism emanating from Afghan territory as a serious security challenge, saying Pakistan would continue protecting its people while supporting a peaceful, stable and economically integrated Afghanistan. He stressed that Afghan territory must not be used for terrorist activities against other countries, particularly Pakistan.

Discussing Pakistan’s international partnerships, he described relations with China as a cornerstone of the country’s foreign policy, while highlighting constructive engagement with the United States and expanding cooperation with Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Iran, Gulf countries, Europe and Central Asia. He also referred to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, describing it as a defensive arrangement aimed at strengthening collective security and credible deterrence, rather than targeting any particular country.

Emphasising the importance of domestic economic resilience, Ishaq Dar said Pakistan’s ability to navigate international uncertainty depended on strengthening its economy, institutions and technological capabilities. He said economic diplomacy remained central to his work, with efforts focused on expanding export markets, attracting productive investment and promoting technology cooperation to create employment and improve livelihoods.

He further called for a fairer international economic system that addressed the development needs of the Global South, particularly through equitable access to finance, climate adaptation support and emerging technologies.

headline: LHC expresses resentment over delay in academic calendar formulation
description: RAWALPINDI - Lahore High Court (LHC) Rawalpindi bench here on Tuesday expressed displeasure over the delay in formulating a unified academic
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
RAWALPINDI - Lahore High Court (LHC) Rawalpindi bench here on Tuesday expressed displeasure over the delay in formulating a unified academic calendar for educational institutions in Punjab and directed the provincial government to submit a final report within a week. Justice Malik Javaid Iqbal Wains conducted the hearing on a petition filed by student Daniyal Hussain, represented by Hafiz Waqar Ahmed Advocate, while state counsel appeared on behalf of the Punjab government. The petition was filed in August 2025. Briefing the court during the proceedings, Abrar Ahmed Khan, president of the All Pakistan Private Schools Management Association (APPSMA) North Punjab and a member of the Academic Calendar Committee, stated that despite clear judicial orders, the committee chaired by the secretary Schools Education Punjab had met five times without finalizing the academic calendar. The representative of the private schools highlighted the prevailing uncertainty facing private educational institutions, students, and parents.

He noted that with winter vacations approaching in December, schools are struggling to finalize teaching plans, examination schedules, and general academic activities due to the absence of a clear framework. During the hearing, the state counsel requested a two-week extension to submit the progress report on the academic calendar. However, considering the urgency of the matter, the court voiced concern over the slow progress and delay, rejecting the two week request and directing the Punjab government to present the final report next week. Emphasizing the need for continuity in the education sector, Khan stressed that a standardized policy ensuring an adequate number of instructional days across both public and private schools is essential. He expressed hope that in light of the court’s strict directives, the provincial government would finalize the calendar without further delay to restore certainty to the province’s education system.

headline: Mysterious illness claims five children’s lives in Khyber
description: KHYBER - Five children died while two others fell unconscious after being affected by a mysterious illness in Qaziano Kalay, within the
author: Ahmad Nabi
article_text:
KHYBER - Five children died while two others fell unconscious after being affected by a mysterious illness in Qaziano Kalay, within the jurisdiction of Bazaar Zakha Khel Police Station in Khyber district, police said.

According to police, seven children belonging to the family of a local tribesman, Shah Jee, were affected by the mysterious illness. Health Department officials and local sources said the affected children experienced seizures before their condition deteriorated. Five of them, including three girls and two boys, all reportedly under the age of five and belonging to the same family, died while being taken to hospital, police said. The two unconscious children were shifted to Hayatabad Medical Complex (HMC), Peshawar, where they are receiving treatment. Hospital sources said their condition was out of danger. Doctors said the initial medical reports were normal, while the remaining test results were expected by Tuesday night. The deceased children were identified as Manawal, Maria, Salman and Hafizullah, while the two children admitted to hospital were identified as Sanan and Salman. Doctors said the medical team would be able to determine the nature of the illness and its possible cause after receiving the remaining test results.

Meanwhile, local sources said on Tuesday that two more children had reportedly fallen seriously ill due to a mysterious disease in the Khwar area of Bazaar Zakha Khel. They were shifted to Bazaar Zakha Khel Hospital for medical treatment. The emergence of additional cases has heightened concerns among local residents, who have urged the relevant authorities to take immediate preventive and medical measures to avoid further loss of life.

headline: Most Britons see Israel as a 'serious threat' to world peace: Survey
description: Some 78% of Britons now regard Israel as a serious threat to world peace, up from 48% in 2005, according to a survey published in the National Centre for
author: Anadolu
article_text:
Some 78% of Britons now regard Israel as a serious threat to world peace, up from 48% in 2005, according to a survey published in the National Centre for Social Research's (NatCen) British Social Attitudes report.

The figure exceeds the shares of respondents who view Iran (75%) and the US (74%) as serious threats, according to the report, titled “A More Dangerous World: British Attitudes to Security, Defense and International Alliances,” which was published last week.

“Israel’s reputation, too, has seemingly suffered from its involvement in recent Middle East conflict,” the report said.

It said the proportion of Britons viewing Israel as a serious threat reached 73% by autumn 2024, after Gaza had suffered “heavy damage” in the wake of Israel’s war on the enclave following an attack by the Palestinian group Hamas on Oct. 7, 2023.

The figure fell to around two-thirds in 2025 before rising to 78% in a spring 2026 survey taken after the US-Israeli bombing campaign against Iran.

Green Party supporters were the most likely to view Israel as a serious threat at 88%, followed by Labour supporters at 84%, Liberal Democrats at 79%, Conservatives at 70% and Reform UK supporters at 62%.

headline: Exports, SME financing key to sustainable economic growth: Bilal Kayani
description: Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani on Tuesday stressed the need to expand exports, improve access to finance for small and medium enterprises
author: APP
article_text:
Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani on Tuesday stressed the need to expand exports, improve access to finance for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), enhance productivity and address structural bottlenecks to achieve sustainable economic growth.

Addressing a special forum on “Economic Security: Pakistan’s Economic Bottlenecks – Diagnosis and Prescription”, he said exports remained the only sustainable source of foreign exchange earnings, emphasising the need to diversify export products, explore new markets and strengthen existing export sectors.

Referring to the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS), he described it as an effective mechanism for supporting exporters through duty-free imports of inputs used in export-oriented goods. However, he pointed out that its outreach remained limited, with fewer than 1,000 of an estimated 10,000 SMEs benefiting from the facility.

He said the government was working to simplify procedures and remove regulatory hurdles to enable more businesses to benefit from existing export support mechanisms.

Sharing findings from consultations with around 50 SME exporters held on the Prime Minister's direction, Kayani said most participants had identified access to finance, rather than energy costs, as their major concern.

He noted that even established exporters, some operating for years, continued to face difficulties in securing financing available under existing schemes.

He said the Prime Minister had prioritised improving access to finance and was engaging banks to assess their performance in extending credit to SMEs, small farmers and low-cost housing projects.

Emphasising private-sector participation in policymaking, the minister said economic policies should not be formulated in isolation and that business representatives facing regulatory and operational challenges should be involved in the decision-making process.

He said recommendations from private-sector-led working groups had contributed to several tax measures announced in the recent budget, including the elimination of super tax for businesses earning between Rs150 million and Rs500 million, a two per cent reduction for businesses earning above Rs500 million and the removal of super tax on exporters.

He added that tax relief had also been extended to salaried individuals.

Regarding reforms in the Export Development Fund, Kayani said the government had accepted recommendations to place its management under private-sector leadership and abolish the export development surcharge.

He said the fund's board was now led by exporters, with 89 exporters represented on it.

The minister also called for stronger coordination between federal and provincial governments to improve the utilisation of development funds, noting that combined development spending by both levels of government exceeded Rs4 trillion.

Highlighting the connection between education and economic productivity, he stressed the need to improve the education system to develop a skilled workforce and achieve long-term economic gains.

He also underscored the importance of empowering local governments by bringing decision-making and resources closer to citizens to address local issues effectively.

Kayani said better governance required strengthening the capacity and quality of public officials, ensuring respectful and informed engagement with citizens and reducing discretionary powers in the implementation of government policies and schemes.

headline: Pakistan-Sri Lanka second Test shifted from Lahore to Rawalpindi
description: The second Test match between Pakistan and Sri Lanka, originally scheduled to be played in Lahore from November 17 to 21, has been shifted to Rawalpindi due to
author: NNI
article_text:
The second Test match between Pakistan and Sri Lanka, originally scheduled to be played in Lahore from November 17 to 21, has been shifted to Rawalpindi due to rising smog levels in the provincial capital.

A spokesperson for the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) confirmed that the decision was taken in view of prevailing weather conditions and increasing smog in Lahore.

The match will now be played at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium from November 17 to 21.

headline: US House blocks effort to impeach Hegseth
description: The US House of Representatives voted 211-204 on Tuesday to send a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively killing the
author: Anadolu
article_text:
The US House of Representatives voted 211-204 on Tuesday to send a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively killing the effort.

Republicans backed the motion 210-1 and were joined by the chamber’s lone independent, while all 203 Democrats who voted opposed it. Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, who authored the resolution, was the only Republican to vote against it.

Massie’s resolution, introduced Monday, contained eight articles of impeachment. They accuse Hegseth of waging war with Iran without congressional authorization, carrying out “extrajudicial killings” in airstrikes against alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean Sea, illegally seizing then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, targeting Democratic Senator Mark Kelly and carrying out an unlawful war in Yemen.

President Donald Trump welcomed the result on social media.

“The Democrats’ attempt to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has miserably FAILED! Every single Republican, except Thomas Massie, a major LOSER, voted in favor of Pete,” he wrote.

“Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military … and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot,” he added.

Hegseth dismissed the effort at a Pentagon news conference earlier Tuesday.

“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt and everybody knows it,” he said. “These are not high crimes. This is the job, and it’s the job well done.”

The vote came a week after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Vice President JD Vance tied that defeat directly to the Iran war.

“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” Vance wrote on the US social media platform X on Nov. 4.

Trump has said the war was “a part of” the losses but defended his decision to attack Iran.

“I did the right thing. I would have done it again,” he told The Wall Street Journal.

The US House of Representatives voted 211-204 on Tuesday to send a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively killing the effort.

Republicans backed the motion 210-1 and were joined by the chamber’s lone independent, while all 203 Democrats who voted opposed it. Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, who authored the resolution, was the only Republican to vote against it.

Massie’s resolution, introduced Monday, contained eight articles of impeachment. They accuse Hegseth of waging war with Iran without congressional authorization, carrying out “extrajudicial killings” in airstrikes against alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean Sea, illegally seizing then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, targeting Democratic Senator Mark Kelly and carrying out an unlawful war in Yemen.

President Donald Trump welcomed the result on social media.

“The Democrats’ attempt to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has miserably FAILED! Every single Republican, except Thomas Massie, a major LOSER, voted in favor of Pete,” he wrote.

“Victories in Venezuela and Iran, the Best Recruitment Numbers in the History of the Military … and Spirit like rarely seen before, led to the EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot,” he added.

Hegseth dismissed the effort at a Pentagon news conference earlier Tuesday.

“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt and everybody knows it,” he said. “These are not high crimes. This is the job, and it’s the job well done.”

The vote came a week after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Vice President JD Vance tied that defeat directly to the Iran war.

“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” Vance wrote on the US social media platform X on Nov. 4.

Trump has said the war was “a part of” the losses but defended his decision to attack Iran.

“I did the right thing. I would have done it again,” he told The Wall Street Journal.

headline: US, China to cooperate on managing AI risks: Bessent
description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday that the United States and China will cooperate on managing risks from artificial intelligence but cautioned
author: Anadolu
article_text:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday that the United States and China will cooperate on managing risks from artificial intelligence but cautioned against illusions about the differences between the two countries.

Speaking at the National Committee on US-China Relations 60th Anniversary Gala Dinner in New York City, Bessent said: “The US trade imbalance with China has long been a source of friction, and unlike a political class that tolerated China’s practices, President (Donald) Trump has taken decisive steps to address them.”

“Let me state firmly and unequivocally tonight, as we work toward a more balanced relationship, our objective is to de-risk, not to decouple,” he said.

“For decades, the American economy has grown too dependent on foreign supply, while China’s has become increasingly reliant on foreign demand. In other words, the United States must produce more of what we consume, while China must consume more of what it produces,” he added.

“Working together, we can strengthen both of our economies without perpetuating the imbalances between them,” Bessent said.

He said the administration’s “renewed emphasis on economic strength does not reflect hostility toward our trading partnerships.”

“After decades of imbalance, we are restoring a spirit of reciprocity for the benefit of both our peoples,” he said.

Bessent said the US and China, at Trump’s direction, have begun a new dialogue on AI “designed to guard against shared risk and prevent misunderstandings between our two systems.”

“We also expect to exchange best practices for evaluating and testing advanced models before their release and for keeping human judgment firmly in command of this technology,” he said.

He said the two countries are establishing a direct channel so that either nation can promptly alert the other to serious incidents involving its AI models.

“We should harbor no illusions about the differences between the United States and China,” Bessent said. “Our interests will not always coincide, and our approach to every challenge likewise will not always converge.”

Leaders to meet next week in China

Bessent said he will join Trump in Shenzhen next week for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping ahead of a fourth meeting between the two leaders in Miami.

“President Trump and President Xi agree that the United States and China should build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity,” he said.

headline: Senate committee inspects state land in Lahore
description: LAHORE - A Sub-Committee of the Senate Standing Committee on Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan, States and Frontier Regions on Tuesday visited various Jammu
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - A Sub-Committee of the Senate Standing Committee on Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan, States and Frontier Regions on Tuesday visited various Jammu and Kashmir State properties in Lahore to review their existing status. The committee took notice of 27 illegal housing societies established on state-owned land, stressing the need to protect state properties and investigate possible fraud in the sale of plots to citizens. Convener of the Senate Standing Committee Senator Nasir Mahmood Butt, accompanied by Sub-Committee members Senator Naseema Ehsan and Senator Nadeem Ahmed Bhutto, visited different properties of the Jammu and Kashmir State and reviewed their existing status. The committee members also inspected state-owned land in Sultanpuri and Rehmanpura. During the visit, the committee was informed that 27 illegal housing societies had been established on Jammu and Kashmir State land, where plots were being sold to citizens, while some people had also constructed houses on the land. The committee was further informed that many citizens were unaware of the actual ownership and legal status of the land, exposing them to possible financial losses and legal complications in the future. Expressing concern, the committee members directed the relevant authorities to conduct a detailed review of land ownership, the legal status of the housing societies, plot transactions and related records to safeguard citizens’ rights and prevent the illegal use of state-owned land. The officials concerned also briefed the committee on the current status of state properties, administrative matters and available records. The members reviewed illegal occupation and encroachments on state land and stressed effective measures for the protection and transparent management of these important state assets. The three-day visit of the Senate Standing Committee on Kashmir Affairs, Gilgit-Baltistan, States and Frontier Regions is underway in Lahore, during which members are visiting different state properties to review their status.

headline: Man arrested for killing wife, daughter
description: LAHORE - The police arrested a man for allegedly shooting dead his wife and nine-year-old daughter besides injuring his father-in-law in Raiwind on Tuesday.
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - The police arrested a man for allegedly shooting dead his wife and nine-year-old daughter besides injuring his father-in-law in Raiwind on Tuesday. Police said, the suspect allegedly opened fire following a domestic dispute, killing his wife, Nazia Bibi, and daughter, Ayesha, before fleeing after critically injuring his father-in-law, Maqbool. According to Superintendent of Police (SP) Investigation Sadar Hassan Farooq Ghuman, a police team led by the Raiwind investigation in-charge arrested the suspect with the help of CCTV footage and human intelligence. Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Investigation Syed Zeeshan Raza had taken notice of the double murder and directed the formation of a team under the supervision of the SP Investigation Sadar to arrest the suspect. The DIG said a strong challan would be prepared to ensure the suspect was brought to justice. He added that those involved in the murder of women and children would not be shown any leniency. He also announced commendation certificates for the police team.

headline: Quality education to be ensured for students: DC
description: LAHORE - Deputy Commissioner Muhammad Ali Ejaz on Tuesday visited Ravi Tehsil to review cleanliness arrangements and educational facilities at a government
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Deputy Commissioner Muhammad Ali Ejaz on Tuesday visited Ravi Tehsil to review cleanliness arrangements and educational facilities at a government school. Accompanied by the CEO LWMC, Chief Officer Metropolitan Corporation Lahore (MCL) and Assistant Commissioner Ravi, the deputy commissioner inspected cleanliness arrangements at Lari Adda, Bund Road Shahdara and Ring Road. LWMC officials briefed him on waste transportation arrangements and the proposed establishment of a new dumping site near the fish market on Ring Road. Later, the deputy commissioner visited Government Secondary School Shahdara Town and inspected various facilities. He interacted with students and sought their feedback about the quality of education and available facilities. He directed the school administration to ensure the immediate provision of clean drinking water and functional washrooms in schools, stressing that students must be provided with a clean and quality educational environment. As part of the ongoing plantation campaign, the deputy commissioner also planted a sapling on the school premises. On the occasion, Muhammad Ali Ejaz said the zero-waste policy would remain in force across the district, adding that all possible measures were being taken to improve cleanliness and provide students with a quality learning environment.

headline: Ahsan Iqbal urges doctors to put humanity before profession
description: LAHORE - Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Professor Ahsan Iqbal on Tuesday urged graduating doctors to uphold professional
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text:
LAHORE - Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Professor Ahsan Iqbal on Tuesday urged graduating doctors to uphold professional ethics, compassion and integrity while embracing modern medical technologies to improve healthcare services in the country. Addressing the 59th Convocation Ceremony of the College of Physicians and Surgeons Pakistan (CPSP) in Lahore, he congratulated the graduating doctors, their parents, families, and teachers, acknowledging their years of dedication, sacrifices, and hard work in achieving the professional milestone. Federal Minister for Planning, Development, and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal stressed that a medical degree is not merely an academic qualification, but a profound and solemn responsibility to serve humanity with honesty, empathy, and unwavering professional commitment. The ceremony was attended by distinguished local and international guests, including CPSP President Professor Muhammad Shoaib Shafi, members of the CPSP Council, President of the Royal College of Physicians of Edinburgh Professor Mark Strachan, and President of the Bangladesh College of Physicians and Surgeons Council Professor Moudud Hossain Alamgir. Emphasizing the sacred nature of the profession, Ahsan Iqbal noted that doctors carry an enormous responsibility because patients approach them in moments of deep vulnerability and distress. A doctor’s fair judgment, compassionate attitude, and professional integrity can make a life-changing difference, he added, stressing that character and empathy are what ultimately earn a patient’s trust. He urged physicians to listen attentively to their patients particularly those enduring financial hardships ensuring that every individual is treated with the utmost dignity and respect. Drawing upon Islamic teachings, the Federal Minister reminded the audience that whoever saves one life, it is as if they have saved all of mankind. He emphasized that this eternal principle underscores the absolute necessity of practicing compassion, honesty, and trustworthiness (Amanah) in public service. He cited the exemplary lives of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Prophet Ibrahim (AS) as enduring guiding lights. Highlighting rapid global shifts, Ahsan Iqbal pointed out that the healthcare sector is undergoing unprecedented transformation driven by breakthroughs in artificial intelligence (AI), genomics, cell and gene therapies, robotic surgery, digital pathology, and telemedicine. He urged young doctors to remain lifelong learners, cultivate curiosity, study new research regularly, and collaborate closely with engineers and computer scientists to stay ahead of evolving practices. Recalling a significant historical account, he shared the story of two Persian doctors who diagnosed Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah R.A with a fatal lung disease in 1946. By keeping the diagnosis strictly confidential to protect his historic mission, they demonstrated a profound commitment to professional ethics and patient confidentiality. Reflecting on national history, Ahsan Iqbal drew parallels between the selfless sacrifices of the 1947 generation who fought to establish Pakistan without seeking personal gain and the vital responsibilities resting on the current generation as the nation approaches its centenary in 2047. Addressing modern challenges such as fake news and growing social polarization, he called on professionals to maintain public trust, foster positive thinking, and focus on areas where they can drive meaningful change.

Finally, he encouraged the new graduates to contribute actively to national development by combining professional excellence with a deep commitment to public service.

headline: Commissioner inspects medical facilities at Lady Willingdon Hospital
description: LAHORE - Commissioner Lahore Division Muhammad Jahanzeb Awan on Tuesday paid a surprise visit to Lady Willingdon Hospital and inspected medical facilities,
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Commissioner Lahore Division Muhammad Jahanzeb Awan on Tuesday paid a surprise visit to Lady Willingdon Hospital and inspected medical facilities, cleanliness and fire safety arrangements. During the visit, he inspected the emergency department, Outpatient Department (OPD), laboratory, blood bank, gynaecology ward, nursery and patients’ attendants’ accommodation. He also interacted with patients in different wards and inquired about the availability of medical facilities and the quality of healthcare services. He also sought feedback from attendants staying at the facility. The commissioner particularly checked the availability and functioning of fire hydrants, access for fire brigade vehicles, emergency exits and firefighting equipment. He also reviewed safety equipment and staff training for its use. He directed the hospital administration to ensure that dengue counters remained fully functional and that patients were looked after with dedication and care. Speaking on the occasion, Muhammad Jahanzeb Awan said that fire hydrants and firefighting equipment were functional, while arrangements for training staff in the use of safety equipment were also reviewed. He said the provision of comprehensive medical facilities in hospitals was among the top priorities of Chief Minister Punjab Maryam Nawaz Sharif, adding that the district administration would extend full cooperation to all hospitals in Lahore.

article_text: LAHORE - Senior Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS) officer Muhammad Jahanzeb Awan on Tuesday assumed charge as Commissioner Lahore Division. He was previously serving as Secretary Services Punjab and is a Grade-20 officer of the PAS. On his arrival at the Commissioner Office, senior officers welcomed him. He met the officers and received briefings on various administrative matters. Additional Commissioner Coordination Bilal Hassan, Additional Commissioner Revenue Rao Abdul Jabbar, Additional Commissioner Consolidation Arshad Bhatti, Director Development Javed Rasheed Chohan, Assistant Commissioner General Wajiha Samreen, Assistant Commissioner Revenue Aleem Ahmad and other officers were present on the occasion.

headline: Foreign woman rape case accused discharged
description: LAHORE - A local court on Tuesday discharged Ahmed Tanveer, an accused in the rape case involving a foreign woman, and his co-accused, Ehtisham, in a separate
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - A local court on Tuesday discharged Ahmed Tanveer, an accused in the rape case involving a foreign woman, and his co-accused, Ehtisham, in a separate kidnapping and robbery case after the complainant disowned them. The two accused were produced before a judicial magistrate at Model Town Courts after completion of their physical remand. During the proceedings, the complainant appeared before the court and recorded his statement, saying that neither Ahmed Tanveer nor Ehtisham was involved in the incident. He told the court that a misunderstanding had occurred during their identification and expressed no objection to their discharge from the case. In view of the complainant’s statement, the court ordered the discharge of both accused in the case. The Ichhra police had registered the kidnapping and assault case on the complaint of a citizen.

headline: Man sentenced to 15 months in explosives recovery case
description: LAHORE - An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday sentenced a man, Muhammad Nauman, to one year and three months in prison after finding him guilty in a case
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday sentenced a man, Muhammad Nauman, to one year and three months in prison after finding him guilty in a case involving the recovery of explosive material. ATC Judge Malik Abid Hussain announced the verdict after completion of the trial. The accused was produced before the court from jail. The court observed that the prosecution had successfully established the charges against the accused. However, it awarded him a lesser sentence on account of his minor age at the time of the offence. The court also ordered the confiscation of his property in favour of the state. The accused, a resident of Tehsil Garboda, District Tank, was allegedly associated with a banned organisation and involved in terrorist activities, according to the prosecution. The Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) Lahore had registered the case against him in 2025 and subsequently submitted the challan before the court, alleging that explosive material had been recovered from his possession.

headline: Punjab PACs recover over Rs11.88b from govt depts
description: LAHORE - The Public Accounts Committees (PACs) of the Punjab Assembly have recovered more than Rs11.88 billion from government departments over financial
author: Staff Reporter
article_text: LAHORE - The Public Accounts Committees (PACs) of the Punjab Assembly have recovered more than Rs11.88 billion from government departments over financial irregularities, audit objections and irregular use of public funds, according to official documents. A performance report of Public Accounts Committees-I, II and III, covering their activities from their formation until September 2026, shows that the three committees collectively recovered Rs11.887 billion. Public Accounts Committee-II topped the list with recoveries exceeding Rs7.36 billion. The committee is chaired by Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) MPA Ali Haider Gilani. Public Accounts Committee-III stood second, recovering more than Rs2.7 billion. MPA Ahmed Iqbal heads the committee. Public Accounts Committee-I recovered Rs1.821 billion (Rs1 billion and Rs82 crore, 11 lakh and 44 thousand), according to the report. The committee is chaired by MPA Iftikhar Chhachhar. The committees examined the financial affairs of government departments, audit objections, utilisation of public funds and cases involving financial irregularities before securing the recoveries. The recoveries reflect the outcome of the committees’ scrutiny of departmental accounts and efforts to address irregularities identified during audits. PSCA’S VIRTUAL CENTRE PROVIDES ASSISTANCE IN 4,599 CASES Punjab Safe Cities Authority’s (PSCA) Virtual Centre for Minorities has facilitated members of minority communities in 4,599 cases, leading to the registration of 786 first information reports (FIRs). According to a spokesperson, the centre provides assistance to minority citizens facing harassment, violence and other issues, while also facilitating legal guidance and coordination with relevant departments. Citizens from minority communities can directly contact the centre by calling the police emergency helpline 15 and pressing 5. Minority officers deployed at the Safe City Authority help complainants resolve their issues and coordinate with relevant institutions. The spokesperson said a monitoring and follow-up mechanism was in place to ensure police action on complaints. He added that providing equal protection, legal assistance and prompt police response to minority communities was a priority.

headline: ATC extends judicial remand of Hammad Azhar
description: LAHORE - An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday extended the judicial remand of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leader Hammad Azhar by another 14 days in the
author: STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday extended the judicial remand of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leader Hammad Azhar by another 14 days in the Jinnah House attack case. Hammad Azhar was produced before the court from jail upon expiry of his previous judicial remand. The investigation officer requested the court to extend the accused’s judicial remand, stating that a supplementary challan was being prepared and would be submitted shortly. He requested that the accused be sent back to jail. The court accepted the request and extended Hammad Azhar’s judicial remand for 14 days, directing police to produce him again on November 24. According to police, the accused is involved in the attack on Jinnah House. He had remained a proclaimed offender in several cases related to the May 9, 2023 incidents. The Jinnah House attack case was registered at Sarwar Road Police Station under FIR No. 96/23. PTI leaders and workers have been accused of attacking Jinnah House during the May 9 violence. ATC SENDS PTI LEADER TO JAIL ON JUDICIAL REMAND An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday sent former MPA and PTI leader Shabbir Gujjar to jail on 14-day judicial remand in the Jinnah House attack case. ATC Judge Manzer Ali Gill conducted the proceedings. Police produced Shabbir Gujjar before the court upon expiry of his previous physical remand and requested further custody for investigation, stating that his mobile phone and vehicle were yet to be recovered. The court questioned the police over their failure to recover the vehicle despite having obtained physical remand of the accused several times earlier. The defence counsel opposed the request for further physical remand. After hearing arguments, the court dismissed the police plea and ordered that Shabbir Gujjar be sent to jail on judicial remand for 14 days. The court directed police to produce the accused again on November 24. Police had arrested Shabbir Gujjar in connection with the Jinnah House attack case. A case (FIR No. 96/23) was registered at Sarwar Road police station in connection with the attack. PTI leaders are accused in the case of sedition and inciting party workers to engage in arson and vandalism.

Hammad Azhar was produced before the court from jail upon expiry of his previous judicial remand. The investigation officer requested the court to extend the accused’s judicial remand, stating that a supplementary challan was being prepared and would be submitted shortly. He requested that the accused be sent back to jail. The court accepted the request and extended Hammad Azhar’s judicial remand for 14 days, directing police to produce him again on November 24. According to police, the accused is involved in the attack on Jinnah House. He had remained a proclaimed offender in several cases related to the May 9, 2023 incidents. The Jinnah House attack case was registered at Sarwar Road Police Station under FIR No. 96/23. PTI leaders and workers have been accused of attacking Jinnah House during the May 9 violence.
ATC SENDS PTI LEADER TO JAIL ON JUDICIAL REMAND 
An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Tuesday sent former MPA and PTI leader Shabbir Gujjar to jail on 14-day judicial remand in the Jinnah House attack case. ATC Judge Manzer Ali Gill conducted the proceedings. Police produced Shabbir Gujjar before the court upon expiry of his previous physical remand and requested further custody for investigation, stating that his mobile phone and vehicle were yet to be recovered. The court questioned the police over their failure to recover the vehicle despite having obtained physical remand of the accused several times earlier. The defence counsel opposed the request for further physical remand. After hearing arguments, the court dismissed the police plea and ordered that Shabbir Gujjar be sent to jail on judicial remand for 14 days. The court directed police to produce the accused again on November 24. Police had arrested Shabbir Gujjar in connection with the Jinnah House attack case. A case (FIR No. 96/23) was registered at Sarwar Road police station in connection with the attack. PTI leaders are accused in the case of sedition and inciting party workers to engage in arson and vandalism.

headline: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
description: PARIS - One of France’s last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104. Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
PARIS - One of France’s last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104. Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters. After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of Ruillé-sur-Loir. With some 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and, after the Allied landings in Normandy on D-Day in 1944, joined the fight against the occupying German forces. President Emmanuel Macron was among many to pay tribute to Alexandre, after her death was announced at a nursing home in Le Mans. “She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you,” Macron posted on social media. Born in 1922 in the Sarthe department of western France, Solange Alexandre, née Dubuisson, grew up in a patriotic family that had suffered in World War One. “My mother lost her first husband in the war, and my father was wounded in 1917. The words homeland and honour were very important to us. They were in my blood,” she recalled in her memoirs. In June 1940 she heard on the radio the appeal from General Charles de Gaulle in London, calling on the French not to give up the struggle against Germany. She had never heard of him, but that did not matter. “From that moment I knew I had to join up,” she wrote. Some months later she was recruited by a friend of her father’s – a Tunisian-born French army veteran called Saïd Belhaffaf, who had joined the Resistance. Using the code-name Corlay, she criss-crossed the region around Le Mans by bicycle, gathering information and passing on messages. “There were no mobile phones back then, and no private cars either because of the lack of petrol. The bicycle was king,” she said in an interview two years ago. In 1943 she met her first husband Guy Déliot, who had deserted from the French gendarmerie after refusing to arrest some Jews. The following April, with the Allied invasion approaching, they decided to take to the maquis, in other words live clandestinely in the forested hills, supplied with food by local farmers. Their group consisted of deserters from German forced labour programmes, as well as survivors from another Resistance outfit that had been destroyed by the enemy. There were also two airmen, one American and one Canadian. “Twice the Gestapo came for me, and twice I slipped through their hands,” she later recalled.

After taking part in the liberation of Tours in September 1944, she ended the war with the rank of sub-lieutenant in the French Interior Forces (FFI). Later she worked as a teacher and followed her husband on his many postings as an officer of the gendarmerie in French overseas territories. He was killed in 1960 in Martinique, and in 1981 she remarried. Twice Solange Alexandre turned down the Légion d’Honneur, saying that she had only done her duty and that others were more worthy. Finally in 2024 she relented. On receiving the award she said: “It is a great pleasure and a great honour. I am very proud – even if it is only a few weeks, or a few months, before I die.”

headline: Keira Knightley’s unforgettable green ‘Atonement’ dress is going up for sale
description: LONDON - Almost two decades after Keira Knightley bewitched audiences in the 2007 film, “Atonement,” the emerald-green silk dress she wore in a
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
LONDON - Almost two decades after Keira Knightley bewitched audiences in the 2007 film, “Atonement,” the emerald-green silk dress she wore in a pivotal scene is coming up for auction. Thanks to its enduring allure, the backless gown designed by Jacqueline Durran is expected to sell for up to £120,000 ($161,000) when it goes under the hammer at Christie’s in London on December 9. Knightley’s character, Cecilia, wore the dress in a climactic scene in Joe Wright’s adaptation of Ian McEwan’s tragic romance novel. During the scene, Cecilia makes love with the housekeeper’s son Robbie (played by James McAvoy) in the grand home library after weeks of romantic tension, and they confess their feelings for one another. “When we started making the movie, we all knew it was a pivotal moment, and it had to be a memorable dress,” Durran told Entertainment Weekly in an interview published in 2017. “Joe (Wright) said that to me, right at the beginning, which was obviously a lot of pressure on me to try and make this memorable dress,” she continued. “But we didn’t know, really. It was a complete surprise how much it did resonate with people and how much it was picked out as a single look from the movie.” “When the film came out in 2007, I just remember so much about that dress,” Caroline Young, author of the 2022 book “The Color of Fashion: The Story of Clothes in Ten Colors,” told CNN.

“It’s glamorous, it’s nostalgic, and that green is so significant,” she added. “Green has a deep history of representing tempestuous love and illicit affairs,” Young wrote in her book, adding that the “Atonement” gown is “one of the most talked about green dresses in recent years.” “Because that segment of the film was set in the 1930s,” Young told CNN, the dress “has this Jean Harlow-esque quality — the sort of slinkiness of the cut, the thin straps.” “It’s this perfect summer before tragedy strikes,” Young added. Wright had various instructions for Durran for the dress design, including that “it should have movement at the hem and be quite full-skirted,” Durran said. He “wanted it as showstopping as we could make it, and that it should be green,” although he “wasn’t specific” about the shade, and “the mood of the dress should be that it could remind the audience that it is the hottest day of the year.” For this reason, Durran said she tried to make the dress from “very fine fabric, and make it very light and unstructured.” She drew on reference books from the 1920s and ‘30s and “pulled out things that I thought would suit Keira.”

headline: John Cena reveals shocking plans for upcoming festive holidays
description: LOS ANGELES - John Cena already knows what he will be doing for the festive season this year. The retired WWE legend turned actor has revealed he makes sure to
author: News Source
article_text: LOS ANGELES - John Cena already knows what he will be doing for the festive season this year. The retired WWE legend turned actor has revealed he makes sure to box off time to spend with his family from mid-December until a few days into the New Year, and he and his wife Shay Shariatzadeh - who he married in 2020 - will be visiting both sides of their family for the holidays. He told The Takedown on SI, “I make sure around [December] 15th, I am a ghost and I will resurface about January 4th or 5th.” “And in that time, I make sure to spend 10 days in Massachusetts with my family and 10 days in Canada with my wife’s side of the family,” he said, adding, “I’d say the past six years, that’s been my path of action. And boy, it’s really been rewarding and great.” The date is significant, as December 14 will be a special John Cena Classic edition of Monday Night Raw on Netflix, with Club WWE subscribers voting for their male and female champions after a series of exhibition matches. Cena admitted his priorities changed as he stepped back from his full-time career with WWE over the past nine years. He said, “When I was full-time with WWE, the most important thing was literally covering my tracks for being a workaholic.” “So, I was a big gift giver, thinking that I could kind of buy through my workaholism. And now the most important thing for me is to be with those and connect with those I love,” the wrestler-cum-actor stated. Cena has dealt with a lot living his last 23 years in the spotlight, including becoming an internet meme, and having wrestling fans point out his hair loss. However, he’s always been able to cope with whatever’s thrown his way by living his life one way. He told the Metro newspaper’s 60 Seconds column, “What’s helped me is, just be authentic. I got a hair transplant. I could have hidden it but the fans have a way to make you honest.” “You could see the back of my head was as bald as my a**. How am I going to hide the fact that I didn’t have hair and now I have hair? Wrestling in the WWE has taught me so much about being the human being that I am today,” John Cena said at the time of the challenges he faced after fame.

headline: Alhamra Arts Council pays tribute to Allama Iqbal
description: LAHORE - The Lahore Arts Council (Alhamra) commemorated the birth anniversary of great poet and philosopher Allama Dr Muhammad Iqbal with a prestigious
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: LAHORE - The Lahore Arts Council (Alhamra) commemorated the birth anniversary of great poet and philosopher Allama Dr Muhammad Iqbal with a prestigious ceremony, highlighting his literary contributions, philosophical vision and lasting influence on generations. Punjab Secretary Information and Culture Syed Tahir Raza Hamdani, Director General of the Iranian Cultural Centre in Lahore Dr Asghar Masoudi, and renowned Seerat scholar Dr Tariq Sharif attended the ceremony. Alhamra Executive Director Muhammad Nawaz Gondal welcomed the distinguished guests. Speaking at the event, Syed Tahir Raza Hamdani stated that honoring national icons and literary giants is crucial for anchoring the youth in their history, identity, and intellectual roots. He noted that these initiatives are being driven directly by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif. According to Hamdani, the Punjab government remains deeply committed to fostering literature, safeguarding the nation’s cultural heritage, and celebrating its luminaries. He also praised Provincial Minister for Information and Culture Azma Bokhari for her vibrant efforts in revitalizing cultural activities throughout the province. Muhammad Nawaz Gondal highlighted the enduring relevance of Iqbal’s philosophy, with a particular focus on Khudi (self-hood), self-confidence, and unwavering belief in one’s potential. He noted that Iqbal’s teachings continue to inspire the youth, strengthen national consciousness, and empower young people to realize their true capabilities. Paying tribute to the national poet in both Urdu and Persian, Dr Asghar Masoudi underscored the deep literary and cultural bonds between the two languages, while emphasizing the global influence of Iqbal’s philosophical thought. A major highlight of the ceremony was a musical presentation by renowned singer Muhammad Sami, whose soulful rendition of Iqbal’s selected verses drew enthusiastic applause from the audience. In honor of the occasion, the Alhamra Mall Complex was beautifully illuminated and decorated, with portraits of Allama Iqbal displayed prominently throughout the venue. The poet’s statue was also adorned with special lighting, becoming a central attraction for crowds of young people and visitors eager to capture photographs. The ceremony concluded with Syed Tahir Raza Hamdani and Muhammad Nawaz Gondal presenting commemorative souvenirs to Dr Asghar Masoudi. Moving forward, Alhamra reaffirmed its commitment to promoting Iqbal’s visionary message through ongoing literary, musical, and intellectual initiatives to inspire future generations.

headline: Cancer patient approached LHC against police harassment, ‘malicious’ FIR
description: RAWALPINDI - Lahore High Court (LHC) Rawalpindi bench has been moved for quashing of a counter-FIR registered at the Women Police Station, Civil
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
RAWALPINDI - Lahore High Court (LHC) Rawalpindi bench has been moved for quashing of a counter-FIR registered at the Women Police Station, Civil Lines, terming it a fabricated second FIR on a matter already sub-judice before a civil forum.

The petition was filed by Syeda Shaheen Bukhari, a cancer patient, and her brother Syed Naveed Ali Bukhari, residents of Airport Housing Society, through their counsels Malik Jawad Khalid, Khurram Shahzad, and Aashir Hanif. The respondents include women police station SHO and the investigation officer along with private parties involved in a property dispute.

According to the petition, the underlying dispute stems from a commercial tenancy. Naveed Bukhari rented out the ground portion of his residential property to a verified tenant – Arif Jamal. However, tensions escalated when members of an alleged land-grabbing group launched a brutal, murderous assault on Naveed on September 24, 2026, breaking his nasal bone and stealing valuables. Following a medico-legal examination at Benazir Bhutto Hospital, FIR No. 1100/26 was registered against the attackers at Police Station Saddar Baroni on October 7, 2026.

The petitioners maintain that after the former occupants vacated the premises, an interim civil dispute arose over remaining belongings, prompting the petitioners to secure a formal Status Quo (Stay Order) from a civil court.

Despite the active stay order, a second counter-FIR (FIR No. 23/26) was registered against the petitioners at the Women Police Station on October 15, 2026, upon the complaint of an unrelated individual –Nazli.

The petition highlights glaring contradictions in the prosecution’s case, pointing out that initial police applications omitted major allegations later introduced in the FIR, including a dramatic shrinking of claimed missing gold from 12 tolas to just 2 tolas.

Furthermore, the petitioners accused Sub-Inspector Khadija of high-handedness, alleging that police conducted an unauthorized raid under the guise of search warrants, broke house locks, and seized valuables beyond any official recovery memo. Citing multiple relevant Supreme Court judgements, the petitioners argued that registering a second counter-FIR on the same occurrence is illegal, void abinitio, and constitutes double jeopardy.

The petitioners have prayed the LHC to quash FIR No. 23/26, restrain police from harassment or illegal raids in light of existing court stay orders, and direct authorities to recover and restore the petitioners’ seized belongings.
