headline: Bukhari warns against bypassing Parliament on creation of new provinces
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan People’s Party (PPP) Parliamentarians Secretary General Syed Nayyer Hussain Bukhari on Tuesday warned against attempts
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan People’s Party (PPP) Parliamentarians Secretary General Syed Nayyer Hussain Bukhari on Tuesday warned against attempts to advance proposals for the creation of new provinces outside Parliament.

He asserted that the Constitution places the authority to decide such matters exclusively within the parliamentary framework.

Emphasising constitutional supremacy and parliamentary sovereignty, Bukhari said the Constitution clearly prescribed the procedure for amendments, requiring a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament.

He categorically rejected the notion that the Constitution could be amended through a referendum, maintaining that even the holding of a referendum must conform to established constitutional and parliamentary procedures.

He said Parliament was the only constitutional forum empowered to deliberate on and decide the creation of new provinces, regretting that despite the significance of the issue, no formal debate was taking place in the legislature.

Bukhari questioned the rationale behind federal ministers representing Punjab making proposals for new provinces outside Parliament, asking why they were not bringing the matter before the Federal Cabinet for a formal discussion.

He maintained that the PPP had a clear and principled position on the issue, stressing that public opinion must be respected and decisions concerning the creation of new provinces should be taken by elected representatives in Parliament in accordance with the Constitution.

The PPP leader observed that no political party had contested the elections by making the creation of new provinces a fundamental commitment of its manifesto. Therefore, he said, such a consequential national and constitutional question should not be reduced to political statements or discussions outside Parliament.

Raising questions about the motives behind the renewed debate, Bukhari asked whether those initiating the discussion were attempting to find a way out of the existing federal structure.

He stressed that parliamentary supremacy, constitutional safeguards, the rights of federating units and the aspirations of the people must remain central to any decision affecting Pakistan’s administrative and constitutional architecture.

Bukhari also cautioned against conducting a referendum along the lines of the General Zia-ul-Haq era, questioning the precise nature of the proposed exercise and what voters would actually be asked to decide.

He asked whether the referendum would seek public opinion on the creation of new provinces across the country or on further dividing each existing province, arguing that clarity on the scope and implications of such proposals was essential.

Referring to 162 countries where powers were concentrated at the Centre, Bukhari also underscored the importance of examining the distribution of powers and the implications for Pakistan’s federal structure.

He reiterated that any initiative concerning new provinces must be rooted in constitutional legitimacy, parliamentary debate and democratic consensus rather than unilateral political pronouncements.

headline: Samar Bilour opens Women Entrepreneurs Exhibition
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for Information and Public Relations, and Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement, Samar Haroon Bilour, on
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for Information and Public Relations, and Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement, Samar Haroon Bilour, on Tuesday inaugurated the Women Entrepreneurs Exhibition organized by the Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Peshawar.

Following the inauguration, the Adviser visited various stalls set up at the exhibition, where women entrepreneurs showcased their businesses, products and ventures. She inspected the stalls and received briefings from the participants about their products and enterprises.

During her interaction with the entrepreneurs, Samar Bilour appreciated their efforts and acknowledged the important role of women in economic activities and business development. She took a keen interest in the diverse range of products displayed by entrepreneurs from across the province and praised their quality, innovation and creativity.

The Adviser said that such exhibitions provide women entrepreneurs with a valuable platform to showcase their talent, promote their products, and connect with potential customers and business partners.

She expressed hope that such opportunities would help strengthen women’s participation in the economy and encourage more women to pursue entrepreneurship.

headline: NA panel for unified central forum for film certification
description: ISLAMABAD - The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday expressed its concern over the absence of a unified
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information and Broadcasting on Tuesday expressed its concern over the absence of a unified central forum for film certification in the country, observing that the existing arrangement, under which provinces have their own film certification mechanisms, could lead to inconsistencies in certification standards and regulatory practices.

The committee emphasized the need for greater coordination and uniformity among the federal and provincial authorities to ensure a coherent and harmonized framework for film certification across the country. It underscored the importance of examining the matter in consultation with all relevant stakeholders to develop an effective mechanism that promotes consistency while respecting the respective constitutional jurisdictions. Committee Chairman Pullain Baloch, MNA, chaired the meeting held at the Parliament House.

The committee was apprised about the working and performance of the Central Board of Film Censors. It was informed that subsequent to the recent amendments in the Motion Picture Ordinance 1979, the nomenclature of the Board would be changed besides carrying out several changes in the composition of the Board enhancing its working.

The committee also expressed grave concern over the non-payment of salaries to media workers and the growing instances of layoffs by media houses. It observed that delays in payment of salaries and the termination of employees without prior notice and without fulfilling their contractual obligations were serious matters affecting the livelihoods and welfare of media professionals.

The committee asked the Ministry to present a clear strategy to address the issue. The Secretary Ministry informed the committee that the government was regularly releasing payments against dues payable to media outlets, however, it was incomprehensible that the media outlets were not fulfilling their obligations.

He further informed that as per direction of the committee, details of outstanding salaries were sought which had not yet been received from the representative organization of media workers. The committee sought a clear and comprehensive way forward from the Ministry within 15 days to address the issue and ensure the payment of outstanding salaries to media workers. It emphasized the need for effective coordination between the Ministry, media outlets and representative organizations to resolve the matter. The committee directed the Ministry to engage with all relevant stakeholders, obtain the requisite details of pending salaries, and submit a concrete plan of action within the stipulated time frame.

Regarding the incident of assault on the Chairman Press Council of Pakistan, the committee was informed that the incident was presently pending adjudication. It was further informed that the Ministry of Information had already taken cognizance of the matter and ordered an investigation into the allegations/ issues involved. The investigating committee had been asked to submit its report within 60 days. It was suggested that the deliberations on the issue may be postponed till the investigation was completed.

The committee in view of the pending judicial proceedings, as well as the investigation already ordered by the Ministry, decided to defer discussion till conclusion of the judicial and inquiry proceedings. The committee was further of the view that any discussion or deliberation by the Committee at this stage may lead to overlapping proceedings or potentially prejudice the matter under consideration. The meeting was attended by MNAs; Ms Kiran Imran Dar, Ms Kiran Haider, Ms Shaheen, Salahuddin Junejo, Ms Mehtab Akbar Rashdi, Ms Rana Ansar, Secretary, Ministry of Information, Chairperson PEMRA and other officers and other officers of the concerned departments.

headline: One killed, five injured in trailer-Datsun collision on KKH
description: SHANGLA/ KOHISTAN - One person was killed and five others sustained serious injuries in a horrific collision between a trailer and a Datsun
author: Aftab Hussain
article_text:
SHANGLA/ KOHISTAN - One person was killed and five others sustained serious injuries in a horrific collision between a trailer and a Datsun vehicle on the Karakoram Highway (KKH) on Tuesday.

According to local police, the deceased was identified as Ehsan, son of Abdul Ghafoor. After completion of the necessary legal formalities, his body was handed over to his heirs. The five injured persons were initially shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital, Pattan, Lower Kohistan, for first aid. They were later referred to Ayub Medical Complex, Abbottabad, for further treatment and medical examinations.

Police said the accident occurred at Janchal on the Karakoram Highway when a trailer collided with a Datsun vehicle. As a result, Ehsan died on the spot, while five others sustained serious injuries.

Upon receiving information about the accident, a Rescue 1122 medical team rushed to the scene, launched rescue operations and provided first aid to the injured.

The injured were identified as Shah Faisal, son of Surkhind, a member of the Mughal caste and resident of Pass; Sethri Bibi, daughter of Abdul Qayyum; Arif Khan, son of Mushabir Khan; Naseer Khan, son of Mushabir Khan; and Fauzia, wife of Ehsanullah.

All five injured persons were shifted to the District Headquarters Hospital, Pattan, Lower Kohistan, for initial treatment. However, considering their condition, they were later referred to Ayub Medical Complex, Abbottabad, for further treatment and necessary medical tests.

headline: Tayyab calls for recovery of encroached KP Auqaf Dept land
description: Peshawar - Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Adviser for Auqaf, Religious and Minority Affairs, Zakat and Ushr, Maulana Tayyab Qureshi, chaired a meeting on
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Adviser for Auqaf, Religious and Minority Affairs, Zakat and Ushr, Maulana Tayyab Qureshi, chaired a meeting on Auqaf properties in Peshawar on Tuesday.

Secretary Auqaf, Religious and Minority Affairs Muhammad Idrees, Administrator Auqaf Gul Nawaz and other relevant officials attended the meeting.

The participants were given a detailed briefing on the Auqaf Department’s properties, vacant plots, income generated through rents and leases, outstanding dues and encroachments, particularly on Auqaf land located at Kalu Shah, Takht Bhai. They were also briefed on encroachments on Auqaf properties by individuals and government departments, as well as the status of recovery of outstanding dues.

Speaking on the occasion, Adviser Maulana Tayyab Qureshi directed the authorities to formulate viable proposals to make Auqaf land productive and profitable so that revenue generated from these properties could be increased.

He also directed the preparation of a comprehensive strategy for taking strict action against illegal occupants of Auqaf properties. Stressing the need for practical measures to retrieve encroached land, he said that action in this regard should not remain confined to paperwork.

He said that Auqaf properties were a national trust and that every possible step should be taken to ensure their proper management, protection and increased revenue generation.

Regarding the Auqaf land at Kalu Shah, Takht Bhai, Maulana Tayyab Qureshi directed the relevant authorities to complete the auction process at the earliest after fulfilling all legal requirements and ensure that the matter was not delayed further.

He also directed the relevant officers to regularly inspect Auqaf properties and conduct raids wherever necessary, emphasizing that the department’s performance should be reflected through practical measures. He made it clear that negligence would not be tolerated in matters relating to the protection of Auqaf properties, action against the land-grabbing mafia, recovery of outstanding dues and enhancement of departmental revenue.

The Adviser urged the officers to work in coordination to improve the performance of the Auqaf Department and ensure that all matters were addressed within the stipulated time. He emphasized that no official matter should be kept pending unnecessarily and that immediate progress should be ensured on issues of public and departmental interest.

The meeting also discussed various proposals and measures for improving the management of Auqaf properties, increasing revenue, eliminating illegal encroachments, recovering outstanding dues and making vacant land usable and productive.

headline: KP adviser directs to establish three more Ombudsperson Regional Offices
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for Law, Labour and Inter-Provincial Coordination Amir Javed has directed the relevant
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for Law, Labour and Inter-Provincial Coordination Amir Javed has directed the relevant authorities to take immediate steps to provide adequate space and other necessary facilities to the Regional Offices of the Ombudsperson to ensure that women do not face unnecessary hurdles in seeking redressal of complaints related to harassment and property disputes.

He expressed these views during a visit to the Ombudsperson’s office on Tuesday. Ombudsperson Rubab Mehdi briefed him on the day-to-day hearings of cases, the institution’s performance, and the administrative and practical challenges it was facing.

Amir Javed directed the relevant authorities to take immediate steps to provide suitable premises and fulfil the necessary administrative and office requirements for establishing three additional Regional Offices of the Ombudsperson. This would save women from having to travel long distances to seek redressal of their grievances and ensure timely access to justice.

The adviser said that transparency, impartiality and adherence to the law should be the fundamental principles governing the dispensation of justice. He emphasized that the positions of both complainants and respondents should be heard with equal attention and patience to ensure that no party suffers injustice.

headline: Crackdown against sale of LPG at exorbitant rates continues
description: Peshawar - On the instructions of Deputy Commissioner (DC) Peshawar, Afaq Wazir, district administration carried out vigorous operations against
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - On the instructions of Deputy Commissioner (DC) Peshawar, Afaq Wazir, district administration carried out vigorous operations against elements involved in selling LPG at exorbitant rates and overcharging.

During the operations, Express LPG Plant located on Ring Road, AK LPG Plant Meera Kachori, Ali Brothers LPG Plant G T Road Jhagra and Wolf LPG Plant Chamkani were sealed for selling LPG at prices above fixed rates and other violations, while the concerned plant owners were arrested and further action against them has been initiated in accordance with the law.

Furthermore, while taking action against overcharging and other violations across the district, 8 shops in Tehsil Mattani, 9 in Tehsil Shah Alam, 11 in Tehsil Saddar and 12 in Tehsil City were sealed. Thus, a total of 40 shops were sealed, while several shop owners were arrested and legal action against them has been initiated.

Deputy Commissioner Peshawar Afaq Wazir has made it clear that providing LPG and essential commodities to the public at fixed rates is the first priority of the administration, saying indiscriminate operations will continue against those involved in overcharging, illegal profiteering and violation of official rates and no one will be allowed to exploit the public.

headline: Police arrest wounded robber following exchange of fire
description: Rawalpindi - Naseerabad police here on Tuesday registered a case against four armed suspects following an armed encounter in the Habib Colony area
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Rawalpindi - Naseerabad police here on Tuesday registered a case against four armed suspects following an armed encounter in the Habib Colony area late Monday night, resulting in the injury and arrest of one suspected robber while three others escaped, the police said.

According to the First Information Report (FIR) registered under sections 324 (attempt to murder), 353 (armed encounter), 186 (obstructing public servant from discharge of duties), and 34 (crime committed by several persons) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), alongside Section 13-2(a) of the Punjab Arms Amendment Ordinance 2015, a police patrolling team was conducting routine checks near Habib Colony when they signaled four individuals riding two motorcycles to stop.

Instead of complying, the suspects opened direct fire on the police party with intent to kill. The police officers took defensive positions on the ground to save themselves. During the exchange of gunfire, one of the attackers was injured by bullets fired by his own accomplices as they fled the scene back toward Habib Colony.

The policemen apprehended the injured suspect on the spot, identifying him as Saeed, son of Abdul Wahid, a resident of Habib Colony, Chakra, Rawalpindi. Officers recovered an unlicensed 30-bore pistol along with an empty magazine from his possession. The preliminary investigation revealed that the arrested suspect was member of a gang involved in car and bike snatching activities. The three fleeing suspects are yet to be indentified.

The injured suspect was shifted to District Headquarter Hospital Rawalpindi under police guard for medical treatment and formal examination, while a search operation has been launched to trace and arrest his three fleeing accomplices. The police confirmed that further investigation into the incident is currently underway.

headline: RWU holds 4th BASR meeting, reviews PhD, MPhil research synopses
description: RAWALPINDI - The fourth meeting of the Board of Advanced Studies and Research (BASR) at Rawalpindi Women University was held under the patronage of
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
RAWALPINDI - The fourth meeting of the Board of Advanced Studies and Research (BASR) at Rawalpindi Women University was held under the patronage of Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr. Tayyaba Zarif, where research synopses for PhD and MPhil programmes from the departments of Management Sciences and Media and Communication Studies presented PhD and MPhil research synopses for approval and review.

The board examined the significance of the proposed research topics, their scope, methodology and academic value. The board also issued instructions to improve and revise several synopses.

RWU Registrar Dr. Huma presented the agenda. External experts in attendance included Dr. Tahir Nadeem, Dean of the Faculty of Engineering and Technology at HITEC University, and Dr. Idrees, former Dean of the Faculty of Social Sciences at Quaid-i-Azam University, Islamabad. Prof. Dr. Bashir Ahmad, Dean of the Faculty of Management and Social Sciences at Al-Kawthar University, joined the meeting online. Members of the university’s BASR committee also took part.

The experts scrutinised the synopses closely and offered suggestions to raise their academic quality, research relevance, and methodological precision.

Prof. Dr. Tayyaba Zarif questioned the research scholars to assess their understanding of their chosen topics, their preparation and their research capabilities.

She stressed that there would be no compromise on research quality or on established research standards.

The Vice Chancellor directed that, before any synopsis is brought to the board, the Departmental Research Committee (DRC) must thoroughly vet it for quality, comprehensiveness, relevance of the topic and research aspects, so that only sound proposals reach the board.

Heads of the relevant departments and faculty members also attended and took part in detailed discussions on the research topics.

The meeting concluded with a commitment to promoting quality research, strengthening academic capacity, and making institutional measures for research and innovation more effective, says a press release.

headline: 5 stolen motorcycles recovered in police crackdown in Kahuta
description: Rawalpindi - Kahuta Police have arrested the ringleader of a motorcycle theft gang along with his accomplice and recovered five stolen motorcycles
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Rawalpindi - Kahuta Police have arrested the ringleader of a motorcycle theft gang along with his accomplice and recovered five stolen motorcycles from their possession, police said. According to police spokesperson, the police traced and arrested the suspects with the help of technical and human intelligence sources.

The gang leader is a previous record-holder and has also been involved in motorcycle theft and house-breaking incidents.

SP Saddar commended police team and said that the arrested suspects would be challaned before the court with solid evidence.

headline: Senate Health Committee calls for strict enforcement of breastfeeding ordinance
description: ISLAMABAD - The Senate Standing Committee on National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination has called for immediate enforcement of
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Senate Standing Committee on National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination has called for immediate enforcement of the “Protection of Breast-Feeding and Child Nutrition Ordinance, 2002”, expressing serious concern over its apparent non-implementation and inadequate regulatory oversight.

In a formal letter addressed to Federal Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination Syed Mustafa Kamal, the Chairman Committee highlighted shortcomings in the enforcement of statutory restrictions governing the advertisement, promotion, marketing and labelling of infant formula and breast-milk substitutes. The letter followed the Committee’s meeting held on November 3, 2026.

The Committee emphasized that the existing legal framework, including the establishment of the National Infant Feeding Board under Section 3 of the Ordinance, must be made fully operational. It called for strict implementation of restrictions on commercial promotional practices, including advertisements, promotional incentives, free samples and direct marketing of designated products. The Committee also stressed compliance with mandatory labelling and packaging requirements under Section 8, including warnings in Urdu, prescribed product information and safeguards against misleading representations suggesting that infant formula is equivalent or superior to mother’s milk. It underscored that breastfeeding and appropriate infant nutrition are matters of significant public health importance.

Taking cognizance of proceedings before the Supreme Court of Pakistan and the Islamabad High Court concerning misleading descriptions, labelling and advertisements of formula and powdered milk products, the Committee directed the Ministry to ascertain compliance with operative judicial orders and ensure continued enforcement of statutory provisions wherever no judicial restraint exists. The Committee further sought comprehensive details of inspections, investigations, notices, prosecutions and penalties imposed during the preceding three years. It called for clearly defined enforcement responsibilities and effective coordination among DRAP, PEMRA and other relevant regulatory authorities.

, including measures to address digital advertising, indirect promotion and brand extensions. The Committee directed the Ministry to undertake an immediate review of the Ordinance’s implementation, operationalize the National Infant Feeding Board and initiate appropriate corrective and enforcement measures. headline: Court rejects plea to drop terrorism charge in Group Captain’s murder case
description: ISLAMABAD - A special anti-terrorism court on Monday dismissed a petition by the accused seeking removal of terrorism charges in the killing
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - A special anti-terrorism court on Monday dismissed a petition by the accused seeking removal of terrorism charges in the killing of Pakistan Air Force Group Captain Asim Tariq.

Muhammad Saad Abbasi, through his counsel, had moved an application under Section 23 of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997, requesting deletion of Section 7 ATA from FIR No. 217/2026 registered at Police Station Margallah and transfer of the case to a regular court. The defence argued that the essential ingredients of terrorism were missing, claiming the deceased was neither in uniform nor on official duty, that the accused had no links to any proscribed organisation or prior criminal record, and that the incident occurred at a secluded place with no likelihood of spreading terror among the public.

Special Public Prosecutor Raja Naveed Hussain opposed the application, contending that Section 7 of the ATA was fully attracted as the accused had targeted a serving officer of the Pakistan Air Force.

Judge Abual Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain of Special Court-I (Anti-Terrorism) rejected the plea. The court held that the deceased was a serving officer of the armed forces travelling on official duty to Noor Khan Air Base when the incident occurred, and that the accused was carrying an unlicensed pistol. These factors, the judge observed, attracted the provisions of Section 6 of the ATA and brought the case within the definition of terrorism. According to the prosecution, on July 5 Group Captain Tariq spotted a young man harassing a girl near the Old Traffic Office in F-8.

After the officer intervened and identified himself, the accused allegedly threatened him, fled on a motorcycle, returned after a U-turn and opened fire on the officer’s vehicle, killing him on the spot.

The application was dismissed and ordered to be placed on the judicial file.

headline: ATC grants 13-day remand of 2 JUI-F men; party alleges harassment
description: ISLAMABAD - An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Tuesday granted 13-day physical remand each of two Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) men,
author: Haris Shirazi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Tuesday granted 13-day physical remand each of two Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) men, Qari Iftikhar Hussain and Rafaqat alias Basharat, in two cases registered over the party’s gatherings in the federal capital.

Both accused were produced in police custody before ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain. Investigating officers Inspector Nadeem Mughal and Inspector Abrar Hussain sought 30 days’ physical remand of each. The judge noted that heinous offences were alleged and that it was the first request for physical remand, and allowed 13 days. The accused are to be produced again on Nov 23.

The FIRs in the cases surfaced on Tuesday. Iftikhar is nominated in FIR No. 1212, registered on Nov 7 at the Industrial Area police station, which says a crowd of 200 to 250 people was present. Rafaqat is named in FIR No. 789, registered on Nov 8 at the Sangjani police station. Both invoke the Anti-Terrorism Act and the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act, 2024, along with Pakistan Penal Code sections on rioting, obstructing public servants, disobeying orders and criminal intimidation.

Police allege that the accused, along with others, held an unlawful assembly, blocked public roads, violated Section 144, resisted police on duty, damaged a police vehicle and confined citizens in residential blocks. Investigators say they were required for interrogation, recovery and the arrest of other suspects.

JUI-F Senator Kamran Murtaza told The Nation the arrests of party leaders in Islamabad were meant to provoke the party into a confrontation. He said Qari Iftikhar, the party’s deputy chief in Islamabad, was picked up along with two others while on his way to a wedding, and that two of them were released near the G-9 Markaz while Iftikhar was taken away.

Murtaza said, the party’s Islamabad chief, Mufti Awais Aziz, was also taken into custody, and other party figures were being pressured. He said, no FIR was shown when the men were picked up, and police were neither disclosing their whereabouts nor allowing meetings. He said, terrorism charges have been brought against peaceful clerics who had never harmed even an animal.

He said the party’s strategy was to stay peaceful, not to take the law into its own hands, and to fight the cases legally. Party lawyers would oppose the remand, he said.

In a statement, the JUI-F media cell said the party condemned the arrest of Mufti Awais Aziz. Party spokesperson Aslam Ghouri said, the government had resorted to cheap tactics, respect for the constitution and the law should not be taken as weakness, and Mufti Awais Aziz should be released immediately. The party spokesperson said, JUI-F would confront what it called government terrorism against its leaders and workers, and urged workers not to be provoked and to await the leadership’s next directive.
